cards.q: 人体最小的骨头长在哪里？
cards.short: 镫骨不到三毫米长
body: 中耳内的锤骨、砧骨、镫骨合称听小骨，是人体已知最小的骨骼。镫骨成年后长度约三毫米，重量只有几毫克。
三块骨头以关节相连，将鼓膜振动逐级放大，再传入内耳的液体。体积虽小，却能把声压提升约二十倍。
骨骼大小与身高体重基本无关，从出生起听小骨已接近成年尺寸，是人体中最早发育完全的骨头。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　中耳解剖图中的锤骨、砧骨与镫骨。
cards.qe: Where is the smallest bone in the human body?
cards.shorte: Stapes is under 3mm
cards.fige: Plate I. The malleus, incus, and stapes in a middle-ear anatomical diagram.
bodye: The malleus, incus, and stapes in the middle ear are the body's three smallest bones. The stapes is shortest, about three millimeters long and under five milligrams in adults.
Hinged together, the three bones amplify the eardrum's vibrations in stages before passing them to the inner ear's fluid, boosting sound pressure roughly twentyfold despite their size.
Bone size otherwise tracks height and weight, but the ossicles are near adult size at birth, making them the first bones to finish developing.

cards.q: 潜水民族的脾脏为何格外大？
cards.short: 脾脏是潜水的氧气罐
body: 印尼巴瑶族世代潜水采集为生，2018年一项研究发现，其脾脏体积比邻近陆居族群平均大五成左右。
脾脏收缩时会把储存的红细胞压入血液，提升血氧携带能力，这种收缩反应在潜水民族中更强更快。
差异并非后天训练所致，基因分析显示，巴瑶族携带一种影响甲状腺激素的基因变异，脾脏增大是遗传适应。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　人体脾脏在腹腔中的解剖位置图。
cards.src: 《潜水民族的生理与基因适应研究》
cards.qe: Why are sea-diving peoples' spleens so large?
cards.shorte: Spleen as a dive tank
cards.fige: Plate I. Anatomical position of the spleen within the human abdominal cavity.
bodye: Indonesia's Bajau people have dived for generations to gather food. A 2018 study found their spleens run roughly fifty percent larger than neighboring land-based groups.
A contracting spleen forces stored red blood cells into circulation, raising blood oxygen capacity. This contraction reflex is stronger and faster in diving populations.
The difference is not just training. Genetic analysis found the Bajau carry a variant affecting thyroid hormone regulation, meaning the larger spleen is an inherited adaptation.
cards.srce: Physiological and Genetic Adaptations to Diving in Sea Nomads

cards.q: 手指甲和脚趾甲谁长得快？
cards.short: 指甲比脚趾甲长得快
body: 手指甲平均每月生长约三毫米，脚趾甲只有其三分之一左右，速度还因手指、年龄和季节而不同。
手指使用越频繁，局部血液循环和微小机械刺激越多，越能促进甲床细胞分裂，所以惯用手指甲长得更快。
常有人以为剪得越勤长得越快，这颠倒了因果；真正决定速度的是血流与甲床细胞分裂节律，与修剪无关。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　手指与脚趾甲床结构对比解剖图。
cards.qe: Which grows faster, fingernails or toenails?
cards.shorte: Fingernails grow faster
cards.fige: Plate I. Comparative anatomy of finger and toe nail-bed structures.
bodye: Fingernails grow about three millimeters a month on average, roughly three times faster than toenails. Growth speed also shifts with the finger, age, and season.
Growth rate tracks local blood circulation and use. Fingers stay active and sit closer to the heart, so nutrient delivery is richer, which speeds up the dominant hand's nails.
Many assume frequent trimming speeds growth, but that reverses cause and effect. Growth is set by blood flow and nail-bed cell division, not by cutting.
cards.srce: Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology

cards.q: 人的一生心跳次数为什么是个例外？
cards.short: 人类心跳总数远超同类
body: 多数哺乳动物一生心跳总数都接近十亿次，体型越大心率越慢、寿命越长，总数大致守恒；人类却能达到约三十亿次。
心率与体型大致呈负相关，背后是体表面积与代谢速率的物理限制，这一规律由心率与寿命的跨物种比较研究揭示。
人类打破这一规律不是心脏特殊，而是现代医疗和生活条件把寿命拉长，远超野生哺乳动物的自然预期寿命。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　人类心脏解剖结构图。
cards.qe: Why is the human lifetime heartbeat count an outlier?
cards.shorte: Human total beats run high
cards.fige: Plate I. Anatomical structure of the human heart.
bodye: Most mammals total close to a billion heartbeats in a lifetime. Larger animals have slower heart rates and longer lifespans, so the total stays roughly constant. Humans reach about three billion.

Heart rate and body size are roughly inversely related, a physical constraint tied to body surface area and metabolic rate. The pattern emerged from cross-species comparisons of heart rate and lifespan.
Humans do not break the rule through a special heart. Modern medicine and living conditions have stretched our lifespan well past what a wild mammal our size would naturally expect.
cards.srce: Rest Heart Rate and Life Expectancy
cards.srcMetae: Journal of the American College of Cardiology, 1997

plate.imgTitle: Anatomy of the arteries of the human body - descriptive and surgical, with the descriptive

cards.q: 芝加哥河为什么倒着流？
cards.short: 芝加哥河被工程逆转流向
body: 1900年芝加哥通过运河工程，让芝加哥河的水流永久改向，不再流入密歇根湖，而是向西南汇入密西西比河水系。
此前城市污水随河流排入湖中，污染了饮用水取水口；工程师们挖深连接运河，利用水位差把河水引向内陆。
这次改道并非一劳永逸，遇暴雨污水系统超负荷时，芝加哥至今仍会开闸放水，让河水短暂倒流回密歇根湖。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　芝加哥河与运河船闸的实景。
cards.src: 大芝加哥都会水资源回收区
cards.qe: Why does the Chicago River flow backward?
cards.shorte: Chicago River's flow was engineered in reverse
cards.fige: Plate I. The lock where the Chicago River meets its canal.
bodye: In 1900 Chicago completed a canal project that permanently redirected the Chicago River away from Lake Michigan and into the Mississippi River system.
Sewage had been fouling the city's drinking-water intake in the lake; engineers deepened the connecting canal and used the elevation difference to pull the river inland.
The fix was not final: during major storms, when the sewer system is overwhelmed, gates still open today to send river water briefly back toward Lake Michigan.
cards.srce: Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago
cards.query: Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal photograph

plate.imgTitle: Harlem Avenue Bridge over Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal - from southwest (2006).jpg

cards.q: 曼哈顿摩天楼为何两头高中间低？
cards.short: 摩天楼分布随基岩起伏
body: 曼哈顿天际线呈两段式：下城与中城摩天楼密集，两者之间的格林尼治村一带普遍低矮。
摩天楼地基需打入坚硬基岩，那里基岩接近地表；中段基岩下陷更深，早年打桩成本更高，聚集意愿更低。
这一说法长期被当作定论，但近年研究显示，分区法规与地价同样影响了摩天楼分布，基岩并非唯一原因。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　曼哈顿天际线，下城与中城两处摩天楼群清晰可辨。
cards.qe: Why do Manhattan's skyscrapers cluster at two ends, not the middle?
cards.shorte: Skyscraper clusters follow the bedrock
cards.fige: Plate I. Manhattan's skyline, with its two distinct skyscraper clusters visible.
bodye: Manhattan's skyline rises in two clusters, Downtown and Midtown, with a noticeably lower stretch around Greenwich Village in between.
Skyscrapers need footings anchored in solid bedrock, which sits near the surface at both ends; in the middle it dips much deeper, once making deep pilings costlier.
The bedrock story is often treated as the whole explanation, but recent research finds zoning rules and land prices shaped the skyline just as much.

plate.imgTitle: Lower Manhattan from Jersey City November 2014 panorama 2.jpg

cards.q: 巴塞罗那街区为何四角都切成八边形？
cards.short: 街区切角便于转弯
body: 巴塞罗那新城区街区呈方形切角的八边形，由工程师赛尔达于19世纪设计，是欧洲少见的规整网格城市。
切角扩大了十字路口空间，让马车与有轨电车转弯更顺畅，也为建筑增加了采光与通风角度。
这套设计常被当成纯粹的审美选择，实际首要目的是交通与卫生功能，美观只是附带结果。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　巴塞罗那新城区俯瞰，街区四角均被切平。
cards.src: 伊尔德方索·赛尔达《巴塞罗那扩建计划》
cards.qe: Why are the corners of Barcelona's city blocks cut off?
cards.shorte: Chamfered blocks ease traffic turns
cards.fige: Plate I. An aerial view of Barcelona's Eixample, its block corners sliced flat.
bodye: Barcelona's 19th-century Eixample district is laid out in octagonal blocks, squares with their corners cut off, designed by engineer Ildefons Cerdà.
The chamfers opened up intersections, giving horse carts and later trams room to turn and improving sightlines, while letting more light and air reach the buildings.
The shape is often read as a stylistic flourish, but its first purpose was traffic flow and sanitation; the elegant look was a side effect.
cards.srce: Ildefons Cerdà, Eixample Plan of Barcelona

cards.q: 威尼斯的房子为何建在木桩上不腐烂？
cards.short: 木桩泡水数百年不朽
body: 威尼斯建筑地基由数以百万计的木桩打入潟湖淤泥支撑，多为赤杨木，部分木桩已在水下伫立数百年。
淤泥隔绝了氧气，缺氧环境抑制了分解木材的真菌与细菌，木质纤维反而随年代增加逐渐矿化变硬。
木桩并非因泡水而腐坏，真正的隐患是水位下降后露出空气，接触氧气才开始朽坏。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　里亚尔托桥下的木桩地基结构。
cards.srcMeta: 世界遗产保护报告，1987年起
cards.qe: Why don't Venice's wooden pile foundations rot underwater?
cards.shorte: Submerged piles harden instead of rotting
cards.fige: Plate I. The wooden pile foundations beneath the Rialto Bridge.
bodye: Venice's buildings stand on millions of wooden piles, mostly alder, driven into the lagoon's mud; some have stood submerged for centuries.
The mud seals out oxygen, starving the fungi and bacteria that break down wood, so the fibers slowly mineralize and harden instead of decaying.
The piles do not rot from being wet; the real danger comes when falling water levels expose them to air, which is when decay actually begins.

plate.imgTitle: Panorama of Canal Grande and Ponte di Rialto, Venice - September 2017.jpg

cards.q: 波特兰和盐湖城，谁的街区更大？
cards.short: 盐湖城街区超波特兰十倍
body: 波特兰标准街区约61米见方，盐湖城街区约201米见方，面积相差约十一倍，是美国城市规划反差最大的实例之一。
波特兰刻意采用小街区，增加临街转角地价并提升步行友好度；盐湖城依照摩门教徒的「锡安城规划」，为每户预留大地块建房和种菜。
两座城市建城时间相近，却因规划理念不同形成悬殊的街区尺度；盐湖城的大街区如今也带来了步行距离过长的新问题。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　盐湖城街区俯瞰，地块尺度远超常规城市街区。
cards.src: 约瑟夫·斯密《锡安城规划图》
cards.qe: Portland or Salt Lake City: whose blocks are bigger?
cards.shorte: Salt Lake City's blocks dwarf Portland's
cards.fige: Plate I. An aerial view of a Salt Lake City block, far larger than a typical city block.
bodye: A standard Portland block runs about 61 meters per side; a Salt Lake City block runs about 201 meters, roughly eleven times the area, one of the starkest contrasts in American city planning.

Portland deliberately kept blocks small to multiply valuable corner lots and keep streets walkable; Salt Lake City followed the Mormon settlers' Plat of Zion, which reserved large lots for houses and gardens.
The two cities were founded only decades apart, yet ended up with wildly different block scales; Salt Lake City's oversized blocks now make some downtown walks surprisingly long.
cards.srce: Joseph Smith, Plat of the City of Zion
cards.query: Temple Square Salt Lake City aerial photograph

b.query: Temple Square Salt Lake City aerial photograph

cards.q: 生蚝吞下时是否还活着？
cards.short: 入口时多数仍存活
body: 生蚝若保存得当，开壳时仍闭合或轻触即收缩，说明食用那一刻多半仍是活体，这是判断新鲜度的常见标准。
生蚝靠闭壳肌保持壳体闭合，活体受触碰会收缩肌肉，死亡后肌肉松弛、壳体张开，细菌迅速滋生，因此讲究现开现吃。
许多人担心生食会让生蚝痛苦，但生蚝神经系统简单，没有大脑，是否具备痛觉至今没有确凿证据，这也是部分素食者仍吃生蚝的理由。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　开壳生蚝的闭壳肌与壳内结构特写。
cards.qe: Is an oyster still alive when you swallow it?
cards.shorte: Often still alive when eaten
cards.fige: Plate I. Close-up of an opened oyster's adductor muscle and shell interior.
bodye: A properly stored oyster that stays closed, or clenches when tapped, is usually still alive at the moment it's eaten, a common test chefs and shuckers rely on for freshness.

An oyster's adductor muscle holds its shell shut and contracts when touched while alive. After death the muscle relaxes, the shell gapes, and bacteria multiply fast, which is why it's served fresh and live.

Some assume every raw oyster is alive, or worry it suffers like an animal with a brain. Oysters have a simple, decentralized nervous system and no confirmed capacity for pain, part of why some vegans still eat them.

cards.q: 伦敦为何禁止出租车驾驶员戴眼镜？
cards.short: 早年要求裸眼视力达标
body: 伦敦出租车（黑色计程车）驾照曾要求裸眼视力达到一定标准，即不依赖眼镜也能看清路况，这项规定常被简化转述为禁戴眼镜。
早期路况颠簸、车窗敞开，眼镜易滑落或蒙尘破损，一旦驾驶中失去矫正视力便有危险，监管方因此把裸眼视力设为门槛。
如今伦敦出租车驾照体检允许佩戴眼镜或隐形眼镜矫正视力，只要矫正后达标即可，裸眼限制已不是唯一的硬性门槛。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　伦敦黑色计程车驾驶舱内的视野与仪表布局。
cards.qe: Why were London cab drivers once banned from wearing glasses?
cards.shorte: Once needed unaided 20/20 vision
cards.fige: Plate I. Driver's-eye view inside a London black cab.
bodye: London black-cab licenses once required a minimum level of unaided, bare-eye vision, good enough to see the road without relying on glasses. The rule is often retold simply as a ban on wearing glasses.
On bumpy roads with open windows, glasses could slip off, fog up, or crack. Losing corrected vision mid-drive was dangerous, so regulators set the bar at unaided eyesight instead.
Today's licensing medical lets drivers wear glasses or contact lenses, as long as corrected vision meets the standard. The bare-eye requirement is no longer the only route to qualifying.

plate.imgTitle: LEVC TX London Taxi, Charing Cross Station - geograph.org.uk - 5910490.jpg

cards.q: 香港摩天楼为何常在中部开洞？
cards.short: 为风水留出龙的通道
body: 香港部分高层住宅楼体中段留有大型方形空洞，最著名的例子是浅水湾一带的高层住宅，空洞贯穿建筑供人透视山海。
本地风水观念认为，山中的龙需经通道下行入海，若建筑完全挡住山海之间的视线，会阻断龙脉，故开洞留出通路。
这类空洞也带来实际工程好处，能降低建筑迎风面积、减小台风时的风压负荷，风水考量与结构抗风效果常被同时提及。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　浅水湾高层住宅中段的方形通透空洞。
cards.qe: Why do Hong Kong skyscrapers often have holes through their middle?
cards.shorte: Gap left for a feng shui dragon
cards.fige: Plate I. The rectangular opening through a Repulse Bay high-rise.
bodye: Some Hong Kong high-rises leave a large rectangular gap partway up the building. A well-known example sits in Repulse Bay, where the opening lets sightlines pass straight through from hill to sea.

Local feng shui belief holds that dragons travel down from the mountains to the water. A building that fully blocks that sightline is thought to sever the dragon's path, so a gap is left to let it through.

These gaps carry a practical engineering upside too: they reduce the building's wind-facing surface area and cut wind load during typhoons, a structural benefit often cited alongside the feng shui story.
cards.query: The Repulse Bay Hong Kong building photograph

plate.imgTitle: 香港-浅水湾-空心大楼 - panoramio.jpg

cards.q: 哪种语言用口哨吹出完整对话？
cards.short: 戈梅拉岛口哨传西语
body: 西班牙拉戈梅拉岛的希尔博口哨语，把西班牙语音节转换成不同频率和断续的口哨声，可在山谷间传出数公里远。
岛上地形多深谷陡坡，说话声传不远，居民便用口哨模拟元音辅音的声学特征，经训练的听者能还原出完整语句含义。
希尔博口哨语并非独立语言，而是西班牙语的口哨编码版本，2009年被联合国教科文组织列入人类非物质文化遗产名录，学校仍在教授。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　拉戈梅拉岛山谷地形与口哨传音路径。
cards.src: 联合国教科文组织非遗名录
cards.qe: Which language can carry a full conversation in whistles?
cards.shorte: La Gomera whistles Spanish
cards.fige: Plate I. La Gomera's ravines, the terrain Silbo whistles carry across.
bodye: On La Gomera in Spain's Canary Islands, Silbo Gomero converts Spanish syllables into whistled tones of varying pitch and rhythm that can carry for several kilometers across ravines.

The island's terrain is steep and deeply cut, so spoken voices don't travel far. Whistling instead mimics the acoustic shape of vowels and consonants, and trained listeners can reconstruct full sentences.
Silbo isn't a separate language but a whistled encoding of Spanish itself. UNESCO added it to its Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009, and it's still taught in local schools.
cards.query: La Gomera Silbo Gomero whistler photograph

cards.q: 盲文点字最初是替谁设计的？
cards.short: 点字源自军用夜读密码
body: 1819年，法军军官夏尔·巴比耶设计凸点密符，供士兵夜间摸读战报，避免点灯暴露位置，这套「夜读」系统共12点一组。
1824年，15岁的盲童路易·布莱叶将巴比耶的12点系统简化为6点一格，单指一次触摸即可辨认，并改为对应字母而非发音。
盲文并非为盲人从零发明，而是脱胎于军事密码；巴比耶原案因点数过多、外形复杂，军方并未采纳。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　巴比耶军用夜读点符原件与布莱叶盲文对照。
cards.src: 美国盲人基金会；梅勒《路易·布莱叶：天才的触感》（2006）
cards.qe: Who was Braille originally designed for?
cards.shorte: Braille began as a military code
cards.fige: Plate I　Barbier's night-writing dots and Braille's alphabet compared.
bodye: In 1819, French officer Charles Barbier designed a raised-dot code so Napoleon's soldiers could read messages by touch in the dark, without lighting a lamp that might reveal their position.
In 1824, fifteen-year-old Louis Braille, blind since childhood, simplified Barbier's twelve-dot cell to six dots read under one fingertip, and mapped it to letters instead of sounds.
Braille was not invented for blind readers from scratch; it grew out of a military cipher. The army itself had rejected Barbier's original version as too complex to read quickly.
cards.srce: American Foundation for the Blind; C. Michael Mellor, Louis Braille: A Touch of Genius (2006)

cards.q: 大脑把口哨语言当成音乐处理吗？
cards.short: 口哨语言激活语言脑区
body: 西班牙加纳利群岛拉戈梅拉岛的居民用哨音「讲」西班牙语，隔着深谷仍可传出数公里，2009年被列入联合国教科文组织非物质文化遗产。
神经科学研究让土耳其同类哨语使用者做脑成像测试，发现大脑处理哨音时更多调用双侧脑区，不像普通语言那样几乎只依赖左半球。
口哨常被当成纯音乐信号，但脑区反应更接近语言而非曲调；哨语并非独立语言，只是把西班牙语音位改写成音高。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　拉戈梅拉岛峡谷地形，哨音借地势远传。
cards.src: 联合国教科文组织非物质文化遗产名录（2009）；京特库恩等，《当代生物学》（2015）
cards.qe: Does the brain treat whistled speech as music?
cards.shorte: Whistled speech lights up language regions
cards.fige: Plate I　La Gomera's ravines, across which whistled speech still carries.
bodye: Islanders on La Gomera in Spain's Canary Islands speak Spanish by whistling, a code audible across ravines for several kilometers. UNESCO listed it as intangible heritage in 2009.

Brain-imaging studies on a related whistled Turkish speech found listeners process the whistles with substantially more activity in both hemispheres, not the near-total left-brain dominance typical of ordinary speech.
Whistling is usually treated as a pure musical signal, yet the brain response resembles language more than melody. The whistling is not a separate language, only spoken Spanish recoded as pitch.
cards.srce: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2009); Güntürkün et al., Current Biology (2015)

plate.imgTitle: Demostración de silbo gomero, La Gomera, España, 2012-12-14, DD 01.jpg

cards.q: 老式中文打字机上有键盘吗？
cards.short: 字盘检字，不用键盘
body: 民国至1980年代常见的中文打字机没有字母键盘，字台上平铺约两千多个常用汉字字模，打字员移动选字杆逐字挑出后击印上纸。
汉字数量庞大，无法像拉丁字母那样压缩进几十个按键；工程师转而把常用字铺成网格，用检索代替按键，速度靠肌肉记忆练出来。
熟练打字员默记字模方位，手速可媲美西文打字机；生僻字备用字盘另存，需要时现拣现装，并非每个汉字都常驻机上。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　双鸽牌中文打字机字盘与选字机构实物。
cards.src: Thomas S. Mullaney《中文打字机：一部历史》，麻省理工学院出版社（2017）
cards.qe: Did old Chinese typewriters have a keyboard?
cards.shorte: A character tray stood in for the keyboard
cards.fige: Plate I　The character tray and selector arm of a Chinese typewriter.
bodye: Chinese typewriters common from the Republican era into the 1980s had no letter keyboard. A flat bed held roughly two thousand common character types; the typist swept a selector arm across the grid, picked a character, and struck it onto the page.

Chinese has too many characters to compress into a few dozen keys the way Latin alphabets can. Engineers instead laid the common characters out in a grid and replaced key-pressing with searching; speed came from muscle memory.

Skilled typists memorized the map of the tray and could work nearly as fast as a Western typewriter. Rare characters lived on supplementary trays, fetched and swapped in only when needed, not every character sat on the machine at once.
cards.srce: Thomas S. Mullaney, The Chinese Typewriter: A History, MIT Press (2017)

cards.q: 汉字最早是用来做什么的？
cards.short: 甲骨文源于占卜刻辞
body: 商代晚期（约公元前1250—前1050年），占卜者灼烧龟甲牛骨使其开裂，依裂纹判断吉凶，再把所问之事刻在甲骨表面，这就是最早的成熟汉字。
刻辞的目的不是记录给人看，而是留存与祖先沟通的凭证；殷墟出土逾十五万片甲骨，已识别单字约四千余个，能确认释读的约半数。
常以为文字诞生于记账或政令传达，商代的第一批成熟汉字却先服务于神明问答；日常记事一类的用途，是后来才逐渐扩展出的。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　殷墟出土甲骨实物，裂纹与刻辞清晰可辨。
cards.src: 殷墟考古发掘记录（中央研究院）；吉德炜《商史资料来源》（1978）
cards.qe: What was Chinese writing first used for?
cards.shorte: Oracle bone script began as divination text
cards.fige: Plate I　An oracle bone fragment from Yinxu, its crack lines and inscription visible.
bodye: In the late Shang dynasty, roughly 1250 to 1050 BCE, diviners scorched prepared turtle shells and ox bones until they cracked, read the cracks as omens, then carved the question itself into the surface, China's earliest mature writing.

The inscriptions were not written to be read by other people; they were records of a transaction with ancestors and spirits. Over 150,000 bone and shell fragments have been excavated at Yinxu since 1899.
Writing is usually assumed to begin with bookkeeping or royal decree. China's first mature script served the spirit world before it served daily record-keeping, which only expanded later.
cards.srce: Yinxu excavation records (Academia Sinica); David N. Keightley, Sources of Shang History (1978)

plate.imgTitle: Yinxu Oracle Bone Inscriptions for Divination (10185440455) cropped.jpg

cards.q: 滑铁卢战役为何比原计划推迟开打？
cards.short: 夜雨泥泞拖累拿破仑炮兵
body: 1815年6月17日夜里到18日凌晨，滑铁卢战场普降大雨，比利时低地泥泞不堪，法军炮兵和骑兵难以行动。
拿破仑原计划清晨开战，但为等地面变干、便于炮兵机动，将进攻推迟到中午前后，比原计划晚了数小时。
这几个小时的延误让普鲁士援军有更多时间赶到战场支援英军，不少历史学者认为这是法军战败的重要因素之一。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　油画中的滑铁卢战场，雨后泥泞的地面延误了拿破仑的炮兵部署。
cards.qe: Why was the start of the Battle of Waterloo delayed?
cards.shorte: Overnight rain mired Napoleon's guns
cards.fige: Plate I. A painting of Waterloo, where mud from overnight rain slowed Napoleon's artillery.
bodye: Rain soaked the Waterloo battlefield overnight on June 17-18, 1815, leaving the Belgian lowlands too muddy for French artillery and cavalry to move quickly.
Napoleon had planned to attack at dawn but waited for the ground to firm up, pushing the assault back to around midday, several hours later than planned.
Those hours gave Prussian reinforcements more time to reach the field and support the British, a factor many historians count among the causes of the French defeat.

cards.q: 人类历史上最短的战争持续了多久？
cards.short: 英桑战争仅打38分钟
body: 1896年英国与桑给巴尔苏丹国交战，从开火到苏丹投降约持续38分钟，是有记录以来最短的战争。
英国军舰炮轰苏丹王宫，桑给巴尔守军装备落后、抵抗微弱，苏丹很快弃宫出逃，战斗随即终止。
这场战争常被称为「半小时战争」，不同记录给出的时长在38至45分钟间浮动，但都不足一小时。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　桑给巴尔石头城的老照片，英舰炮击的王宫就在附近街区。
cards.qe: How long did the shortest war in recorded history last?
cards.shorte: The Anglo-Zanzibar War lasted 38 minutes
cards.fige: Plate I. Stone Town, Zanzibar, near the palace shelled by British warships in 1896.
bodye: Britain and the Sultanate of Zanzibar fought in 1896; from the first shot to the Sultan's surrender, the fighting lasted about 38 minutes, the shortest war on record.
British warships shelled the Sultan's palace. Zanzibar's poorly equipped defenders barely resisted, and the Sultan fled almost immediately, ending the fighting.
Often called the 'Half-Hour War,' accounts of its length vary from 38 to 45 minutes, but all agree it stayed under an hour.

plate.imgTitle: Puerto de Stone Town, Zanzíbar, Tanzania, 2024-05-31, DD 03.jpg

cards.q: 威尼斯贡多拉为什么全是黑色的？
cards.short: 禁奢法令统一贡多拉船色
body: 16世纪威尼斯贵族竞相把贡多拉漆成华丽颜色、镶金镶银，借此炫耀财力。16世纪中期，威尼斯参议院立法规定贡多拉一律涂黑。
这类禁奢法意在压制贵族间的攀比消费，统一船色也让贡多拉从身份炫耀物变成普通交通工具。
如今黑色常被解读为庄重或哀悼的象征，但最初只是行政规定的结果，并非美学或宗教选择。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　威尼斯运河上一列漆黑的贡多拉，船身颜色统一始于禁奢立法。
cards.qe: Why are Venice's gondolas always painted black?
cards.shorte: A sumptuary law standardized gondola color
cards.fige: Plate I. A row of black gondolas on a Venetian canal; the uniform color traces back to a sumptuary law.
bodye: In the 16th century, Venetian nobles competed to decorate their gondolas in lavish colors and gilding. By the mid-1500s, Venice's Senate had passed a law requiring all gondolas to be painted black.
The sumptuary law aimed to curb competitive spending among nobles; standardizing the color turned gondolas from status symbols into ordinary transport.
Black is now often read as a mark of solemnity or mourning, but it began simply as an administrative rule, not an aesthetic or religious choice.

cards.q: 「让他们吃蛋糕」真的是玛丽王后说的吗？
cards.short: 成文时她仍是奥地利孩童
body: 「让他们吃蛋糕」常被归为法国王后玛丽·安托瓦内特的名言，但没有任何一手史料证实她说过这句话。
这句话最早见于卢梭《忏悔录》手稿，成文时她还是奥地利的孩童，尚未抵达法国。
后世作家把这句冷漠之语安在她头上，用来渲染贵族奢靡，这一说法流传两百多年，至今仍常被当作史实引用。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　凡尔赛宫中的玛丽·安托瓦内特肖像，这句名言从未见于她本人的文字。
cards.qe: Did the queen really say 'let them eat cake'?
cards.shorte: The line predates her time in France
cards.fige: Plate I. A portrait of Marie Antoinette at Versailles; the famous line never appears in her own writing.
bodye: The line 'let them eat cake' is widely attributed to Queen Marie Antoinette of France, but no primary source shows she ever said it.
The phrase first appears in Rousseau's Confessions manuscript, written while Marie Antoinette was still a child in Austria, before she ever set foot in France.
Later writers pinned the callous line on her to dramatize royal excess, and the story has circulated for over two centuries, still often repeated as fact.
cards.query: Marie Antoinette Vigee Le Brun portrait painting

cards.q: 自由女神像最初是什么颜色？
cards.short: 女神像氧化后才变绿
body: 自由女神像1886年落成时，铜质外皮呈暗棕色，与今天所见的绿色完全不同。
女神像外皮为纯铜打造，铜在空气和海盐中缓慢氧化生成铜绿，这一过程持续了约二十至三十年。
许多人以为绿色是最初设计颜色，那层铜绿只是氧化的自然结果，并非人工上色。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　自由女神像铜质表皮特写，氧化生成的铜绿覆盖了原本的棕色。
cards.qe: What color was the Statue of Liberty originally?
cards.shorte: It only turned green after oxidizing
cards.fige: Plate I. A close-up of the Statue of Liberty's copper skin, its original brown hidden beneath a green patina.
bodye: When the Statue of Liberty was dedicated in 1886, its copper skin was a dark brown, nothing like the green it shows today.
The statue's copper surface slowly oxidized in air and sea salt, forming a green patina over roughly twenty to thirty years.
Many assume green was the original design, but that patina is simply the natural result of oxidation, not an applied color.

plate.imgTitle: National Park Service 9-11 Statue of Liberty and WTC fire.jpg

cards.q: 中世纪教堂玻璃为何下厚上薄？
cards.short: 玻璃从不缓慢流动
body: 中世纪教堂彩窗常见下缘厚、上缘薄，厚度差可达两三倍。1998年《美国物理学报》计算显示，室温下玻璃粘度极高，其自然流动所需时间远超地球年龄。
厚度差异源自制作工艺：工匠用吹管让玻璃团旋转摊平成圆盘，再切割成窗格，同一块圆盘边缘与中心厚度本就不均。安装时工匠习惯将较厚一边朝下，便于稳固镶嵌。
玻璃属于无定形固体，室温下粘度接近固体量级，观测尺度上不会流动。下厚上薄现象在近代平板玻璃窗中并不出现，进一步说明成因在于工艺而非材料流动。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　中世纪彩色玻璃窗局部，下缘明显厚于上缘。
cards.qe: Why are old cathedral windowpanes thicker at the bottom?
cards.shorte: Glass never slowly flows
cards.fige: Plate I. Detail of a medieval stained-glass window, its base notably thicker than its top edge.
bodye: Medieval stained-glass windows often show glass two to three times thicker at the base than the top. A 1998 study in the American Journal of Physics calculated this could not result from glass flow.

The unevenness comes from manufacturing: glassblowers spun molten glass into a disc naturally thicker toward the rim, then cut it into panes. Glaziers typically mounted the thicker edge downward for stability.

Glass is an amorphous solid; at room temperature its viscosity keeps it effectively motionless on any observable timescale. Modern flat window glass shows no such thickening, confirming the cause is craft, not flow.
cards.query: Chartres Cathedral stained glass window photograph

cards.q: 猫从高处失足坠落，为何总能脚先落地？
cards.short: 空中翻正靠脊柱扭转
body: 猫的翻正反射约在出生三至四周内发育成熟，即便从静止状态自由落下，也能在半空完成转体。1894年法国科学家马雷用连续摄影首次记录下这一过程。
猫在下落中把身体弯成两截，前后半身分别收缩与伸展四肢，制造不同的转动惯量，再依次转动。整套动作全程角动量守恒，并未违反物理定律。
常见误解认为猫违反了角动量守恒定律，实际净角动量全程为零。翻正反射存在下限，坠落高度过低时躯体来不及完成转体，落地姿势可能失败。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　连续摄影记录猫从倒垂姿态坠落中的翻正过程。
cards.qe: Why do falling cats almost always land on their feet?
cards.shorte: Righting relies on a spinal twist
cards.fige: Plate I. Sequential photography capturing a cat's righting turn during a fall.
bodye: A cat's righting reflex matures by three to four weeks of age, letting it reorient in midair even when dropped from rest. French scientist Étienne-Jules Marey first captured the sequence on film in 1894.

Mid-fall, the cat bends at the waist, tucking one half of its body while extending the other to give each half a different moment of inertia, then rotates them in sequence. Total angular momentum stays zero throughout.
A common myth holds this breaks conservation of angular momentum; it does not. The reflex also has a lower limit: dropped from too little height, a cat may not finish turning before it lands.
cards.srce: International Journal of Solids and Structures

cards.q: 核反应堆水池里的蓝光从何而来？
cards.short: 带电粒子超光速留下蓝光
body: 核反应堆水池和乏燃料池常见幽蓝辉光，苏联物理学家切连科夫1934年首次系统记录该现象，1958年该发现获诺贝尔物理学奖。
水的折射率约1.33，光在水中速度降为真空下的约四分之三。反应堆内高能电子仍能超过这一局域光速，沿途激发水分子释放蓝紫端光子，形成蓝光。
此现象常被误传为粒子突破光速上限，实为超过水中光速而非真空光速，与狭义相对论并不冲突。切连科夫辐射方向呈锥形，可用来反推粒子能量。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　反应堆乏燃料贮存池水下的切连科夫蓝光。
cards.qe: Where does the blue glow in nuclear reactor pools come from?
cards.shorte: Charged particles outrun light in water
cards.fige: Plate I. Blue Cherenkov glow beneath the water of a reactor spent-fuel storage pool.
bodye: Nuclear reactor pools and spent-fuel pools often glow pale blue. Soviet physicist Pavel Cherenkov first systematically documented the effect in 1934; the 1958 Nobel Prize in Physics recognized its explanation.

Water's refractive index of about 1.33 slows light to roughly three-quarters of its vacuum speed. Fast electrons from radioactive decay can still exceed that local speed, exciting water molecules to emit blue-shifted light.

The effect is often misdescribed as particles breaking the universal speed of light; they only exceed light's speed in water, not in vacuum, so relativity is untouched. The glow forms a cone that reveals particle energy.
cards.query: Advanced Test Reactor Cherenkov radiation photograph

cards.q: 滚烫的锅上，水珠为何跳着舞不蒸发？
cards.short: 水珠靠蒸汽膜悬空
body: 德国医生莱顿弗罗斯特1756年在论文中描述此现象。当锅温远超水的沸点，超过约200摄氏度后，水珠不再贴锅面沸腾，而是悬空滑动数十秒。
水珠接触极热锅面的瞬间，底部薄层迅速汽化，垫出一层蒸汽膜。蒸汽导热能力远低于金属直接接触，使水珠悬浮其上，反而比中温锅蒸发得更慢。
常识认为锅越热水珠消失越快，但沸腾曲线在莱顿弗罗斯特点之后出现反常下凹：温度继续升高，水珠存活时间反而变长，这一区间称为膜态沸腾。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　高速摄影记录水珠在灼热锅面上悬浮滑动的瞬间。
cards.qe: Why does a water droplet dance on a scorching pan instead of evaporating?
cards.shorte: A vapor film levitates the droplet
cards.fige: Plate I. High-speed capture of a water droplet gliding on a superheated pan.
bodye: German physician Johann Gottlob Leidenfrost described the effect in a 1756 treatise. Once a pan's surface passes roughly 200 degrees Celsius, a water drop stops boiling flat against it and instead glides for tens of seconds.

On contact with the superheated surface, the drop's underside instantly vaporizes into a thin cushion of steam. Steam conducts heat far worse than direct metal contact, so the levitated drop evaporates more slowly than expected.

It seems obvious that a hotter pan evaporates water faster, but the boiling curve dips sharply at the Leidenfrost point: past it, rising temperature makes drops survive longer, a regime called film boiling.
cards.query: Leidenfrost effect water droplet skillet photograph

cards.q: 移植的心脏还会听大脑指挥吗？
cards.short: 移植心脏无神经仍自跳
body: 心脏移植手术不会重新缝合神经纤维，新心脏只能依靠自身窦房结独立起搏。术后静息心率常在每分钟90至100次，高于常人的70次左右。
窦房结是心脏自带的起搏点，由特殊心肌细胞构成，能自发产生电信号驱动心跳。正常心脏还受迷走神经压低心率、交感神经提高心率，移植心脏切断了这层调控，只剩窦房结自主定速。
心电图上有时能看到两个P波：一个来自失去连接、仍自行放电的原心房残余组织，另一个才是真正驱动心跳的移植心脏窦房结信号，但两者互不影响。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　移植心脏的心电图，可见两个独立起源的P波
cards.qe: Does a transplanted heart still take orders from the brain?
cards.shorte: A denervated heart still keeps its own beat
cards.fige: Plate I. An ECG after heart transplant, showing two independently sourced P waves
bodye: Heart transplant surgery does not reconnect nerve fibers. The new heart beats only through its own sinoatrial node. Resting heart rate after transplant typically runs ninety to a hundred beats per minute, higher than the usual seventy.

The sinoatrial node is the heart's built-in pacemaker, made of specialized muscle cells that generate electrical signals on their own. A normal heart rate is also shaped by the vagus nerve, which slows it, and the sympathetic nerve, which speeds it up. A transplanted heart loses that regulation and beats at the node's own steady pace.

An electrocardiogram sometimes shows two P waves: one from leftover native tissue that still fires but is disconnected, and one from the donor heart's node, which alone drives the heartbeat. The two do not interfere with each other.

cards.q: 舌头真的分甜区、酸区、苦区吗？
cards.short: 舌头味觉分区图是误译
body: 所谓甜区、酸区、苦区、咸区的舌头分布图，源自德国学者哈尼希1901年的一篇论文，后被误译误传为舌面存在明确味觉分区。
1942年，美国心理学家波林将原文中差异极小的数据重新绘图，夸大了区域界限，此后教科书沿用数十年，而多数味蕾能同时感知几种基本味道。
现代研究证实，甜、咸、酸、苦、鲜五种基本味觉在舌头各处都能被感知，只是舌尖对甜咸略敏感，差异极小，并非教科书画出的清晰分区。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　舌面味觉敏感度原始数据，后被误传为分区图
cards.src: 《感觉与知觉的实验心理学史》
cards.qe: Does the tongue really have separate zones for sweet, sour, and bitter?
cards.shorte: The tongue taste map was a mistranslation
cards.fige: Plate I. Hänig's original taste-sensitivity data, later mistaken for a zone map
bodye: The familiar tongue map with sweet, sour, bitter and salty zones traces back to a 1901 paper by German researcher David Hänig, later mistranslated into a claim of sharply separated regions.

In 1942, American psychologist Edwin Boring redrew Hänig's data, which showed only tiny differences, and exaggerated the boundaries between them. Textbooks kept the diagram for decades, even though most taste buds can sense several basic tastes at once.

Modern research confirms that sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami can all be detected across the whole tongue. The tip is only slightly more sensitive to sweet and salty, a small difference, not the clean zones textbooks once drew.
cards.srce: Sensation and Perception in the History of Experimental Psychology

cards.q: 为什么喝水压不住辣，牛奶却可以？
cards.short: 牛奶靠脂肪破解辣味
body: 辣椒素是脂溶性生物碱，不溶于水。全脂牛奶含约3%乳脂，实验中缓解辣感的效果明显优于常温清水。
辣椒素与舌部痛觉受体TRPV1结合产生灼烧感；牛奶中的酪蛋白能包裹并带走这种脂溶性分子，而水只能暂时冲淡，无法真正剥离受体。
很多人辣到流泪第一反应是灌水，实际只会把辣椒素冲到口腔更多部位，让灼烧感暂时扩散而非缓解。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　辣椒果实剖面与全脂牛奶对照图版。
cards.qe: Why doesn't water help with chili heat, but milk does?
cards.shorte: Milk's fat breaks the burn
cards.fige: Plate I　Chili pepper cross-section paired with a glass of whole milk.
bodye: Capsaicin is a fat-soluble alkaloid, barely soluble in water. Whole milk, roughly 3% fat, relieves the burn far better than plain water in sensory trials.
Capsaicin binds the TRPV1 heat receptor on the tongue. Casein in milk surrounds and carries away the fat-soluble molecule, while water only spreads it around without detaching it.
Reaching for water when chili burns is instinctive, but it mostly spreads capsaicin across more of the mouth, prolonging the sting rather than easing it.
cards.query: Capsicum annuum fruit cross section photograph

cards.q: 巧克力表面泛白霜，是发霉变质了吗？
cards.short: 泛白是脂肪析出非发霉
body: 巧克力反复经历约5摄氏度以上的温度波动后，表面常析出细小白色结晶，业内称为起霜，并非霉菌滋生。
巧克力中的可可脂具有多种结晶形态，温度波动会使脂肪重新熔化再结晶，析出的脂肪或糖分迁移到表面形成白色薄层。
很多人看到白霜就整块丢弃，起霜多数只影响外观与口感，风味和安全性通常不受影响，仍可安全食用。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　巧克力块体表面标本图版。
cards.qe: Is the white bloom on chocolate mold?
cards.shorte: White bloom is fat, not mold
cards.fige: Plate I　Specimen of a chocolate bar's surface.
bodye: After chocolate cycles through temperature swings of roughly 5°C or more, fine white crystals often surface — the industry calls this bloom, not mold.
Cocoa butter crystallizes in several different forms; temperature swings melt and re-form the fat, and the migrating fat or sugar forms a thin white layer.
Many people toss chocolate the moment it turns white, but bloom usually only changes texture and looks — flavor and safety are typically unaffected.

cards.q: 下午三点喝的咖啡，为什么凌晨还睡不着？
cards.short: 咖啡因五小时消耗一半
body: 咖啡因进入血液后，人体清除一半约需五小时；一杯咖啡若在下午三点喝下，到晚上八点体内仍残留约一半咖啡因。
咖啡因主要经肝脏细胞色素酶代谢分解，血液浓度随时间大致按指数曲线下降，个体代谢速度受基因和肝功能影响而有差异。
很多人以为咖啡因几小时就代谢干净，按五小时半衰期计算，一杯咖啡的影响往往要十小时以上才基本消退。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　咖啡因血药浓度随时间衰减曲线图版。
cards.src: FDA消费者咨询《咖啡因：多少算多》
cards.srcMeta: 美国食品药品监督管理局
cards.qe: You drink coffee at 3pm — why are you still awake at midnight?
cards.shorte: Caffeine's half-life is 5 hours
cards.fige: Plate I　Curve of caffeine blood concentration decaying over time.
bodye: The body clears about half of any dose of caffeine in roughly five hours. Coffee drunk at 3pm still leaves about half its caffeine on board by 8pm.
Caffeine is broken down mainly by liver enzymes, and blood concentration falls in a roughly exponential curve; genetics and liver function shift the rate person to person.
People often assume caffeine clears in a few hours, but at a five-hour half-life, one cup's effects commonly linger past the ten-hour mark before fading.
cards.srce: FDA Consumer Update: Spilling the Beans, How Much Caffeine Is Too Much

cards.q: 海水的蓝色，是天空映出来的吗？
cards.short: 水分子吸收红光呈蓝
body: 纯水对红光的吸收强度是对蓝光的约百倍，光穿透十米水层后，红光已大幅衰减，蓝绿光相对保留更多。
水分子中氢氧键的振动频率恰好能吸收红外及可见光谱红端的光子，这是分子固有的振动吸收特性，与天空反射无关。
常见说法认为海水蓝色只是反射天空，但阴天海水依旧呈蓝；天空反射只影响水面高光，不改变水体本身颜色。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　深水蓝色与光谱吸收对照
cards.qe: Is the ocean's blue color just a reflection of the sky?
cards.shorte: Water absorbs red light, turns blue
cards.fige: Plate I. Deep blue water compared with its light-absorption spectrum
bodye: Pure water absorbs red light roughly a hundred times more strongly than blue light. After passing through about ten meters of water, red light is largely gone while blue and green remain.

The vibration frequency of water's O-H bonds happens to absorb photons at the red end of the visible spectrum and beyond into the infrared — an intrinsic molecular property, unrelated to any reflection of the sky.
Ocean blue is often assumed to be a mirror of the sky, but the sea stays blue even under overcast skies. Sky reflection only adds surface glare — it doesn't change the water's own color.
cards.srcMetae: Braun & Smirnov, Journal of Chemical Education · 1993

cards.q: 镜子把左右换了，还是把前后换了？
cards.short: 镜像本质是前后翻转
body: 把写有文字的纸对着镜子，文字左右颠倒但上下不变；这一现象几乎人人从小观察过，却极少被准确解释。
镜面只反转与镜面垂直的那一个方向，即前后方向；人转身面对镜子时，是自己把左右轴也一并转了个方向，造成左右颠倒的错觉。
若把镜子放在头顶或脚下，颠倒的会变成上下而非左右；镜子并不偏爱左右，颠倒方向完全取决于观察者与镜面的相对朝向。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　镜中镜像文字对照
cards.qe: Does a mirror swap left and right, or front and back?
cards.shorte: A mirror flips front-to-back, not sides
cards.fige: Plate I. Mirror-reversed text compared with the original
bodye: Hold a page of text up to a mirror and the letters reverse left to right while staying upright — a sight nearly everyone has seen since childhood, yet rarely explained correctly.

A mirror only reverses the axis perpendicular to its surface — front to back. When a person turns to face the mirror, they rotate their own left-right axis, which creates the illusion of a left-right swap.

Place the mirror overhead or underfoot instead, and the reversal becomes up-down, not left-right. A mirror has no preference for any direction — which way things flip depends entirely on the viewer's orientation.
cards.query: Leonardo da Vinci mirror writing manuscript

cards.q: 闪电比太阳表面还热，为何很少点燃周围空气？
cards.short: 闪电瞬时温度超太阳表面
body: 闪电通道瞬间温度可达约三万摄氏度，接近太阳表面温度（约五千五百摄氏度）的五倍以上，是地球上自然产生的最高温之一。
闪电放电通道极窄，持续时间仅几十微秒，传递的总热能有限；空气受热迅速膨胀又冷却，来不及把足够能量传给周围物体。
人们常把温度等同于烧灼能力，但物体是否被点燃取决于总热量与接触时间；闪电确会引燃干草和树木，只是概率远低于直觉预期。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　闪电放电通道高速摄影
cards.src: 美国国家气象局闪电安全资料
cards.qe: Lightning is hotter than the Sun's surface — why doesn't it torch everything nearby?
cards.shorte: Lightning briefly outheats the Sun
cards.fige: Plate I. High-speed photograph of a lightning discharge channel
bodye: A lightning channel can briefly reach about 30,000°C — more than five times the Sun's surface temperature of roughly 5,500°C, making it among the hottest things that occur naturally on Earth.

The discharge channel is extremely narrow and lasts only tens of microseconds, so the total heat delivered stays limited. Air heats and expands almost instantly, then cools before much energy can transfer to nearby objects.

Temperature is often equated with scorching power, but whether something ignites depends on total heat and contact time. Lightning does start grass and tree fires — just far less often than the temperature alone would suggest.

cards.q: 淋浴时浴帘为什么会往你身上贴？
cards.short: 浴帘内吸的涡旋机制
body: 浴帘常在淋浴几秒后向内卷起贴向身体，这一现象十分常见，二零零一年一项计算机流体力学研究首次给出量化解释。
热水形成的水雾在帘内外温差驱动下产生环状涡旋气流，涡旋中心气压低于帘外，把浴帘向淋浴区一侧吸拉。
长期流传的解释是水流带动空气形成伯努利效应吸帘，但数值模拟显示主因是涡旋低压，该研究因此获二零零一年搞笑诺贝尔奖。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　淋浴浴帘内卷气流示意
cards.src: 淋浴浴帘内卷现象的流体力学模拟
cards.qe: Why does a shower curtain cling inward while you're showering?
cards.ae: A low-pressure vortex pulls it in
cards.shorte: A vortex is what sucks the curtain in
cards.fige: Plate I. Airflow behind the inward-billowing shower curtain
bodye: A shower curtain often billows inward and clings to your body within seconds of the water starting — a common annoyance that a 2001 computational fluid dynamics study finally explained with real numbers.

Hot water vapor and the temperature difference across the curtain drive a ring-shaped vortex of air. Pressure at the vortex's core drops below the pressure outside the curtain, pulling the curtain toward the shower.

The popular explanation blames Bernoulli's principle from the water flow dragging air along, but simulations point to vortex low pressure as the real cause — research that went on to win a 2001 Ig Nobel Prize.
cards.srce: Fluid Dynamics of the Shower Curtain Effect

cards.q: 古埃及工人罢工要求什么？
cards.short: 史上最早罢工为讨口粮
body: 公元前1152年左右，拉美西斯三世在位第29年，代尔麦地那陵墓工匠因谷物口粮迟发多日，放下工具停工，前往邻近神庙静坐抗议。
工匠薪酬不发现金，全靠国家配给的谷物和啤酒维生，粮仓管理疏漏或运输延误就意味着全家断粮，工匠遂以停工向上级施压，事件被记入纸草档案。
这场停工是已知最早的劳工罢工记录，工匠并非奴隶而是拿国家俸禄的专业匠人，抗议目标始终是足额发粮，而非改善建墓本身的劳动条件。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　都灵博物馆藏《罢工纸草》记录代尔麦地那工匠停工经过的僧侣体文字。
cards.qe: What did ancient Egyptian workers demand when they went on strike?
cards.shorte: History's first strike was over grain
cards.fige: Plate I. Hieratic text on the Turin Strike Papyrus recording the Deir el-Medina work stoppage.
bodye: Around 1152 BCE, in year 29 of Ramesses III, tomb builders at Deir el-Medina saw their grain rations arrive late, downed their tools, and marched to nearby temples to sit in protest.

Workers were paid in grain and beer rather than cash, so any lapse in the storehouse or delayed delivery meant hunger for their families; the stoppage was recorded on papyrus by officials forced to respond.
This is the earliest documented labor strike on record. The men were salaried craftsmen, not slaves, and their sole demand throughout was full, on-time rations rather than better working conditions.

cards.q: 中世纪欧洲修道院为何养鱼塘？
cards.short: 为常年斋戒日常备鲜鱼
body: 中世纪基督教历法一年中近半天数禁食肉类，从每周五到长达四十天的大斋期，修道院便挖掘阶梯式池塘养殖鲤鱼等淡水鱼备用。
许多修道院远离海岸和渔场，运输鲜鱼困难，僧侣利用溪流筑坝分级建塘，把鱼苗、育成鱼和待食成鱼分池饲养，形成可持续的鱼塘系统。
这类鱼塘并非修行清苦的象征，而是精密的水产工程：西多会等修会绘制引水图纸管理水位，鲤鱼因耐低氧、易于越冬成为最常见的养殖鱼种。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　芳廷斯修道院阶梯式鱼塘与引水渠遗址照片。
cards.src: 芳廷斯修道院鱼塘遗址
cards.qe: Why did medieval European monasteries keep fish ponds?
cards.shorte: Ponds kept fish ready for fast days
cards.fige: Plate I. Ruins of Fountains Abbey's terraced stew ponds and water leat.
bodye: The medieval Christian calendar barred meat on nearly half the year's days, from every Friday to the forty days of Lent, so monasteries dug terraced ponds to raise carp and other freshwater fish.

Many monasteries sat far from coasts and fisheries where fresh fish was hard to transport, so monks dammed streams into graded ponds, keeping fry, growing fish, and ready-to-eat stock in separate pools.

These ponds were not a sign of ascetic poverty but of precise water engineering: orders such as the Cistercians drew up leat diagrams to manage water levels, and carp became the standard stock for tolerating low oxygen and overwintering well.

cards.q: 为什么冰面比冰块本身更滑？
cards.short: 抛光冰面比粗糙冰块更滑
body: 同样温度的冰，压光处理后的冰场表面摩擦系数可低至0.01左右，未经打磨的天然冰块摩擦系数明显更高，粗糙度才是决定滑度的关键变量。
冰表面在熔点以下仍存在一层准液态分子层起润滑作用，若冰面被压光机反复刮平重浇，微观凹凸被抹去，这层液膜才能均匀铺展，摩擦骤降。
过去认为滑冰靠冰刀压强使冰局部熔化，现今研究认为这一压力远不足以熔冰，真正主角是准液态层与摩擦生热，粗糙未抛光的冰块难获同等效果。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　冰场压光机刮平重浇冰面制造光滑冰层的作业照片。
cards.qe: Why is a polished ice rink slicker than a raw block of ice?
cards.shorte: Polished ice outslicks rough ice
cards.fige: Plate I. An ice resurfacing machine flattening and reflooding a rink to a smooth finish.
bodye: At the same temperature, a professionally resurfaced rink can have a friction coefficient as low as about 0.01, while an unpolished natural ice block runs noticeably higher — roughness, not the ice itself, is what mainly sets the slip.

Ice retains a thin quasi-liquid molecular layer below its melting point that acts as a lubricant. Resurfacing machines shave off microscopic bumps and reflood the surface, letting that film spread evenly so friction drops sharply.

Skating was long attributed to blade pressure locally melting the ice, but that pressure is now known to be far too small; the real causes are the quasi-liquid layer and frictional heat, which a rough, unpolished block cannot exploit as well.

plate.imgTitle: Moscow, VDNKh skating rink, resurfacing machine (24397992193).jpg

cards.q: 声音在水中传播比空气中快多少？
cards.short: 水中声速约为空气中4倍
body: 空气中声速约每秒343米（20摄氏度），淡水中约每秒1480米，海水中约1500米，换算下来水中声速约为空气中的4.3倍。
声音靠分子碰撞传递振动，水分子排列远比气体紧密，相邻分子间距小、弹性模量大，振动能更快从一个分子传到下一个，故传播速度明显更快。
不少人以为介质越稠密声音传播越慢，如同泥地比公路难走，但声速取决于弹性与密度的比值，水的弹性优势远盖过密度增加的拖累，固体中声速更快。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　水下声呐换能器收发水中声波的设备照片。
cards.qe: How much faster does sound travel in water than in air?
cards.shorte: Sound moves ~4x faster in water
cards.fige: Plate I. A hydrophone transducer used to send and receive underwater sound waves.
bodye: Sound travels at about 343 meters per second in air at 20°C, versus roughly 1,480 m/s in fresh water and about 1,500 m/s in seawater — sound in water runs about 4.3 times faster.

Sound propagates through molecular collisions. Water molecules sit far closer together than gas molecules and their higher elastic modulus lets vibration pass from one molecule to the next much faster, sharply raising the speed.

It's tempting to assume a denser medium slows sound, the way thick mud is harder to cross than pavement, but speed depends on the ratio of elasticity to density — water's far greater stiffness outweighs its added density, and sound travels faster still through solids.
cards.srce: Speed of Sound in Pure Water, Technical Guide

cards.q: 为什么金属勺在热茶里比木勺烫手？
cards.short: 金属导热速度远超木材
body: 不锈钢导热系数约15-25瓦/(米·开尔文)，铝约205瓦，木材仅0.1-0.2瓦，两者相差可达上百倍，同泡在热茶中，金属勺柄升温快得多。
金属内部自由电子密集，能迅速携带热能扩散，勺头吸收的热量几秒内就能传到手指；木材细胞壁多孔且缺少自由电子，热量传递被逐层阻滞。
烫手程度取决于材料导热快慢而非温度高低，金属勺柄与木勺柄浸入同一杯茶，实际温度几乎相同，手感差异纯粹来自热量传到皮肤的速度不同。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　不锈钢勺与木勺并排插入同一杯热茶的照片。
cards.src: 《传热学基础》材料导热系数表
cards.qe: Why does a metal spoon in hot tea feel hotter than a wooden one?
cards.shorte: Metal spoons conduct heat far faster
cards.fige: Plate I. A stainless steel spoon and a wooden spoon side by side in a cup of hot tea.
bodye: Stainless steel conducts heat at roughly 15-25 W/(m·K), aluminum about 205, and wood only 0.1-0.2 — a gap that can exceed a hundredfold, so a metal handle heats up far faster than a wooden one in the same cup of tea.

Metals are packed with free electrons that carry thermal energy rapidly through the material, so heat absorbed at the bowl reaches your fingers within seconds; wood's porous cell walls and lack of free electrons block that transfer at every layer.

How hot a handle feels depends on conduction speed, not actual temperature — a metal and a wooden handle in the same cup reach nearly the same temperature, and the difference you feel is purely how fast that heat reaches your skin.
cards.srce: Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, thermal conductivity tables
cards.query: stainless steel spoon in tea cup photograph

cards.q: 高压锅为什么能让水烧到120度？
cards.short: 增压使沸点升至120度
body: 标准气压下水在100摄氏度沸腾，高压锅密封后内部气压可升至约2个大气压，沸点相应升高到约120摄氏度，食物因此在更高温度下更快煮熟。
液体沸点取决于蒸气压何时等于外部压强，高压锅盖锁紧后蒸汽无法逸出，锅内压强随温度持续上升，水分子需更高温度才能积累出足够蒸气压。
很多人以为水永远在100度沸腾，那只是一个大气压下的特例，海拔更高、气压更低时水不到100度就沸腾，密闭增压则能把沸点反向推高。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　高压锅锁扣式锅盖与限压阀结构的照片。
cards.src: 饱和蒸汽压力-温度对照表
cards.srcMeta: 美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）
cards.qe: Why can a pressure cooker heat water past 100°C?
cards.shorte: Sealed pressure pushes boiling point up
cards.fige: Plate I. Cutaway view of a pressure cooker's locking lid and pressure-release valve.
bodye: Water boils at 100°C under standard atmospheric pressure, but a sealed pressure cooker can raise internal pressure to about 2 atmospheres, pushing the boiling point up to roughly 120°C and cooking food faster at that higher temperature.

A liquid boils once its vapor pressure matches the surrounding pressure. With the lid locked, steam cannot escape, so pressure inside keeps climbing with temperature, forcing water molecules to reach a higher temperature before they can build enough vapor pressure to boil.

Many assume water always boils at 100°C, but that's only true at one atmosphere: at higher altitude and lower pressure it boils below 100°C, while sealing in pressure pushes the boiling point the other way, higher still.
cards.srcMetae: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), USA

cards.q: 人体细胞总数与细菌数量哪个更多？
cards.short: 旧说十比一被最新研究推翻
body: 2016年剑桥/魏茨曼团队重新测算,成年男性体内细菌约3.8×10^13个,人体细胞约3.0×10^13个,比例约1.3∶1。
此前广泛流传的'细菌数是人体细胞十倍'源自20世纪70年代的粗略估算,长期被教科书沿用却从未经严格验证。
新估算把肠道菌群体积、红细胞数量等参数重新核算后发现,两者其实处于同一数量级,人体更像是与微生物势均力敌的共生体。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　显微镜下人体细胞与共生菌群并置,呈现两者数量级相当的证据。
cards.src: Sender等《人体内人类与细菌细胞数量修订估算》
cards.qe: Are there more human cells or more bacteria in the body?
cards.shorte: A 2016 recount overturned the old 10:1 claim
cards.fige: Plate I  Human cells juxtaposed with resident gut bacteria under the microscope, evidence of their comparable numbers.
bodye: A 2016 recalculation by Cambridge and Weizmann Institute researchers put an adult male's bacteria at about 3.8x10^13 and human cells at about 3.0x10^13, a ratio near 1.3 to 1.
The long-cited claim that bacteria outnumber human cells ten to one traces back to a rough 1970s estimate that textbooks kept repeating without ever being rigorously checked.
The new count recalculated gut microbial volume and red blood cell numbers and found the two populations sit at essentially the same order of magnitude, more a tie than a bacterial takeover.

cards.q: 声音在钢铁中传播速度是空气中的多少倍？
cards.short: 钢中声速约为空气17倍
body: 声音在钢铁中的传播速度约为每秒5900米,在空气中约为每秒343米,前者约为后者的17倍。
声速取决于介质的弹性模量与密度,固体分子排列紧密、原子间作用力强,振动能迅速由一个质点传递给相邻质点,因此声速远高于气体。
常见印象里声音'靠空气传播',但气体其实是声速最慢的介质之一;液体次之,固体传声普遍最快,把耳朵贴在铁轨上能更早听到远处火车。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　钢轨断面照片,示意固体介质中声波传导的路径。
cards.src: 金斯勒等《声学基础》(Fundamentals of Acoustics)
cards.qe: How many times faster does sound travel through steel than through air?
cards.shorte: Sound moves about 17x faster in steel than air
cards.fige: Plate I  Cross-section of a steel rail, illustrating how sound propagates through a solid medium.
bodye: Sound travels through steel at roughly 5,900 meters per second, versus about 343 meters per second in air, around seventeen times faster.
Sound speed depends on a medium's stiffness and density. In solids, atoms sit close together and transmit vibrations from one to the next almost instantly, far outpacing gas molecules.

Sound is often pictured as an 'air' phenomenon, but gases are actually among the slowest media for it; liquids do better, and solids fastest of all, pressing an ear to a rail lets you hear a distant train sooner than through open air.
cards.srce: Kinsler et al., Fundamentals of Acoustics

cards.q: 哪种植物的叶片能承受人的重量？
cards.short: 王莲叶片靠肋状结构承重
body: 王莲(Victoria amazonica)叶片直径可达3米,边缘卷起如盘,若重量均匀分布,单张叶片可承受约45公斤而不下沉。
叶背密布放射状粗壮叶脉与横向支撑肋,内部充气组织增加浮力,把压强分散到整张叶面,类似天然桁架结构。
承重前提是重量必须均匀分摊,常借助木板等分散点压力;若人直接单脚踩踏集中受力,叶片会迅速刺穿下沉,并非可以随意站立。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　王莲巨大圆叶漂浮水面照片,展示放射状叶脉支撑结构。
cards.src: 英国皇家植物园(邱园)物种档案
cards.qe: Which plant's leaf can support the weight of a person?
cards.shorte: Victoria's ribbed leaf spreads out the load
cards.fige: Plate I  Photograph of a giant Victoria water lily leaf afloat, showing its radiating rib structure.
bodye: The giant water lily Victoria amazonica grows leaves up to three meters across with an upturned rim; when weight is spread evenly, a single leaf can support roughly 45 kilograms without sinking.
The underside carries thick radiating veins and cross-ribs, with air-filled tissue adding buoyancy. Together they spread pressure across the whole leaf like a natural truss.
The catch is that weight must be distributed evenly, usually with a board; step directly on one spot and the leaf punctures and sinks at once, it is no platform for casual standing.
cards.srce: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew — Victoria amazonica

cards.q: 世界上最难习得的辅音是哪一个？
cards.short: 捷克颤音ř举世罕见
body: 捷克语字母「ř」发音时舌尖既要卷舌打颤，又要挤出摩擦声，颤音与擦音在同一瞬间叠加，这种组合在世界语言里极为罕见，基本只存在于捷克语。
舌尖位置只要偏移一两毫米，颤音就会消失变成擦音，或者摩擦消失变回普通颤音，捷克儿童平均要到七八岁才能稳定发出这个音。
很多人以为「ř」只因作曲家德沃夏克（Dvořák）的名字才出名；这个音位在捷克语音系统里本就独立存在，历史上其他斯拉夫语也曾出现类似组合，后来演化成了别的辅音。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　作曲家德沃夏克（Dvořák）肖像，其姓氏正是「ř」发音最著名的试炼场。
cards.qe: What is the hardest consonant in the world to learn?
cards.shorte: Czech trill 'ř' is a global rarity
cards.fige: Plate I. Portrait of composer Antonín Dvořák, whose surname is the classic test of pronouncing 'ř'.
bodye: The Czech letter 'ř' requires the tongue tip to trill and produce frication at the same instant, fusing a trill and a fricative into one sound — a combination almost unique to Czech among the world's languages.
A millimeter of tongue misplacement collapses the trill into a plain fricative or the frication into a plain trill; Czech children typically don't master the sound reliably until age seven or eight.

Many assume 'ř' is famous only because of composer Antonín Dvořák's surname; the sound is a fully independent phoneme in Czech, and similar trilled-fricative combinations once existed in other Slavic languages before evolving into different consonants.
cards.srce: The Sounds of the World's Languages

cards.q: 罗马竞技场地下能容纳多少机关？
cards.short: 地下藏数十套升降系统
body: 罗马竞技场地下的”地牢”（hypogeum）分两层，遍布通道与关闭室，考古复原显示环形结构里布置了数十套人力绞盘升降梯，用来把关在笼中的野兽直接送上场心。
每套升降梯靠绞盘、配重与滑轮组驱动，数名奴隶转动绞盘收绳，笼子经竖井升起，触发地面活板门弹开，猛兽在观众眼前突然出现，全程只需一两分钟。
很多人以为角斗士只在开阔地面搏斗；整场演出高度依赖地下的机械调度，德国考古学家团队在上世纪末系统测绘了这套升降系统，才还原出它的真实规模。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　竞技场地下复原图，标出环形分布的人力绞盘升降井位置。
cards.qe: How many mechanisms could the underground of the Roman Colosseum hold?
cards.shorte: Dozens of lift systems lay hidden underground
cards.fige: Plate I. Reconstruction of the Colosseum hypogeum marking the ring of capstan-lift shafts.
bodye: The Colosseum's underground hypogeum had two levels riddled with passages and holding chambers; reconstructions show the elliptical understructure held dozens of human-powered capstan lifts for hoisting caged animals straight up to the arena floor.

Each lift ran on a capstan, counterweights, and pulleys; slaves turned the capstan to reel in rope, raising a cage through a shaft until a trapdoor above sprang open and the beast appeared before the crowd — the whole sequence took only a minute or two.

Many assume gladiators fought only in the open arena; the spectacle actually depended on elaborate underground machinery, and it took a German archaeological team's survey at the end of the 20th century to reconstruct the system's true scale.

cards.q: 水滴从高空落下为何无法砸伤人？
cards.short: 雨滴终速仅每秒数米
body: 雨滴下落不会无限加速：空气阻力很快追平重力，多数雨滴在几十米内就达到”终极速度”，常见雨滴（直径1到5毫米）终速大约每秒2到9米，远低于自由落体理论速度。
阻力大小取决于雨滴迎风面积，雨滴越大表面张力越难维持球形，会被气流压成扁平状甚至压裂成更小的水滴，体积越大分裂越快，速度也就冲不上去。
教科书插画常把雨滴画成上圆下尖的”泪滴形”；高速摄影显示真实雨滴更接近扁平的圆饼状，尖端朝下的经典形状基本不存在。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　雨滴直径与终极下落速度关系曲线，速度随直径增大而趋于平台。
cards.src: 《The Terminal Velocity of Fall for Water Droplets in Stagnant Air》
cards.qe: Why can't a raindrop falling from high altitude hurt anyone?
cards.shorte: Raindrops top out at a few m/s
cards.fige: Plate I. Curve of raindrop diameter versus terminal fall velocity, plateauing as diameter grows.
bodye: A falling raindrop doesn't keep accelerating: air drag catches up with gravity within tens of meters, so most raindrops reach 'terminal velocity' — for a typical 1-5 mm drop, roughly 2 to 9 meters per second, far below what free fall alone would predict.

Drag depends on the drop's frontal area; the bigger the drop, the less its surface tension can hold a spherical shape, so airflow flattens it and eventually splits it into smaller drops — the bigger it gets, the faster it breaks apart, capping the speed.

Textbooks love to draw raindrops as a 'teardrop' — round on top, pointed below; high-speed photography shows real raindrops are closer to a flattened bun shape, and the classic pointed-bottom teardrop essentially never occurs.
cards.srce: The Terminal Velocity of Fall for Water Droplets in Stagnant Air

plate.imgTitle: Curled mudcracks with raindrop imprints (modern; Kodachrome Basin, Utah, USA) 4.jpg

cards.q: 为何磁铁无法吸附铝或铜？
cards.short: 缺磁畴，但挡不住涡流
body: 永久磁铁靠的是铁、钴、镍这类金属里成片对齐的”磁畴”，靠净磁矩才会被磁铁吸住；铝和铜的电子结构里没有这种自发对齐，宏观上几乎不显磁性，磁铁贴上去自然吸不住。
严格说，铝是极弱的顺磁体，铜是极弱的抗磁体，磁化率数量级只有铁的十万分之一左右，日常磁铁的磁场强度根本不足以产生能感觉到的吸力。
静止不吸不等于完全绝缘：把强磁铁丢进铜管，磁铁下落时铜里会感应出涡电流，涡流磁场反过来阻碍磁铁运动，磁铁会像掉进蜂蜜里一样缓慢下沉，这是电磁感应在起作用，并非磁性本身。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　磁铁穿过铜管演示：静止不吸铁，下落却被涡流大幅减速。
cards.qe: Why can't a magnet attract aluminum or copper?
cards.shorte: No magnetic domains — but eddy currents still bite
cards.fige: Plate I. A magnet dropped through a copper tube: no static pull, yet its fall is dramatically slowed.
bodye: Permanent magnets rely on aligned 'magnetic domains' found in metals like iron, cobalt, and nickel — a net magnetic moment is what lets a magnet grip them; aluminum and copper's electron structure has no such spontaneous alignment, so macroscopically they show almost no magnetism and a magnet simply won't stick.

Strictly speaking, aluminum is a very weak paramagnet and copper a very weak diamagnet — their magnetic susceptibility is roughly a hundred-thousandth that of iron, far too small for an everyday magnet's field to produce any noticeable pull.

No static attraction doesn't mean no interaction at all: drop a strong magnet down a copper pipe and its fall induces eddy currents in the copper, whose own magnetic field opposes the motion — the magnet sinks as if through honey. That's electromagnetic induction at work, not magnetism itself.

cards.q: 人类眨一次眼需要多长时间？
cards.short: 眨眼0.3秒，大脑补画面
body: 高速摄影记录显示，一次完整眨眼——从闭眼到睁眼——平均耗时约0.3到0.4秒，其中眼睑真正闭合的时间只占约0.1秒左右。
眨眼靠眼轮匝肌快速收缩拉下眼睑，再由提上睑肌迅速拉起，是人体最快的肌肉动作之一，几乎不受主观控制，平均每分钟发生15到20次。
很多人以为眨眼那一刻眼前会”黑一下”；大脑会在眨眼期间主动抑制视觉输入、拼接眨眼前后的画面，这种”眨眼抑制”让我们几乎察觉不到视野中断。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　眨眼动作分解：眼睑闭合与睁开的高速摄影定格。
cards.src: 《Analysis of Blink Rate Patterns in Normal Subjects》
cards.qe: How long does a single human blink take?
cards.shorte: 0.3s per blink — the brain fills the gap
cards.fige: Plate I. A blink broken into frames: the eyelid caught closing and reopening by high-speed camera.
bodye: High-speed film shows a complete blink — from closing to reopening — averages about 0.3 to 0.4 seconds, with the eyelid actually shut for only around 0.1 second of that.

A blink is driven by the orbicularis oculi muscle snapping the eyelid shut, then the levator muscle pulling it back up — one of the fastest muscle movements in the body, largely involuntary, happening 15 to 20 times a minute on average.

Many assume the view briefly goes black during a blink; the brain actively suppresses visual input during the blink and stitches together the view from just before and after, a phenomenon called 'blink suppression' that keeps us from noticing the gap.
cards.srce: Analysis of Blink Rate Patterns in Normal Subjects

plate.imgTitle: Human eye with eyelid pulled open, anterior view.jpg

cards.q: 哪种天体会让时空扭曲到光线转弯？
cards.short: 太阳早已让光线弯折
body: 会让光线弯折的不只是黑洞：只要有质量，就会让周围时空弯曲进而偏折光线，太阳这样的恒星已能产生可测偏折——1919年日全食观测中，星光掠过太阳边缘偏转了约1.75角秒。
光本身走的仍是”直线”，只是这条直线画在被大质量天体压弯的时空里；质量越大、光线经过的距离越近，弯曲角度就越明显，黑洞、中子星只是把这种效应放大到了极致。
很多人把”光线弯曲”和”黑洞”划等号；这正是广义相对论最早、也是最著名的实证之一——爱丁顿团队1919年的日食观测让爱因斯坦一夜成名，主角不是黑洞，是太阳。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　1919年日全食观测示意，星光掠过日面边缘发生偏转。
cards.src: 《A Determination of the Deflection of Light by the Sun's Gravitational Field》
cards.srcMeta: Dyson, Eddington & Davidson，Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A，1920
cards.qe: Which celestial body warps spacetime enough to bend light?
cards.shorte: The Sun was already bending starlight
cards.fige: Plate I. The 1919 total solar eclipse observation, where starlight grazing the Sun's edge was deflected.
bodye: Bending light isn't just a black-hole trick: any mass warps the spacetime around it and deflects light passing by, and an ordinary star like the Sun already produces a measurable deflection — during the 1919 total solar eclipse, starlight grazing the Sun's edge bent by about 1.75 arcseconds.

Light itself still travels a 'straight line' — it's just that the line is drawn through spacetime bent by a massive body; the greater the mass and the closer the light passes, the more pronounced the bending. Black holes and neutron stars simply push the same effect to its extreme.

Many equate 'bent light' with 'black hole'; this is actually one of General Relativity's earliest and most famous confirmations — Eddington's 1919 eclipse expedition made Einstein a household name overnight, and the star of that story wasn't a black hole, it was the Sun.
cards.srce: A Determination of the Deflection of Light by the Sun's Gravitational Field
cards.srcMetae: Dyson, Eddington & Davidson, Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, 1920
