cards.q: 啄木鸟头骨真的能缓震吗？
cards.short: 啄木鸟头骨异常坚硬
body: 啄木鸟啄击树干时，头部瞬间减速可达约1200倍重力，持续不足一毫秒，每日啄击可达数千次。
2022年比利时研究团队发现，啄木鸟头骨并非弹性缓冲垫，而是坚硬结构，几乎不吸收冲击；大脑不受伤，靠的是脑体积小、与颅骨贴合紧密，冲击应变被分散。
此前认为头骨像缓冲垫一样吸震，这项研究推翻了这一说法——若头骨真能大幅缓冲，啄击效率反而会下降，不利于凿开树皮觅食。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　啄木鸟凿击树干的姿态照片。
cards.srcMeta: Van Wassenbergh 等，比利时安特卫普大学，2022年
cards.qe: Does a woodpecker's skull actually cushion the impact?
cards.shorte: Woodpecker skull is unusually stiff
cards.fige: Plate I. Photograph of a woodpecker pecking at a tree trunk.
bodye: When a woodpecker strikes wood, its head decelerates by roughly 1,200 g in under a millisecond, up to several thousand times a day.

A 2022 Belgian study found the skull is not an elastic cushion but a rigid structure that absorbs almost no shock; the brain stays safe because it is small and tightly packed, spreading out the strain.
Textbooks long assumed the skull cushions each blow. The study overturned that: a truly shock-absorbing skull would blunt each strike, making it harder to chisel through bark.
cards.srcMetae: Van Wassenbergh et al., University of Antwerp, 2022

cards.q: 家猫为什么尝不出甜味？
cards.short: 甜味受体基因先天失活
body: 猫的Tas1r2基因存在缺陷，无法合成完整的甜味受体亚基；2005年基因测序研究证实，这一缺陷见于家猫及几乎所有猫科动物。
甜味感知依赖Tas1r2与Tas1r3两种蛋白结合成受体；猫的Tas1r2基因中一段约247个碱基对缺失，导致受体无法组装，舌头上没有识别糖分子的通道。
猫舔奶油或蛋糕，并非因为尝到甜味，而是被脂肪与奶香气味吸引；整个猫科家族都缺乏这一受体，从家猫到狮子老虎都尝不出糖的甜。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　家猫舌面味蕾结构特写。
cards.src: 《公共科学图书馆·遗传学》(PLOS Genetics)
cards.srcMeta: 莫奈尔化学感官中心团队，2005年
cards.qe: Why can't house cats taste sweetness?
cards.shorte: Sweet-receptor gene is inactive
cards.fige: Plate I. Close-up of taste buds on a domestic cat's tongue.
bodye: Cats carry a defective Tas1r2 gene and cannot make a complete sweet-taste receptor subunit; 2005 sequencing work confirmed the defect in domestic cats and nearly every other felid.

Sweet taste requires Tas1r2 and Tas1r3 proteins to combine into one receptor. A roughly 247-base-pair deletion in the cat Tas1r2 gene prevents that assembly, leaving no working channel on the tongue to detect sugar.
A cat licking cream or cake isn't tasting sugar — it's drawn in by fat and dairy aroma. The whole cat family shares this gap: house cats, lions, and tigers alike cannot taste sugar's sweetness.

cards.q: 捕蝇草为何要被碰两次才合拢？
cards.short: 捕蝇草靠计数触发捕猎
body: 捕蝇草叶片内侧各有三根感觉毛，昆虫触碰一次会产生一次电信号；须在约20秒内触碰第二次，叶片才会闭合。
触碰产生的电信号在细胞间累积，须达到两次阈值才会触发离子通道开放与细胞膨压骤变；单次触碰不足以启动这一过程。
这套机制更像原始计数记忆，而非简单反射——雨滴或枯叶偶然触碰通常只有一次，不会触发闭合，捕蝇草借此避免徒劳消耗能量。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　捕蝇草张开的捕虫夹特写。
cards.srcMeta: 维尔茨堡大学 Hedrich 团队，2016年
cards.qe: Why does a Venus flytrap need two touches to snap shut?
cards.shorte: Flytrap snaps shut only after counting
cards.fige: Plate I. Close-up of an open Venus flytrap trap.
bodye: Each Venus flytrap lobe carries three trigger hairs; one touch fires a single electrical signal. A second touch must follow within about 20 seconds before the leaf snaps shut.

The signals build up between cells, and only after crossing a two-touch threshold do ion channels open and turgor pressure shift fast enough to close the trap; one touch alone can't start the process.
This looks more like primitive counting memory than a simple reflex — a raindrop or falling leaf usually brushes the hairs only once, so it never triggers closure, sparing the plant a wasted snap.

cards.q: 深海鮟鱇鱼的雄鱼最终去哪了？
cards.short: 雄鱼永久融合进雌鱼
body: 部分深海鮟鱇鱼中，体型远小于雌鱼的雄鱼一旦找到配偶，会咬住其腹部，皮肤与血管逐渐融合为一体，终生附着。
融合后雄鱼的眼睛、鳍和多数内脏退化，只保留精巢，靠雌鱼血液获取养分；这种性寄生是深海黑暗中罕遇配偶的应对策略。
并非所有鮟鱇鱼都如此——永久融合只见于部分深海种类，近岸浅水的鮟鱇鱼雌雄体型相近，交配后各自游开，没有寄生现象。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　深海鮟鱇鱼雌鱼标本照片。
cards.qe: Where does a deep-sea anglerfish's mate end up?
cards.shorte: Male permanently fused to female
cards.fige: Plate I. Photograph of a female deep-sea anglerfish specimen.
bodye: In some deep-sea anglerfish, a male far smaller than the female bites onto her belly once he finds her; skin and blood vessels gradually fuse the two together for life.

After fusing, the male's eyes, fins, and most organs degenerate, leaving only testes, and he draws nutrients from her blood. This sexual parasitism is a way to secure a rare mate in the dark deep sea.

Not every anglerfish does this — permanent fusion appears only in some deep-sea species. Shallow-water anglerfish are similar in size between sexes and simply swim apart after mating, with no parasitism at all.

cards.q: 验证了万亿个数，为什么这道猜想仍未被证明？
cards.short: 验证越多仍无法证明
body: 哥德巴赫猜想认为，每个大于2的偶数都能写成两个质数之和。计算机已验证到约4乘以10的18次方，尚未发现反例。
验证只是对每个具体数字逐一核实，穷举再多也只是有限个例子，无法覆盖无穷多个偶数，因此不能构成数学证明。
民间常把大规模验证等同于证明，但数学证明须对所有情形普遍成立。此猜想由哥德巴赫在1742年提出，至今仍是数论最著名的未解难题之一。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　数学家克里斯蒂安·哥德巴赫的肖像版画。
cards.src: 克里斯蒂安·哥德巴赫致欧拉的信
cards.qe: It's been checked against enormous numbers — so why is this still unproven?
cards.shorte: More checking still isn't proof
cards.fige: Plate I  Portrait engraving of mathematician Christian Goldbach.
bodye: Goldbach's Conjecture holds that every even number greater than 2 is the sum of two primes. Computers have checked into the range of 4×10^18 without finding an exception.
Checking only confirms specific numbers one at a time. However many are tested, that's still a finite set — it can't cover infinitely many even numbers, so it isn't a proof.

Large-scale checking is often mistaken for proof, but a proof must hold in every case without exception. Goldbach proposed the idea to Euler in an 1742 letter; it remains one of number theory's most famous open problems.

cards.q: 恒星爆炸时能在几秒内制造哪些元素？
cards.short: 超新星秒级合成重元素
body: 大质量恒星核心坍缩引发超新星爆炸，冲击波扫过外层物质仅数秒，就能把硅、氧等轻元素聚变到铁镍，同时用中子俘获合成金、铂、铀等比铁重的元素。
坍缩瞬间核心释放海量中子，外层物质在冲击波高温高压下被迅速轰击，重核来不及衰变就连续俘获中子，几秒内跳过上百个不稳定同位素，直达稳定重元素。
常识以为重元素诞生要经年累月，实际上金银铂金大部分是在几秒内、恒星死亡瞬间一次性造出，地球上的贵金属正是超新星爆炸的遗物。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　超新星爆炸抛射物中重元素合成过程示意
cards.qe: What elements can a star forge in just seconds during its explosion?
cards.shorte: Supernovas forge heavy elements in seconds
cards.fige: Plate I. Nucleosynthesis of heavy elements in a supernova shockwave
bodye: A massive star's core collapses into a supernova, and within just seconds the shockwave sweeping through the outer layers fuses light elements like silicon and oxygen up to iron and nickel, while rapid neutron capture builds heavier elements such as gold, platinum, and uranium.

At the moment of collapse the core releases a flood of neutrons; outer material slammed by the shockwave's heat and pressure captures neutrons faster than the resulting nuclei can decay, jumping through over a hundred unstable isotopes in seconds to reach stable heavy elements.

Heavy elements are often assumed to take ages to form, but most of the gold, silver, and platinum around us was forged within seconds, in the instant of a star's death — the precious metals on Earth are largely supernova debris.
cards.srce: B²FH, 'Synthesis of the Elements in Stars'
cards.query: Cassiopeia A supernova remnant Chandra X-ray photograph

cards.q: 黑洞视界边缘的时间流逝有多慢？
cards.short: 视界边缘时间几近凝固
body: 广义相对论预言，越靠近黑洞视界，引力势阱越深，时间流逝相对远处观测者越慢；数学上当趋近视界，时间膨胀因子趋向无穷大。
这是引力时间膨胀效应：强引力场会拉伸时空本身，使邻近时钟走得更慢，从远方望去，坠落者的钟摆会越走越慢，画面也越来越红移。
常见误解是坠落者自己也会感觉变慢，实际上对他本人而言时间流逝正常，看到的是外部宇宙飞速演化；变慢只是远处观测者眼中的景象。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　黑洞周围时空弯曲导致的引力时间膨胀示意
cards.src: 史瓦西《爱因斯坦理论中的质点引力场》
cards.qe: How slow does time run at the edge of a black hole's event horizon?
cards.shorte: Time nearly halts at the horizon
cards.fige: Plate I. Gravitational time dilation near a black hole's warped spacetime
bodye: General relativity predicts that the closer you get to a black hole's event horizon, the deeper the gravitational well, and the slower time passes relative to a distant observer; mathematically, the dilation factor grows toward infinity right at the horizon.

This is gravitational time dilation: a strong gravitational field stretches spacetime itself, so nearby clocks tick more slowly. Watched from afar, an infalling clock appears to tick slower and slower, its light shifting further toward red.

A common misconception is that the falling observer also feels time slow down; for them time passes normally — they see the outside universe race through its history. The slowdown is only how things look to a distant observer.
cards.srce: Karl Schwarzschild, 'On the Gravitational Field of a Point Mass'
cards.query: M87 black hole Event Horizon Telescope photograph

plate.imgTitle: Black hole - Messier 87 crop max res.jpg

cards.q: 掷两次骰子点数和为 7 的概率是多少？
cards.short: 两骰之和为7概率最高
body: 两枚骰子点数和从2到12共11种结果，但各结果组合数不同：和为7时有6种组合，概率6/36≈16.7%，是全场最高值。
点数和背后是组合数：和为2或12只能来自一种搭配(1+1或6+6)，和为7却能来自1+6、2+5、3+4等六种搭配，组合越多概率越大。
常见误解是11种和值概率均等，各占1/11；真实情况是概率呈中间高两端低的钟形分布，7最容易出现，2和12反而最罕见。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　两枚骰子各点数和组合数的钟形分布图
cards.qe: What's the probability that two dice add up to 7?
cards.shorte: Sum of 7 is the likeliest roll
cards.fige: Plate I. Bell-shaped distribution of two-dice sum combinations
bodye: Rolling two dice produces sums from 2 to 12 — eleven possible outcomes — but each sum is reached by a different number of combinations: a sum of 7 has six, giving it a probability of 6/36, about 16.7%, the highest of them all.

The count behind each sum is combinatorial: a sum of 2 or 12 comes from only one pairing (1+1 or 6+6), while a sum of 7 can come from 1+6, 2+5, 3+4, and three more pairings — six in total. More pairings mean higher probability.
It's tempting to assume all eleven sums are equally likely, each at 1/11; the real distribution is bell-shaped, peaking at 7, with 2 and 12 the rarest outcomes of all.
cards.srce: Gerolamo Cardano, Liber de Ludo Aleae

cards.q: 生日悖论中多少人同生日概率过半？
cards.short: 23人即过半概率重名
body: 看似一年365天，直觉上凑到过半概率总要上百人，但概率论证明只需23人，两人生日相同的概率就已超过50%。
关键不在人数本身，而在人数带来的配对组合数：23人间共有253种两两配对，每一对不撞生日的概率略低于1，累乘253次后，全员都不撞的概率就跌破了一半。
常见误解是要凑到183人（365的一半）才够，这混淆了「与我同生日」和「任意两人同生日」；后者配对数远多于人数本身，所以门槛低得多。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　生日悖论中配对数随人数增长的示意图
cards.src: 冯·米泽斯《分配与占据概率》
cards.qe: How many people are needed for a 50% chance two share a birthday?
cards.shorte: 23 people beat 50-50 odds
cards.fige: Plate I. Growth of birthday-pair combinations with group size
bodye: A year has 365 days, so intuition suggests you'd need well over a hundred people before two probably share a birthday — but probability theory shows just 23 people are enough to push the odds past 50%.

What matters isn't the headcount itself but the pairs it creates: 23 people form 253 possible pairs. Each pair has a slightly-less-than-certain chance of not sharing a birthday, and multiplying that near-certainty 253 times drags the overall no-match probability below one half.

A common guess is that you'd need 183 people — half of 365 — but that confuses 'shares my birthday' with 'any two people share a birthday.' The second question has far more pairs to work with, so the threshold is much lower.
cards.srce: Richard von Mises, on partition and occupancy probabilities

cards.q: 成熟前的土豆为何有毒？
cards.short: 未熟土豆含龙葵素
body: 土豆块茎在未成熟、发芽或见光变绿时，会大量积累一种叫龙葵素（solanine）的糖苷生物碱，正常成熟薯肉含量很低，但芽眼和绿皮部位可高出十几倍。
龙葵素是茄科植物抵御虫害和真菌的天然防御武器，未成熟或受损的土豆会启动这种防御，把毒素集中堆积在表皮、芽眼这些最易被啃食的部位。
常见误解是削皮煮熟就绝对安全，但龙葵素耐高温、不易被烹饪分解，真正管用的做法是挖去发芽变绿部位，而不是指望高温能替你解毒。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　土豆发芽变绿部位龙葵素富集示意
cards.src: Friedman《马铃薯糖苷生物碱综述》
cards.qe: Why are unripe potatoes poisonous?
cards.shorte: Green potatoes carry solanine
cards.fige: Plate I. Solanine buildup in a sprouting, greening potato
bodye: Potato tubers that are unripe, sprouting, or greened by light exposure build up large amounts of a glycoalkaloid called solanine. Normal ripe flesh contains very little, but the skin and eyes in green or sprouted areas can carry over ten times as much.

Solanine is a natural defense that nightshade plants use against insects and fungi; unripe or damaged potatoes activate this defense and concentrate the toxin in the skin and eyes — the parts most likely to be eaten first.

Peeling and cooking are widely assumed to make any potato safe, but solanine is heat-stable and largely survives cooking. The reliable fix is cutting away sprouted, greened areas — not counting on heat to detoxify them.

plate.imgTitle: Potato with green spot and growing potato sprout.jpg

cards.q: 东京地铁为何雇人推乘客上车？
cards.short: 推手助乘客挤进车厢
body: 20世纪逼近战后的东京，早高峰客流一度超出车厢设计载客量的两倍以上，铁路公司开始雇用戴白手套的站务员，专门负责把乘客推进车厢关上门。
这类「推手」（日语称押し屋）会趁车门关闭前，用手掌和身体把乘客的身躯、包袋一并压进车厢，确保车门顺利闭合、列车准点发车。
常有人以为这是夸张的都市传说，实际这一岗位至今仍存在于新宿、涩谷等超高负荷站点，只是手法更轻柔规范，已被写入铁路公司正式培训手册。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　东京地铁站务员协助乘客上车的历史场景
cards.qe: Why does the Tokyo subway employ people to push passengers aboard?
cards.shorte: Pushers cram riders onto trains
cards.fige: Plate I. Tokyo subway staff helping pack passengers aboard
bodye: In postwar Tokyo, rush-hour crowds sometimes exceeded twice a train car's rated capacity. Rail operators began hiring white-gloved staff whose sole job was to push riders into the cars so the doors could close.
These 'pushers' (oshiya in Japanese) press against passengers' bodies and bags just before the doors shut, packing them fully into the car so the doors can seal and the train can depart on schedule.

It sounds like an exaggerated urban legend, but the role still exists today at overloaded stations like Shinjuku and Shibuya — just gentler and more standardized now, and formally written into rail companies' staff training manuals.
cards.srce: BBC, 'The Men Who Push People Onto Tokyo's Trains'
cards.query: Tokyo Shinjuku Station rush hour photograph

cards.q: 哪种动物的瞳孔是W形？
cards.short: 乌贼瞳孔呈W形
body: 乌贼的瞳孔收缩时呈锯齿状W形，中央窄、两端宽，是头足类中最具辨识度的瞳孔形态之一，常见于多种乌贼科动物。
研究者提出，W形瞳孔配合乌贼单一视觉色素造成的色差，能让不同波长的光在视网膜上分别聚焦，从而间接辨别出颜色差异。
乌贼其实只有一种视锥色素，理论上应是色盲；异形瞳孔制造的色差恰好弥补了这一缺陷，并非只是装饰性花纹或伪装用途。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　乌贼瞳孔收缩呈锯齿状W形的特写
cards.src: 头足类瞳孔与色觉关系研究
cards.qe: Which animal has W-shaped pupils?
cards.shorte: Cuttlefish pupils form a W
cards.fige: Plate I. Close-up of a cuttlefish's pupil contracted into a jagged W shape
bodye: When contracted in bright light, a cuttlefish's pupil narrows into a jagged W shape — narrow in the middle, wide at both ends. It is one of the most distinctive pupil forms among cephalopods.

Researchers propose the W-shaped pupil works with the chromatic blur from the cuttlefish's single visual pigment, letting different wavelengths focus separately on the retina — an indirect way to sense color.
Cuttlefish have only one cone pigment and should in theory be colorblind; their oddly shaped pupil turns chromatic aberration into an advantage, not merely a decorative or camouflage trait.

cards.q: 为什么所有质数大于3后都相邻6的倍数？
cards.short: 质数都是6k±1型
body: 除2、3外的整数按被6除的余数分成六类：0,1,2,3,4,5。余0,2,3,4的数分别能被6,2,2,3整除，必为合数。
只剩余数为1和5（即6k+1与6k-1）的两类数可能是质数，因此除2、3外的所有质数必然形如6k±1，紧贴6的倍数两侧。
这只是必要条件，不是充分条件：6k±1里仍混有合数，如25、35，说明贴近6的倍数不代表这个数一定是质数。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　六列同余筛法示意：仅6k±1两列留有质数
cards.qe: Why are all primes above 3 adjacent to a multiple of 6?
cards.shorte: Primes fit form 6k±1
cards.fige: Plate I. A mod-6 residue sieve diagram: only the 6k±1 columns retain primes
bodye: Aside from 2 and 3, every integer falls into one of six residue classes mod 6: 0,1,2,3,4,5. Those with remainder 0, 2, 3, or 4 are divisible by 6, 2, 2, or 3, so they must be composite.
That leaves only remainders 1 and 5 — numbers of the form 6k+1 and 6k−1 — as candidates for primality. So every prime above 3 must sit right beside a multiple of 6.
This is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one: numbers of form 6k±1 can still be composite, like 25 or 35 — sitting near a multiple of 6 doesn't guarantee primality.
cards.srce: An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers (Hardy & Wright)

cards.q: 为什么19世纪芝加哥曾整体抬高？
cards.short: 整座城市曾被抬高
body: 19世纪中期，芝加哥地势低洼、排水极差，霍乱等疫病频发；1850年代起，全城街道与建筑被整体抬高约1.2至1.8米。
工程队用成千上万个千斤顶同步顶起建筑物，边抬边在下方砌筑新地基，许多商铺甚至旅馆在照常营业的同时被整体抬升。
很多人以为芝加哥抬高地基只是传说夸张，实际上这项工程持续约20年，还为后来的排污系统与摩天大楼地基技术打下基础。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　千斤顶群同步抬升芝加哥街区建筑的历史场景
cards.qe: Why did 19th-century Chicago raise the whole city?
cards.shorte: Chicago was jacked up citywide
cards.fige: Plate I. Historical scene of jackscrews raising a block of Chicago buildings in unison
bodye: In the mid-1800s, Chicago sat on low, poorly drained land plagued by cholera and other outbreaks. Starting in the 1850s, the city raised its streets and buildings citywide by roughly 1.2 to 1.8 meters.
Crews used thousands of jackscrews to lift buildings in unison while masons built new foundations underneath — some shops and hotels stayed open for business the entire time they were being raised.

Many assume the story of Chicago being jacked up is exaggerated folklore; the project actually ran for about two decades and laid the groundwork for the city's later sewer system and skyscraper foundations.
cards.query: Tremont House Chicago building raising engraving

cards.q: 为什么墨西哥城地基一直在下沉？
cards.short: 建在古湖床持续下沉
body: 墨西哥城建在已干涸的特斯科科湖湖床上，过度抽取地下水导致地面持续下沉，市中心部分区域近一个世纪以来已下沉超过9米。
湖床下方是松软的粘土含水层，长期为城市供水而被大量抽取地下水后，粘土层逐渐压实收缩，地表因此持续沉降，且难以逆转。
下沉速度并不均匀：城市不同区域因地下水层结构差异，沉降快慢相差数倍，导致地面出现明显倾斜、开裂甚至建筑倾倒。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　墨西哥城地面沉降对比历史照片
cards.src: 墨西哥城地面沉降卫星观测报告
cards.qe: Why does Mexico City's ground keep sinking?
cards.shorte: Built on a drained lakebed, still sinking
cards.fige: Plate I. Historical photograph comparing ground subsidence levels in Mexico City
bodye: Mexico City sits on the drained bed of former Lake Texcoco. Decades of excessive groundwater pumping have kept the ground sinking — parts of downtown have dropped more than 9 meters over the past century.

Beneath the old lakebed lies a soft clay aquifer; drawing huge volumes of groundwater from it for the city's water supply causes the clay to compact and shrink, so the surface keeps subsiding, largely irreversibly.
The sinking isn't uniform: differences in the aquifer's structure mean some areas sink several times faster than others, producing visible tilting, cracked streets, and even leaning buildings.
cards.srce: Mexico City land subsidence satellite study
cards.query: Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral tilting photograph

cards.q: 木星的大红斑会永远存在吗？
cards.short: 大红斑持续缩小
body: 19世纪观测者记录的大红斑，东西跨度一度超过4万公里；哈勃望远镜近年测量显示，风暴已缩小到约1.6万公里左右。
大红斑是已被观测近两百年的巨型风暴。能量来自木星内部热流与强烈纬向风切变，边缘不断被小涡旋撕扯削弱，令风暴逐年收缩。
这团风暴目前依然比地球大一圈，尚未消失的迹象。但缩小趋势自二十世纪末持续至今，天文学家仍在观察它是否会继续萎缩甚至瓦解。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　哈勃望远镜拍摄的木星大红斑影像。
cards.src: 哈勃太空望远镜「外行星大气遗产计划」（OPAL）观测数据
cards.qe: Will Jupiter's Great Red Spot last forever?
cards.shorte: Great Red Spot keeps shrinking
cards.fige: Plate I. Hubble Space Telescope image of Jupiter's Great Red Spot.
bodye: 19th-century observers logged the Great Red Spot spanning over 40,000 km east-west. Recent Hubble measurements put it at roughly 16,000 km.

The storm has been tracked for nearly two centuries. Powered by heat welling up from Jupiter's interior and fierce wind shear, its edges are steadily worn down by smaller eddies, shrinking it year by year.
It's still wider than Earth, with no sign of vanishing. But the shrinking trend has held since the late 20th century, and astronomers are watching whether it keeps contracting or breaks apart.
cards.srce: Hubble Space Telescope Outer Planet Atmospheres Legacy (OPAL) program data

cards.q: 如果参宿四取代太阳，会发生什么？
cards.short: 参宿四能吞没内行星
body: 参宿四是猎户座的红超巨星，半径约为太阳的700倍。若把它放在太阳系中心，表面将掠过水星、金星、地球、火星轨道，抵达小行星带附近。
参宿四之所以如此膨胀，是因为它已耗尽核心氢燃料，进入演化晚期：核心收缩升温，外层氢壳燃烧加剧，恒星外壳被迅速推开、大幅膨胀。
参宿四看起来只是夜空中一个光点，实际体积却能装下太阳系内四颗类地行星的公转范围。它终将以超新星爆发结束一生，但爆发时间无法精确预测。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　哈勃望远镜拍摄的参宿四与太阳大小对照。
cards.src: 哈勃太空望远镜参宿四成像研究
cards.qe: What would happen if Betelgeuse replaced the Sun?
cards.shorte: Could engulf the inner planets
cards.fige: Plate I. Hubble Space Telescope imagery comparing Betelgeuse's size with the Sun.
bodye: Betelgeuse is a red supergiant in Orion with a radius about 700 times the Sun's. Placed at the center of the solar system, its surface would sweep past Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars, reaching close to the asteroid belt.

The star swelled because it has exhausted the hydrogen fuel in its core and entered a late stage of evolution: the core contracts and heats, hydrogen-shell burning intensifies, and the outer layers are pushed rapidly outward.

Betelgeuse looks like a single point of light, yet its volume could contain the orbits of four rocky planets. It will eventually end as a supernova, though exactly when remains impossible to predict precisely.
cards.srce: Hubble Space Telescope imaging study of Betelgeuse

cards.q: 《神奈川冲浪里》标志性蓝色从何而来？
cards.short: 海浪蓝色是欧洲进口颜料
body: 《神奈川冲浪里》约作于1831年，画面中大面积使用普鲁士蓝，一种由柏林发明的化学合成颜料。
普鲁士蓝1704年在柏林被意外合成，19世纪经荷兰商船传入日本，因其色泽浓艳且价格低于天然群青，很快被浮世绘画师采用。
常被当作日本传统色的浮世绘海浪蓝，源头是欧洲实验室的化学发明，并非本土矿物颜料。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　葛饰北斋《神奈川冲浪里》中的普鲁士蓝浪涛。
cards.qe: Where did the iconic blue in The Great Wave come from?
cards.shorte: The wave's signature blue was a European import
cards.fige: Plate I. Prussian blue waves in Hokusai's Great Wave off Kanagawa.
bodye: The Great Wave off Kanagawa, made around 1831, uses broad passages of Prussian blue, a synthetic pigment invented in a chemistry lab, not ground from any mineral.
Prussian blue was accidentally synthesized in Berlin in 1704, then reached Japan in the 19th century via Dutch trading ships, prized for its vivid tone and lower cost than natural ultramarine.
Though treated as a native Japanese color, the wave's signature blue traces back to a European laboratory rather than any local mineral pigment.
cards.query: The Great Wave off Kanagawa Hokusai woodblock print

cards.q: 兵马俑出土时为何迅速褪色？
cards.short: 兵马俑出土数分钟内掉色
body: 秦始皇陵兵马俑出土时多带彩绘，但陶俑表面的生漆底层暴露在干燥空气中后，数分钟内便开始卷曲剥落，颜色迅速消失。
生漆层此前长期埋藏在稳定的湿度环境里，出土后湿度骤降导致漆层收缩变形，附着其上的矿物颜料随之脱落，与陶胎本身关系不大。
许多人以为兵马俑本就是陶土本色，事实是几乎每尊出土时都曾色彩鲜明，褪色是保存条件突变造成的后果。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　出土初期尚存彩绘痕迹的兵马俑陶俑。
cards.src: 兵马俑彩绘保护研究报告
cards.qe: Why did the Terracotta Army lose its color so quickly after excavation?
cards.shorte: Color vanished within minutes of excavation
cards.fige: Plate I. A terracotta figure with surviving paint shortly after excavation.
bodye: Many Terracotta Army figures emerged from the pit richly painted, but once their lacquer ground was exposed to dry air, it began curling and flaking within minutes, taking the color with it.

The lacquer layer had sat in a stable, humid burial environment for over two thousand years; the sudden drop in humidity after excavation makes it shrink and warp, dislodging the mineral pigments bound to it.

The figures are often assumed to have always been bare clay, but nearly every one was vividly painted when unearthed — the color loss is a side effect of the sudden change in conditions, not their original state.
cards.query: Terracotta Army painted warrior figure photograph

plate.imgTitle: Apart from humans, there are terracotta horses too (35519047822).jpg

cards.q: 梵高生前的画作卖得怎么样？
cards.short: 一生只卖出一幅油画
body: 梵高在世时共创作约860幅油画，加上素描等作品逾2000件，但生前有记录的售出画作只有一幅——《红色葡萄园》。
他的画风在当时被视为色彩过于强烈、笔触过于潦草，不符合主流市场趣味，画商与藏家大多不愿收购。
他去世后画价一路攀升，如今单幅作品拍卖价可达数千万美元，与生前几乎无人问津的境况形成鲜明反差。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　梵高《红色葡萄园》，他生前唯一售出的画作。
cards.src: 梵高书信项目及馆藏研究
cards.srcMeta: 梵高博物馆，阿姆斯特丹
cards.qe: How did Van Gogh's paintings sell during his lifetime?
cards.shorte: He sold only one painting in his life
cards.fige: Plate I. Van Gogh's The Red Vineyard, the only painting he sold in his lifetime.
bodye: Van Gogh made roughly 860 oil paintings and over 2,000 works in total during his decade as an artist, yet only one sale is documented in his lifetime — The Red Vineyard.
His color was seen as too intense and his brushwork too loose for contemporary taste, so dealers and collectors mostly passed on his work.
Prices climbed steeply after his death; single paintings now sell for tens of millions of dollars, a stark contrast to the near-total silence around his work while he was alive.
cards.srce: Van Gogh Letters Project and Collection Research

cards.q: 专家票选20世纪最具影响力作品是哪件？
cards.short: 小便池登顶艺术票选
body: 2004年英国一项调查中，500位艺术界人士投票，将杜尚1917年的现成品《泉》——一个签了名的小便池——评为20世纪最具影响力的艺术品。
杜尚买来一个工业量产的瓷质小便池，倒置签上化名，投给独立艺术家协会展览，质疑「艺术品」只能靠手工技艺定义的传统标准。
原作早已遗失，如今展出的都是后来授权复制的版本，但这件曾被拒展的小便池，仍被视为观念艺术的起点，其影响力盖过了同时代任何一幅名画。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　1917年斯蒂格利茨拍摄的《泉》原始影像。
cards.src: 英国艺术界影响力调查
cards.qe: What artwork did experts vote most influential of the 20th century?
cards.shorte: A urinal topped the art world's vote
cards.fige: Plate I. Stieglitz's 1917 photograph of Duchamp's original Fountain.
bodye: In a 2004 UK survey, 500 art-world professionals voted Marcel Duchamp's 1917 readymade Fountain — a signed urinal — the most influential artwork of the 20th century.
Duchamp bought a mass-produced porcelain urinal, turned it on its back, signed it with a pseudonym, and submitted it to an open exhibition, challenging the idea that art required handmade craft.

The original is long lost; every Fountain on display today is a later authorized replica, yet the once-rejected urinal is still treated as the starting point of conceptual art, outranking any painting of its era.

plate.imgTitle: Marcel Duchamp, 1917, Fountain, photograph by Alfred Stieglitz.jpg

cards.q: 蒙娜丽莎为何会成为世界最有名的画？
cards.short: 失窃事件让她全球闻名
body: 蒙娜丽莎在16世纪完成后长期只是卢浮宫众多藏品之一，1911年被意大利工人佩鲁贾偷走后失踪两年多，才成为报纸头版的焦点。
失窃案持续两年多占据国际新闻版面，画作下落不明期间，反而有大批民众专程到卢浮宫排队，只为看那面挂过它的空墙。
找回画作后，蒙娜丽莎已从卢浮宫众多杰作之一变成全球符号，今天的知名度与这桩世纪失窃案的持续曝光密不可分。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　达·芬奇《蒙娜丽莎》，现藏于巴黎卢浮宫。
cards.qe: Why did the Mona Lisa become the most famous painting in the world?
cards.shorte: A theft made her a global icon
cards.fige: Plate I. Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, now at the Louvre in Paris.
bodye: Painted in the early 1500s, the Mona Lisa was for centuries just one of many treasures in the Louvre, until an Italian handyman named Vincenzo Peruggia stole it in 1911 and it vanished for over two years.
The theft dominated international headlines for two years; while the painting was missing, crowds lined up at the Louvre just to see the blank wall where it used to hang.
After its recovery, the Mona Lisa went from one masterpiece among many to a global symbol — its fame today owes as much to that century-old theft as to the painting itself.
cards.query: Mona Lisa Leonardo da Vinci painting Louvre

cards.q: 超市迷你胡萝卜是独立品种吗？
cards.short: 迷你胡萝卜由碎料削成
body: 1986年，加州农场主迈克·尤罗塞克将折断、畸形的胡萝卜削磨成两指长的圆柱，包装成“迷你胡萝卜”出售。
此举本是为处理销路差的畸形胡萝卜，削掉外皮棱角后统一削成圆柱形，卖相更好，损耗率也大幅降低，此法后被全行业效仿。
迷你胡萝卜并非某种矮化培育的独立品种，超市货架上的“婴儿胡萝卜”多数产自这种打磨工艺，而非专门种植的迷你作物。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　削磨成型的迷你胡萝卜。
cards.qe: Is the mini carrot its own variety?
cards.shorte: Baby carrots are whittled from culls.
cards.fige: Plate I. A baby carrot shaped by whittling.
bodye: In 1986, California farmer Mike Yurosek began shaving broken, misshapen carrots into two-inch cylinders, packaging them as “baby carrots.”
The process turned unsellable, deformed carrots into a uniform product, trimmed of skin and edges, better looking and far less wasteful, and was soon adopted industry-wide.
Baby carrots are not a dwarf variety. Most “baby carrots” on supermarket shelves are whittled from ordinary carrots, not grown small on purpose.

plate.imgTitle: Discarded plastic baggie of baby carrots.jpg

cards.q: 寿司店里的绿色芥末是山葵吗？
cards.short: 多数山葵实为辣根染色
body: 真山葵（Wasabia japonica）栽培周期长、产量稀少，寿司店常用的翠绿膏状“芥末”里，九成以上是辣根、芥末粉与绿色素调成。
辣根气味主要来自硫代葡萄糖苷分解产生的异硫氰酸酯，与山葵所含成分相近，价格却只是山葵的几十分之一，因而被广泛用作替代品。
即便在日本本土，多数寿司店供应的也是辣根调制品，只有高档店才会现磨真山葵茎，二者外观相近，肉眼很难分辨。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　山葵茎的横切面与研磨质地。
cards.src: 山葵产地种植面积统计
cards.qe: Is sushi-bar green paste real wasabi?
cards.shorte: Most “wasabi” is dyed horseradish.
cards.fige: Plate I. A cross-section of a wasabi rhizome, freshly grated.
bodye: Real wasabi (Wasabia japonica) is slow-growing and hard to farm, so supply is scarce. Over 90% of the bright green paste served at sushi counters is horseradish, mustard powder, and green dye.
Horseradish shares the same glucosinolate-derived isothiocyanates that give wasabi its bite, tastes similarly sharp, and costs a fraction of the price, making it the default substitute.
Even in Japan, most sushi restaurants serve the horseradish blend; only high-end shops grate fresh wasabi stems to order. The two look nearly identical to the eye.
cards.srcMetae: Japan's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries

cards.q: 番茄曾被制成药丸出售吗？
cards.short: 番茄曾作专利药丸出售
body: 1834年，美国俄亥俄州医生约翰·库克·贝内特将番茄浓缩物制成药丸，宣称可治疗腹泻、黄疸、消化不良等多种疾病，风靡一时。
彼时番茄刚从“有毒观赏植物”的污名中脱身，浓缩汁液又恰好呈现药膏质感，借着专利药热潮包装上市，顺势推动了番茄在北美的食用普及。
药丸疗效缺乏依据，不少配方甚至不含实际番茄成分，几年内便被更廉价的仿制品冲垮，番茄最终以食材而非药物的身份留存至今。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　番茄植株与果实的植物学图版。
cards.qe: Was tomato sauce once sold as medicine?
cards.shorte: Tomato pills were once patent medicine.
cards.fige: Plate I. A botanical plate of the tomato plant and fruit.
bodye: In 1834, Ohio physician John Cook Bennett made pills from concentrated tomato extract, claiming they cured diarrhea, jaundice, indigestion, and more. Tomato pills became a brief sensation.

Tomatoes were just shedding their reputation as a poisonous ornamental, and the concentrate's paste-like texture suited the patent-medicine fashion of the day, a packaging trick that also helped normalize eating tomatoes.
The pills had no proven effect, and some recipes barely contained real tomato. Cheaper knockoffs collapsed the fad within years, leaving the tomato to endure as food, not medicine.

plate.imgTitle: Naturalis Biodiversity Center - L.0939626 - Solanum lycopersicum - Artwork.jpeg

cards.q: 生腰果可以直接生吃吗？
cards.short: 市售生腰果均经蒸汽处理
body: 商店里标注“生腰果”的坚果，几乎全部经过蒸汽蒸煮或高温烘烤去壳处理，并非完全未经加热的天然生果。
腰果壳夹层含腰果酚等刺激性油脂，与漆树、芒果同属漆树科，性质近似毒漆藤所含的漆酚，徒手剥壳会灼伤皮肤，须经蒸汽或高温处理才能安全去壳。
所以市面标注“生腰果”的产品，只是相对未经额外烘焙调味而言，真正未经任何加热处理的腰果几乎不会流入零售市场。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　腰果与其下悬的假果连生形态。
cards.qe: Can raw cashews be eaten straight off the tree?
cards.shorte: “Raw” cashews are steam-treated first.
cards.fige: Plate I. A cashew nut fused beneath its false fruit.
bodye: Nuts labeled “raw cashews” in stores have almost always been steamed or roasted to remove the shell; they are not truly unheated, natural raw nuts.

The shell's inner layer contains anacardic acid and related irritant oils, chemically close to the urushiol in poison ivy and mango sap. Bare-handed shelling burns skin, so steam or heat treatment is required before the nut can be safely removed.
So “raw” on the label mostly just means unroasted and unseasoned. Truly unheated, unprocessed cashews almost never reach retail shelves.

plate.imgTitle: Anacardium occidentale-- Cashew apple and nut (30853573405).jpg

cards.q: 浓缩咖啡比美式咖啡因更高吗？
cards.short: 浓缩单杯咖啡因低于美式
body: 一份约30毫升的浓缩咖啡约含63毫克咖啡因，一杯240毫升美式或滴滤咖啡约含95毫克，按每杯计算，后者总量反而更高。
浓缩咖啡萃取时间短、水量少，咖啡因浓度可达滴滤咖啡的数倍，但美式常用更多水稀释萃取、单杯饮用量也大得多，总摄入量随之超过浓缩咖啡。
人们常将苦味与刺激感等同于咖啡因高低，而总摄入量取决于萃取浓度与单次饮用量的乘积，并非只看口感浓烈程度。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　浓缩咖啡与滴滤咖啡的萃取容量对比。
cards.qe: Does espresso have more caffeine than drip coffee?
cards.shorte: A shot has less caffeine than drip.
cards.fige: Plate I. Brewing volumes of espresso and drip coffee, compared.
bodye: A 30ml espresso shot has about 63mg of caffeine; a 240ml cup of drip coffee has about 95mg. Per serving, the drip coffee actually contains more.
Espresso is brewed fast with little water, giving it several times the caffeine concentration of drip coffee, but drip uses more water and is served in a larger cup, so total intake ends up higher.
Bitterness and intensity are often mistaken for caffeine strength. What actually determines total intake is concentration multiplied by serving size, not how strong a cup tastes.

cards.q: 东京新宿站为何被列入吉尼斯纪录？
cards.short: 全球日均客流最高车站
body: 东京新宿站是吉尼斯世界纪录认证的全球最繁忙车站，日均进出乘客约350万人次，汇集十余条铁路与地铁线路。
新宿站是多家铁路与地铁公司共用的换乘枢纽，连接JR、私铁与地铁线路，车站周边有上百个出入口通向地下商业街。
许多人默认全球最繁忙的交通枢纽会出现在纽约或伦敦这类超大城市，但按客流量计，东京都市圈车站长期居于榜首。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　新宿站错综复杂的站台与通道网络，连接多条铁路与地铁线路。
cards.qe: Why is Tokyo's Shinjuku Station in the Guinness World Records?
cards.shorte: World's busiest station by daily ridership
bodye: Shinjuku Station in Tokyo holds the Guinness World Record for busiest train station, with roughly 3.5 million passengers passing through daily across more than a dozen rail and subway lines.

The station is a shared transfer hub for several railway and subway operators, linking JR lines, private commuter railways, and the metro through more than a hundred exits into the streets and underground arcades around it.
People often assume the world's busiest transit hub sits in New York or London. By passenger count, though, Tokyo's stations have long topped the list, Shinjuku foremost among them.
cards.fige: Plate I. The tangled platforms and passageways of Shinjuku Station, where multiple rail and subway lines converge.

plate.imgTitle: Buildings with colorful neon street signs at blue hour, Shinjuku, Tokyo.jpg

cards.q: 纽约曼哈顿的南北大道真的朝正北吗？
cards.short: 路网偏离正北约29度
body: 1811年委员会规划确立的曼哈顿街道网格，南北向大道并非正对真北，整体向东偏转约29度。
规划者让网格顺应曼哈顿岛狭长的走向，并未机械对齐地理南北，这样划出的地块更规整，也更贴合海岸轮廓。
很多人默认城市“南北向”道路就是指南针意义上的正南北，曼哈顿的编号街道系统整体是斜的，只被当地人当作“正向”。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　1811年委员会规划图，标示出曼哈顿街道网格相对真北的偏转角度。
cards.srcMeta: 纽约市城市规划局历史档案
cards.qe: Do Manhattan's north-south avenues really point true north?
cards.shorte: Street grid tilts about 29° off true north
bodye: The Manhattan street grid set out by the Commissioners' Plan of 1811 doesn't point true north. Its numbered avenues are rotated roughly 29 degrees east of true north across the whole island.
The planners fit the grid to the island's long, narrow shape rather than aligning it strictly to compass directions, producing more regular blocks that matched Manhattan's actual coastline.
People often assume a city's 'north-south' avenues run true north. Manhattan's numbered street system is tilted as a whole, a rotation locals simply treat as their working sense of north.
cards.fige: Plate I. The 1811 Commissioners' Plan, showing how Manhattan's street grid tilts away from true north.
cards.srcMetae: NYC Department of City Planning archives

cards.q: 为什么人们都以为拿破仑很矮？
cards.short: 身高换算引发的历史误会
body: 拿破仑去世时验尸记录身高五英尺二法寸，约合1.68米，接近当时法国男性平均身高。
英国作家沿用同一数字却按英寸换算，得出约1.57米，加上讽刺画家的夸张描绘，「矮个子」形象由此流传。
「小伍长」称号源自军中昵称而非身材，他所配属的近卫掷弹兵又刻意挑选高个子士兵，反衬之下他显得更矮。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　拿破仑肖像与法英尺寸换算对照
cards.srcMeta: 英军随行医生测量记录，1821年
cards.qe: Why did everyone believe Napoleon was short?
cards.shorte: A height myth born from unit conversion
cards.fige: Plate I. Napoleon's portrait beside the French-English foot conversion.
bodye: At his autopsy, Napoleon's height was recorded as 5 feet 2 inches in French units, about 1.68 m, close to the average French man of his era.
British writers kept the same figure but read it in English inches, yielding roughly 1.57 m; caricaturists exaggerated the gap, and the 'short' image stuck.
His nickname 'le Petit Caporal' referred to rank, not stature; his Imperial Guard grenadiers were chosen for above-average height, making him look smaller by contrast.

plate.imgTitle: Napoleon I of France by Andrea Appiani.jpg

cards.q: 澳大利亚军队为何打不过鸸鹋？
cards.short: 军队完败于鸸鹋的军事行动
body: 1932年澳大利亚西部，退伍兵组成的机枪队奉命清剿两万余只啃食麦田的鸸鹋，行动持续约一个月。
鸸鹋奔跑时速可达50公里且极易分散逃窜，机枪需要人力搬运架设，往往刚架好枪鸸鹋已经跑散，命中率很低。
此役后来被称为「鸸鹋战争」，军方战报承认收效甚微，最终把防治任务交还给自行设置围栏的农民。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　鸸鹋群与澳大利亚西部麦田地貌
cards.src: 澳大利亚战争纪念馆档案
cards.qe: Why couldn't the Australian army beat the emus?
cards.shorte: An army defeated by a flock of emus
cards.fige: Plate I. Emus against the wheat-field landscape of Western Australia.
bodye: In 1932, Western Australia sent a machine-gun crew of army veterans to cull over 20,000 emus ravaging wheat fields; the campaign ran about a month.
Emus can run up to 50 km/h and scatter unpredictably; by the time gunners had set up, the birds had usually bolted, so hit rates stayed low.
Dubbed the 'Emu War,' the operation was later judged largely ineffective, and authorities handed the problem back to farmers building their own fences.

plate.imgTitle: Dromaius novaehollandiae (head) Battersea Park Children's Zoo.jpg

cards.q: 法国大革命为什么要把一天改成十小时？
cards.short: 革命历法将一天定为十小时
body: 1793年法国推行十进制时间：一天十小时、一小时百分钟、一分钟百秒，与同期推出的公制单位配套。
革命政府认为旧历法与旧度量衡都带着教会和王权色彩，统一改用十进位，意在与理性、平等的新秩序相呼应。
钟表商来不及大量改制新式钟面，民众也难以适应，这套时间制度不到两年便被搁置，仅少数钟表实物留存至今。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　法国大革命时期的十进制钟面
cards.qe: Why did revolutionary France try a 10-hour day?
cards.shorte: A calendar that made a day ten hours long
cards.fige: Plate I. A French Revolutionary decimal clock face.
bodye: In 1793, France introduced decimal time: a 10-hour day, 100-minute hours, and 100-second minutes, paired with the new metric system launched the same period.
The revolutionary government saw the old calendar and units as tied to church and crown, and pushed decimalization to echo a rational, egalitarian new order.
Clockmakers couldn't retool fast enough and the public struggled to adapt; the system was shelved within two years, leaving only a few surviving clocks.

cards.q: 郑和船队带回的「麒麟」到底是什么？
cards.short: 东非长颈鹿被当作祥瑞麒麟
body: 1414年孟加拉使团将一头长颈鹿献给明成祖，经郑和船队沿途联络运抵南京，官员将其视为祥瑞「麒麟」。
「麒麟」本是汉语中的神话瑞兽，长颈鹿在东非索马里语中的读音与其相近，官员借谐音附会，用以颂扬皇帝德政。
这类朝贡「祥瑞」在当时并不罕见，学者多认为附会瑞兽是政治宣传需要，而非官员真信长颈鹿就是麒麟本尊。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　沈度所绘献麒麟（长颈鹿）图卷
cards.srcMeta: 费城艺术博物馆藏，约1414年
cards.qe: What was the 'qilin' that Zheng He's fleet brought back?
cards.shorte: An East African giraffe mistaken for a mythical qilin
cards.fige: Plate I. Shen Du's painting of the tribute giraffe presented as a qilin.
bodye: In 1414, envoys from Bengal presented a giraffe to the Yongle Emperor; it reached Nanjing through contacts made along Zheng He's fleet routes, and officials hailed it as an auspicious 'qilin.'
'Qilin' properly names a mythical beast, but the giraffe's name in Somali sounded close to the Chinese word, giving officials a pretext to link the animal to the omen and praise the emperor's virtue.
Such 'auspicious tribute' claims were common at court; historians mostly read the qilin label as political messaging, not a genuine belief that the animal was mythical.

cards.q: 维多利亚时代女性为何吞砒霜美容？
cards.short: 砒霜美容丸曾风靡英国
body: 19世纪末英国药房公开出售「砒霜美容丸」，宣称长期服用可使皮肤透白、目光明亮，售价与普通药品相仿。
少量砒霜会扩张毛细血管并抑制红细胞携氧能力，使人脸色苍白，恰好迎合当时偏爱病弱式白皙的审美。
长期服用会导致慢性中毒、器官损伤甚至死亡，英国直到20世纪初才通过药品法规限制此类产品公开销售。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　维多利亚时代砒霜美容丸广告
cards.src: 坎贝尔医生砒霜美容丸广告
cards.qe: Why did Victorian women swallow arsenic to look beautiful?
cards.shorte: Arsenic wafers once marketed as a beauty aid
cards.fige: Plate I. An advertisement for Victorian arsenic complexion wafers.
bodye: In late 19th-century Britain, pharmacies openly sold 'arsenic complexion wafers,' claimed to whiten skin and brighten eyes with regular use, priced like ordinary medicine.
Small doses of arsenic dilate capillaries and impair red blood cells' oxygen-carrying capacity, producing a pale look that matched the era's taste for a frail, porcelain complexion.
Prolonged use caused chronic poisoning, organ damage, and death; only in the early 20th century did British pharmacy law begin restricting such over-the-counter products.
cards.srce: Dr. Campbell's Arsenic Complexion Wafers ad

cards.q: 古希腊碑文为何写着写着就换方向？
cards.short: 书写方向逐行交替
body: 公元前7世纪至前5世纪，希腊人常用牛耕式转行书写：一行从左到右，下一行从右到左，字母形状也随之镜像翻转。克里特岛戈尔廷法典是现存最完整的实例。
早期希腊字母尚未固定书写方向，牛耕式转行让目光顺势移到下一行行首，不必跳回远端页边。这种写法因形似耕牛犁地转弯而得名“牛耕体”。
牛耕式书写并非希腊独有，伊特鲁里亚文、赫梯象形文字碑刻也曾使用。复活节岛的朗格朗格文更进一步，下一行文字整体旋转180度，而非仅调换方向。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　戈尔廷法典石刻拓片局部，可见牛耕式转行书写。
cards.srcMeta: 克里特岛铭文，约公元前450年
cards.qe: Why do some ancient Greek inscriptions switch writing direction mid-text?
cards.shorte: Line direction alternated each row
cards.fige: Plate I. Detail of the Gortyn law code inscription, showing boustrophedon lines.
bodye: From the 7th to 5th century BCE, Greeks often wrote boustrophedon: one line left to right, the next right to left, with letterforms mirrored to match. The Gortyn law code in Crete is the most complete surviving example.

Early Greek script had no fixed direction yet. Writing boustrophedon let the eye continue straight into the next line instead of jumping back across the page. The name comes from Greek for 'ox-turning,' like an ox turning at the end of a furrow.

Boustrophedon was not unique to Greek — it also appears in Etruscan and Hittite hieroglyphic inscriptions. Easter Island's undeciphered Rongorongo script goes further: each alternate line is rotated a full 180 degrees, not just reversed.

cards.q: 全球语言里“妈妈”读音相近是巧合吗？
cards.short: 源于婴儿发音生理
body: 汉语“妈妈”、斯瓦希里语“mama”等互不相关的语言中，母亲称谓大多含“m”辅音与“a”元音，父亲称谓则常见“p/b/d”等塞音，这一模式跨越数十个不相关语系。
m、p、b、d与元音a是婴儿最早、最容易发出的音节，出现在牙牙学语阶段。各地父母将这些音自然理解成对自己的称呼，语言因此各自独立地收敛出相似词形，而非源自共同祖先。
对应关系并非固定：格鲁吉亚语用“deda”称母亲，“mama”却指父亲。语音相似常被误当作语言同源的证据，实际只是人类婴儿发声能力趋同的结果。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　语言学家罗曼·雅各布森留影，他系统提出“妈妈爸爸”命名理论。
cards.qe: Do similar-sounding words for 'mama' across languages prove common ancestry?
cards.shorte: Rooted in infant babbling
cards.fige: Plate I. Portrait of linguist Roman Jakobson, who proposed the babbling theory of 'mama/papa' words.
bodye: In dozens of unrelated languages — Mandarin 'mama,' Swahili 'mama' — words for mother tend to carry the nasal 'm' and the vowel 'a,' while words for father favor stop consonants like p, b, or d. The pattern spans language families with no shared ancestry.

M, p, b, d, and the vowel a are among the first, easiest sounds an infant can produce, emerging during early babbling. Parents everywhere independently hear these sounds as the baby naming them, so the words converge through infant physiology rather than a common origin.

The mapping is not fixed: in Georgian, 'deda' means mother while 'mama' means father. Sound similarity is often mistaken for proof of shared language ancestry — it is really a byproduct of how infant vocal development converges worldwide.

cards.q: 全球语言里，主谓宾语序是最常见的吗？
cards.short: 主宾谓语序全球居首
body: 语言类型学的大规模统计（如世界语言结构地图集WALS，涵盖约1377种语言）显示，“主宾谓”语序（如日语、土耳其语）占比最高，接近四成；英语式“主谓宾”约占三成五，位居第二。
主宾谓语序常见于格标记丰富的语言：名词自带格尾表明是主语还是宾语，词序不必承担辨义功能。历史上原始印欧语等诸多祖语被重建为“主宾谓”，属后代分支各自演变出不同语序。
英语、汉语、法语等大语种恰好都是“主谓宾”，容易让人误以为这是语言的自然常态。这种印象更多来自现代强势语言的影响力，而非全球近7000种语言的真实语序分布。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　安卡拉《奥古斯都功业录》拉丁语铭文照片，拉丁语传统语序即为“主宾谓”。
cards.srcMeta: 德莱尔、哈斯佩马特主编，2013年
cards.qe: Is Subject-Verb-Object, like in English, the world's most common word order?
cards.shorte: SOV order leads worldwide
cards.fige: Plate I. The Res Gestae Divi Augusti inscription in Ankara — Latin's traditional word order is Subject-Object-Verb.
bodye: Large-scale typological surveys — such as the World Atlas of Language Structures, covering roughly 1,377 languages — find that Subject-Object-Verb order (as in Japanese or Turkish) is the most common, at nearly 40 percent. English-style Subject-Verb-Object comes second, at around 35 percent.

SOV order is especially common in languages with rich case marking, where noun endings — not word order — signal subject versus object. Many reconstructed ancestral languages, including Proto-Indo-European, are believed to have been SOV; several descendant branches later shifted to SVO independently.

Because English, Mandarin, French, and Spanish all happen to be SVO, it's easy to assume that's the default pattern for human language. That impression owes more to which languages became globally dominant in the modern era than to the actual distribution across the world's nearly 7,000 languages.

cards.q: 哪种立体只有五个面？
cards.short: 四棱锥、三棱柱皆五面
body: 五面体最常见的两种是四棱锥（1个四边形+4个三角形）和三棱柱（2个三角形+3个矩形），面数都是五。
多面体的面数由顶点、棱、面满足欧拉公式 V-E+F=2 决定，五个面可以由不止一种顶点棱组合拼出。
五种正多面体中没有一个是五面体：四面体四面，六面体六面，八、十二、二十面体依次递增，五面体天生不规则。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　四棱锥与三棱柱两种五面体的实物比较。
cards.qe: Which solid has only five faces?
cards.shorte: Two basic five-faced solids
cards.fige: Plate I　A square pyramid and a triangular prism, the two basic five-faced solids.
bodye: The two common pentahedra are the square pyramid (one square base, four triangles) and the triangular prism (two triangles, three rectangles) — five faces each.
Euler's formula V − E + F = 2 ties vertices, edges, and faces together; five faces can be built from more than one combination of the other two.
None of the five Platonic solids has five faces: the counts run 4, 6, 8, 12, 20, so any five-faced solid is necessarily irregular.

cards.q: 圆周率为何能用正方形测出？
cards.short: 内外接正方形夹出π
body: 给圆画一个外切正方形和一个内接正方形，面积分别是4r²和2r²，圆面积πr²恰好夹在两者之间。
这说明2<π<4；把正方形换成边数更多的正多边形继续夹逼，边数越多，π的范围就收得越窄。
公元前250年前后，阿基米德用九十六边形做夹逼，得到223/71<π<22/7，误差已不到千分之一。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　圆的外切正方形与内接正方形面积对比示意。
cards.qe: Why can pi be pinned down with a square?
cards.shorte: Two squares box in pi
cards.fige: Plate I　Comparing the areas of a circle's circumscribed and inscribed squares.
bodye: Draw a square around a circle and one inside it: areas 4r² and 2r². The circle's own area, πr², falls neatly between the two.
That alone gives 2 < π < 4. Swap the squares for many-sided polygons and keep bracketing — the more sides, the tighter the range gets.
Around 250 BCE, Archimedes bracketed pi with a 96-sided polygon, getting 223/71 < π < 22/7 — accurate to better than one part in a thousand.

cards.q: 橡果能直接食用吗？
cards.short: 橡果须去除单宁才能吃
body: 橡果富含单宁，生吃味道极苦，还会刺激肠胃；不同橡树品种单宁含量差异很大，有些几乎无法下咽。
处理方法是反复用水浸泡或水煮，把可溶的单宁一点点冲洗出去，直到涩味消失，橡果才转为可食用的淀粉。
北美原住民与朝鲜半岛都有成熟的去涩传统，磨粉后做成橡子糕或橡子豆腐，并非只能当饥荒食物。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　橡果去涩后磨制成的橡子淀粉与橡子豆腐。
cards.qe: Can acorns be eaten straight off the tree?
cards.shorte: Acorns need their tannins leached out
cards.fige: Plate I　Acorn starch and acorn jelly made after leaching out the tannins.
bodye: Acorns are loaded with tannins. Raw, they taste sharply bitter and can upset the stomach; tannin levels vary a lot by oak species, and some are nearly unbearable.
The fix is repeated soaking or boiling in water, which washes the soluble tannins out bit by bit until the bitterness is gone and the acorn becomes edible starch.
Native American communities and the Korean peninsula both developed mature leaching traditions, grinding the starch into cakes or jelly — acorns were never just famine food.

cards.q: 哪座城市的消防栓涂成不同颜色以示流量？
cards.short: 纽约消防栓按颜色标流量
body: 纽约市消防栓的栓帽按颜色区分出水量：浅蓝色最大，绿色次之，橙色再次，红色最小，颜色一眼可辨。
这套色标源自美国消防协会（NFPA）的全国标准，按每分钟出水加仑数分四级，方便消防员到场后直接取用合适水量的栓口。
这套标准并非纽约独有，全美大多数城市都在用；纽约只是因为栓身颜色格外醒目、常被拍照，才被当成代表案例。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　纽约市街头按颜色区分出水量等级的消防栓。
cards.src: NFPA 291消防栓测试与标识标准
cards.qe: Which city color-codes fire hydrants by flow rate?
cards.shorte: NYC hydrants are color-coded by flow
cards.fige: Plate I　A New York City fire hydrant capped in a color that marks its flow class.
bodye: New York City caps its hydrants by color to signal water output: light blue for the highest flow, green next, then orange, then red for the lowest — readable at a glance.
The code comes from the National Fire Protection Association's national standard, sorting hydrants into four classes by gallons per minute so firefighters can grab the right one fast.
The standard isn't unique to New York — most U.S. cities use it. New York just became the poster example because its hydrants get photographed so often.
cards.srce: NFPA 291: Recommended Practice for Fire Flow Testing and Marking of Hydrants

cards.q: 为什么鸵鸟的眼球比脑更重？
cards.short: 鸵鸟眼球比脑还重
body: 鸵鸟眼球直径约5厘米，是陆地动物里最大的眼睛，重量能超过它自己的大脑，脑只有几十克。
非洲稀树草原视野开阔，天敌又靠速度突袭，硕大的眼睛能在数公里外发现动静，这对生存比脑容量更关键。
鸵鸟并不比其他鸟类笨：眼睛占据头骨大半空间挤压了脑腔，这是空间分配问题，并非智力被眼睛占用。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　鸵鸟头骨中眼窝与脑腔的相对大小。
cards.src: 吉尼斯世界纪录：陆生动物最大眼睛
cards.srcMeta: 吉尼斯世界纪录（Guinness World Records）
cards.qe: Why is an ostrich's eyeball heavier than its brain?
cards.shorte: An ostrich's eye outweighs its brain
cards.fige: Plate I　The relative size of the eye socket and brain cavity in an ostrich skull.
bodye: An ostrich's eyeball is about 5 centimeters across, the largest of any land animal, and it can outweigh the bird's own brain, which runs only a few dozen grams.
On the open African savanna, predators rely on speed and surprise; a huge eye can spot movement kilometers away, which matters more for survival than extra brain tissue.
Ostriches aren't dumber than other birds: the eyes simply take up most of the skull, crowding the brain cavity. It's a matter of space allocation, not intelligence lost to eyesight.
cards.srce: Guinness World Records: Largest eye of a land animal

cards.q: 为什么湿衣服贴身时感觉更冷？
cards.short: 湿衣导热又助蒸发散热
body: 水的导热速率约为空气的23倍，湿衣贴肤时体热经水迅速导出；水分蒸发每克再吸热约2260焦耳，两者叠加显著提升散热速度。
水分子间氢键紧密，导热效率远高于空气分子；同时蒸发吸走的是皮肤表面的高能水分子，带走的热量称潜热，因此体感温度骤降。
并非衣物本身变冷，而是它加速了热量流失；干衣同样能导热，只是速度慢得多，风力越大蒸发越快，体感也越冷。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　湿棉布纤维微距摄影，展示水膜贴肤加速导热与蒸发的路径。
cards.qe: Why does wet clothing against skin feel colder?
cards.shorte: Wet fabric conducts and evaporates heat fast
cards.fige: Plate I. Macro photograph of wet cotton fiber, showing the heat path through the water film against skin.
bodye: Water conducts heat about 23 times faster than air; wet clothing draws body heat away through the water quickly, while evaporation absorbs roughly 2,260 joules per gram, and the two effects combine to sharply speed up cooling.

Water molecules are tightly bonded by hydrogen bonds, giving water far higher thermal conductivity than air; evaporation also removes the highest-energy water molecules from the skin's surface, carrying away latent heat.
The clothing itself isn't cold — it accelerates heat loss; dry fabric conducts heat too, just far more slowly, and the stronger the wind, the faster the evaporation and the colder it feels.
cards.srce: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics

cards.q: 为何人不能自己挠自己痒？
cards.short: 小脑预判抵消触感
body: 1998年英国神经科学家萨拉-杰恩·布莱克摩尔团队用机械臂实验证明，自己触碰产生的感觉体验明显弱于他人以相同方式触碰。
大脑在发出运动指令的同时，小脑会生成一份感觉预测，提前抵消即将到来的触觉信号，这种自我预判使触感被大幅削弱，痒感随之减弱。
实验中若用延迟或不规则装置改变触碰的时间和路径，预判就会失准，此时自己挠痒也能重新感到痒，说明关键在于能否被准确预测，而非谁在挠。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　人体小脑解剖剖面图，标示与体感皮层相连的预测回路。
cards.src: Blakemore SJ, Wolpert DM, Frith CD. (1998). Central Cancellation of Self-produced Tickle Sensation.
cards.qe: Why can't people tickle themselves?
cards.shorte: Cerebellum cancels the expected touch
cards.fige: Plate I. Cross-section of the human cerebellum, showing the predictive circuit linked to somatosensory cortex.
bodye: In 1998, British neuroscientist Sarah-Jayne Blakemore's team used a robotic arm to show that self-produced touch feels markedly weaker than the identical touch delivered by someone else.

As the brain issues a motor command, the cerebellum generates a sensory prediction that cancels the incoming touch signal in advance; this self-prediction blunts the sensation and dulls the ticklish feeling.

When the device adds a delay or randomizes the touch's timing and path, the prediction fails and self-tickling can feel ticklish again — showing predictability, not who does the tickling, is what matters.
cards.srce: Blakemore, S.J., Wolpert, D.M., Frith, C.D. (1998). Central Cancellation of Self-produced Tickle Sensation.

cards.q: 人的骨骼为何不是一体成型？
cards.short: 婴儿骨块多利于生长愈合
body: 新生儿全身约有270到300块骨骼组织，成年后融合为206块；骨骼分块生长，靠骨骺软骨板不断延长，直至约18到25岁才闭合。
分成多块再由关节连接，既能各骨独立生长而不破坏整体结构，又能借助关节实现弯曲、旋转等灵活运动，这是单一整块骨骼无法完成的。
各骨骺闭合时间并不同步，例如锁骨要到约25岁才完全愈合，是全身最晚定型的骨骼；骨折时也只需修复受损的一块，无需处理整副骨架。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　人体骨骼全身正面解剖图，标示主要骨块与关节分布。
cards.src: Scheuer L, Black S. (2000). Developmental Juvenile Osteology.
cards.qe: Why isn't the human skeleton formed as one piece?
cards.shorte: More infant bones ease growth and healing
cards.fige: Plate I. Full anterior anatomical illustration of the human skeleton, showing major bones and joints.
bodye: A newborn has roughly 270 to 300 separate bony elements, fusing into 206 by adulthood; bones lengthen at cartilage growth plates, which typically don't close until about age 18 to 25.

Splitting the skeleton into pieces joined by joints lets each bone grow independently without disrupting overall structure, while joints enable bending, rotation, and other movement a single fused mass could not.

Growth plates close at different times — the clavicle, for instance, doesn't fully fuse until about 25, the last bone to mature; a fracture also only requires repairing the one affected bone, not the whole frame.
cards.srce: Scheuer, L., Black, S. (2000). Developmental Juvenile Osteology.

cards.q: 血液为何要分成红细胞和血浆？
cards.short: 红细胞与血浆密度不同分层
body: 全血由约55%血浆与45%红细胞按体积组成，二者密度不同——红细胞约1.10克/立方厘米，血浆约1.03——因此静置或离心后会分层。
红细胞专职携带血红蛋白运输氧气，血浆则以水为主运送蛋白质、营养、激素与代谢废物；功能分开让二者各自优化，也降低了全血整体黏稠度。
血液在血管中因心脏搏动持续流动混合，并不会自然分层；分层只发生在离心或静置的试管中，古代医生曾误将其中白细胞与血小板层当作病态物质。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　离心后血液试管分层照片，标示血浆、白细胞层与红细胞层比例。
cards.src: Hoffbrand AV, Moss PAH. (2016). Essential Haematology.
cards.qe: Why does blood separate into red blood cells and plasma?
cards.shorte: Red cells and plasma differ in density and layer apart
cards.fige: Plate I. Photograph of a centrifuged blood tube, showing the proportions of plasma, white cell layer, and red cells.
bodye: Whole blood is roughly 55% plasma and 45% red blood cells by volume; the two differ in density — red cells about 1.10 g/cm3, plasma about 1.03 — so they separate into layers when left standing or centrifuged.

Red cells specialize in carrying hemoglobin to transport oxygen, while water-based plasma carries proteins, nutrients, hormones, and metabolic waste; splitting the functions optimizes each and lowers whole blood's viscosity.

Inside vessels, the heartbeat keeps blood constantly mixed, so it never naturally separates; layering only happens in a centrifuged or standing tube, and early physicians once mistook the white cell and platelet layer for a diseased substance.
cards.srce: Hoffbrand, A.V., Moss, P.A.H. (2016). Essential Haematology.

cards.q: 太阳会在哪个方向膨胀成红巨星？
cards.short: 各向均匀膨胀，非定向
body: 约50亿年后，太阳核心氢燃料耗尽，外层膨胀为红巨星，半径将增至现在约200倍，接近今天地球公转轨道的距离。
太阳自转缓慢、近似球形，膨胀是外层气体在自身引力与内部辐射压作用下的整体反应，没有哪个方向受力更大，因此各方向扩张速度基本一致。
扩张均匀不代表结局确定：太阳质量流失会使地球轨道外移，一些模型显示地球有望勉强逃过吞没，但膨胀外层的阻力也可能把地球重新拖入。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　毕宿五红巨星示意图，参照展示恒星膨胀后的层次结构。
cards.src: Schroder KP, Connon Smith R. (2008). Distant Future of the Sun and Earth Revisited.
cards.srcMeta: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society，2008年
cards.qe: In which direction will the Sun expand into a red giant?
cards.shorte: Expansion is isotropic, not directional
cards.fige: Plate I. Illustration of Aldebaran, a red giant star, shown as a reference for a star's expanded outer layers.
bodye: In about 5 billion years, the Sun's core will exhaust its hydrogen fuel and its outer layers will swell into a red giant, its radius growing to roughly 200 times today's — near the distance of Earth's current orbit.

The Sun spins slowly and stays nearly spherical; the expansion is the outer gas envelope's overall response to gravity and internal radiation pressure, with no direction favored, so it swells at essentially the same rate all around.

Uniform expansion doesn't settle the ending: mass loss from the Sun should push Earth's orbit outward, and some models suggest Earth narrowly escapes being engulfed, while drag from the swollen outer layers could still pull it back in.
cards.srce: Schroder, K.P., Connon Smith, R. (2008). Distant Future of the Sun and Earth Revisited.
cards.srcMetae: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 2008

cards.q: 中子星的一茶匙物质有多重？
cards.short: 中子星物质密度近原子核
body: 中子星核心密度约为每立方厘米4亿吨，接近原子核的密度；一茶匙（约5毫升）这种物质的质量可达约10亿吨，接近一座小型山脉。
大质量恒星核心坍缩时，电子被压入质子形成中子，电子简并压无法再支撑重力，物质被压缩到几乎没有原子间空隙，密度因此逼近原子核本身。
这份质量无法真正舀出带走：脱离中子星巨大引力后，物质会因失去约束瞬间释放能量并解体，茶匙里装的只是等效质量，而非可保存的实物。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　蟹状星云脉冲星艺术想象图，标示中子星内部密度分层。
cards.src: Lattimer JM. (2012). The Nuclear Equation of State and Neutron Star Masses.
cards.srcMeta: Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science，2012年
cards.qe: How much would a teaspoon of neutron star matter weigh?
cards.shorte: Neutron star matter nears nuclear density
cards.fige: Plate I. Artist's illustration of the Crab Pulsar, showing the density layers inside a neutron star.
bodye: A neutron star's core reaches a density of about 400 million tons per cubic centimeter, near that of an atomic nucleus; a teaspoon (about 5 mL) of it would weigh roughly a billion tons — close to a small mountain range.

When a massive star's core collapses, electrons are forced into protons to form neutrons; electron degeneracy pressure can no longer resist gravity, and matter is compressed until almost no space remains between particles.

This mass could never actually be scooped out: freed from the neutron star's immense gravity, the matter would instantly release energy and disintegrate — the teaspoon holds an equivalent mass, not a storable object.
cards.srce: Lattimer, J.M. (2012). The Nuclear Equation of State and Neutron Star Masses.
cards.srcMetae: Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science, 2012

cards.q: 胃为什么没把自己消化掉？
cards.short: 胃黏液层隔绝强酸
body: 胃液pH可低至1.5，堪比强酸；胃壁内侧却覆盖着约0.5毫米厚的黏液-碳酸氢盐屏障，酸液无法直接接触细胞表面。
黏液层由胃壁细胞持续分泌并快速更新，胃上皮细胞本身每2到4天就整体更替一轮，受损细胞尚未被腐蚀就已脱落重生。
黏液屏障被削弱时（如长期服用某些消炎药或感染幽门螺杆菌），胃酸才会真正侵蚀胃壁，这才是溃疡常见成因，并非胃酸本身有问题。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　胃黏膜组织切面与黏液-碳酸氢盐屏障示意
cards.qe: Why doesn't the stomach digest itself?
cards.shorte: A mucus layer shields the stomach
cards.fige: Plate I. Cross-section of gastric mucosa and its mucus-bicarbonate barrier
bodye: Gastric juice can reach pH 1.5, a strongly acidic level. Yet the stomach lining is coated with a mucus-bicarbonate barrier about 0.5 millimeters thick that keeps acid from touching living cells.
The mucus layer is constantly secreted and renewed, and the epithelial cells beneath it are replaced entirely every two to four days, shedding before acid can wear them down.
Ulcers form only once this barrier is weakened, commonly by long-term use of certain anti-inflammatory drugs or infection with H. pylori. The acid itself was never the flaw.
cards.srce: Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology

cards.q: 为何莫奈晚年画作色彩偏红黄？
cards.short: 白内障染红晚期画作
body: 莫奈晚年患白内障,自述约1912年发病,1923年才接受手术。患病期间他的画作蓝紫色明显减少,红黄色调大幅增加。
老年白内障使晶状体变浑浊发黄,滤掉部分蓝紫光,视网膜接收的光线整体偏暖,他晚期用色随之显著偏红黄。
晚年手术后他重新调整部分画作色调,但仍有作品保留偏红黄的原状,后世研究常借助这批画作反推白内障病程。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　莫奈《日本桥》(1922)画面整体呈红橙色调
cards.qe: Why did Monet's late paintings turn reddish-yellow?
cards.shorte: Cataracts reddened his late works
cards.fige: Plate I. Monet's 1922 painting The Japanese Footbridge, dominated by red-orange tones
bodye: Monet developed cataracts in his later years, by his own account around 1912, and underwent surgery only in 1923. During this period his paintings show far less blue-violet and much more red-yellow.
Aging cataracts cloud and yellow the eye's lens, filtering out blue and violet light, so the retina receives an overall warmer light, pushing his late palette toward red and yellow.
After surgery he revised some works, but other paintings kept their reddish tone as painted. Later researchers use these color shifts to help date the progression of his cataracts.

plate.imgTitle: Claude Monet - The Japanese Footbridge (Museum of Fine Arts, Houston).jpg

cards.q: 为什么面包放冰箱会变硬变干？
cards.short: 冷藏加速面包淀粉老化
body: 面包冷藏后比放在常温下更快变硬变干,这一现象在食品科学中称为淀粉老化(回生),0-4°C正是回生速度最快的温区。
面包中的淀粉分子在烘烤时吸水糊化,冷却后逐渐重新排列结晶,冰箱温度恰好落在结晶速度最快的区间,比冷冻或室温都更快变硬。
真正延缓老化的做法是冷冻保存,零下低温会抑制分子运动,回生速度反而大幅下降,室温存放短期内也比冷藏更软。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　切片白面包实物照片
cards.src: Cornford, Axford & Elton, J. Sci. Food Agric.
cards.qe: Why does bread go hard and dry faster in the fridge?
cards.shorte: Fridge speeds up starch retrogradation
cards.fige: Plate I. A photograph of a sliced loaf of white bread
bodye: Bread hardens and dries out faster in the refrigerator than at room temperature - a process food scientists call starch retrogradation. The 0-4°C range happens to be where retrogradation runs fastest.

Starch molecules gelatinize by absorbing water during baking, then slowly recrystallize as the loaf cools. Refrigerator temperatures sit right in the range where that recrystallization is quickest, faster than either freezing or room temperature.

The real fix is freezing: sub-zero cold suppresses molecular movement, so retrogradation slows dramatically. Bread left at room temperature for a short while even stays softer than refrigerated bread.
cards.srce: Cornford, Axford & Elton, J. Sci. Food Agric.

cards.q: 阿姆斯特丹运河边房子为何多向前倾？
cards.short: 屋顶滑轮吊运家具入户
body: 阿姆斯特丹许多运河边老宅的正面明显向街道方向前倾,倾角可达数度,并非年久失修,而是当初建造时的刻意设计。
这类房屋楼梯狭窄陡峭,大件家具无法从室内搬运上楼,外墙顶部装有伸出的吊钩或横梁,家具靠滑轮从窗外吊入,前倾可让货物起吊时不撞墙面。
如今这类装置多已成为装饰性遗存,不少家庭仍会在搬家时真实使用它吊运沙发或衣柜,前倾角度在市政规范中被允许,但有上限。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　阿姆斯特丹运河边前倾山墙老宅照片
cards.qe: Why do Amsterdam's canal houses lean forward?
cards.shorte: A pulley beam hoists furniture through windows
cards.fige: Plate I. A photograph of forward-leaning canal houses in Amsterdam
bodye: Many old canal-side houses in Amsterdam visibly lean toward the street, sometimes by several degrees. It isn't decay - the tilt was built in on purpose.

These houses have narrow, steep staircases that can't fit large furniture. A hoisting beam juts out from the top of the facade, so furniture is winched up and in through the windows by pulley; the forward lean keeps swinging loads from hitting the wall.
Today the beams are mostly decorative, though some households still use them for real when moving in a sofa or wardrobe. City regulations permit the forward lean, but only up to a limit.
cards.query: Amsterdam canal house facade hoisting beam photograph

plate.imgTitle: Water reflection of canal houses at blue hour in Damrak Amsterdam the Netherlands.jpg

cards.q: 蜘蛛的血液是什么颜色？
cards.short: 血蓝蛋白呈淡蓝色
body: 蜘蛛没有红细胞与血红蛋白，血淋巴中溶解的呼吸蛋白是血蓝蛋白，靠铜离子而非铁离子结合氧气，氧合后液体呈淡蓝色。
血蓝蛋白分子远大于血红蛋白，直接游离溶于血淋巴而不装入细胞；铜离子结合氧后改变光吸收特性，浓度足够时才会透出蓝色，缺氧或稀薄时接近无色。
科幻或想象中常把蜘蛛血画成墨水般艳蓝，实际多数蜘蛛血淋巴接近无色到浅蓝，远不如鲎血浓重，需汇聚成滴或借显微镜才能看出蓝调。
cards.fig: 图版Ⅰ　欧洲园蛛（Araneus diadematus）标本照片。
cards.qe: What color is spider blood?
cards.shorte: Hemocyanin tints it blue
cards.fige: Plate I. Specimen photograph of the European garden spider (Araneus diadematus).
bodye: Spiders have no red blood cells or hemoglobin. The respiratory protein dissolved in their hemolymph is hemocyanin, which binds oxygen with copper rather than iron, turning the fluid pale blue when oxygenated.

Hemocyanin molecules are far larger than hemoglobin and float free in the plasma instead of being packed into cells. Copper-bound oxygen changes how the fluid absorbs light, producing a blue tint only at sufficient concentration; low-oxygen or dilute hemolymph looks nearly colorless.

Fiction often paints spider blood as ink-blue, but most spider hemolymph is closer to colorless-to-pale blue, far weaker than horseshoe crab blood — the tint is only obvious pooled in a drop or under a microscope.

cards.q: 企鹅的羽毛是防水的吗？
cards.short: 尾脂腺分泌油脂防水
body: 企鹅每平方厘米体表约有15根羽毛，是现存鸟类中羽毛密度最高的类群之一，绒羽与外层正羽紧密交叠，几乎不留缝隙。
尾脂腺分泌的油脂经喙涂抹到羽毛表面，与羽枝、羽小钩构成的致密结构共同作用，令水珠无法渗透，同时锁住一层保温空气。
这层防水并非皮肤自带的永久性状，需每日梳理补充油脂来维持；一旦沾染污油或羽毛受损，防水层迅速失效，企鹅可能因浸湿失温甚至溺水。
cards.fig: 图版Ⅰ　帝企鹅羽毛特写照片。
cards.qe: Are penguin feathers waterproof?
cards.shorte: Preen oil makes them waterproof
cards.fige: Plate I. Close-up photograph of Emperor penguin plumage.
bodye: Penguins carry roughly 15 feathers per square centimeter of skin, among the densest plumage of any bird; the tightly overlapping down and contour feathers leave almost no gaps for water to enter.

Oil from the uropygial gland is spread over the feathers with the bill; combined with the fine interlocking barbs and hooklets, it keeps water from soaking through while trapping a layer of insulating air underneath.

This waterproofing isn't a permanent trait of the skin — it must be renewed daily through preening. If the oil is fouled or feathers are damaged, the barrier fails quickly, and a soaked penguin can lose heat or even drown.
cards.srce: Handbook of the Birds of the World, Vol. 1

cards.q: 树木何时长得最快？
cards.short: 新梢数周内长成全年量
body: 温带树木的年生长并不匀速：多数新梢的伸长集中在春末至初夏约六周内完成，此后速度骤降，入秋基本停止。
春季气温回升、光照变长，顶芽中生长素与赤霉素浓度骤增，推动细胞快速分裂伸长；盛夏后激素水平回落，生长随之放缓。
常被想象成整个生长季匀速增高变粗，实际树干直径的生长也同样挤在初夏前后完成，入冬树木进入休眠，全年增粗几乎为零。
cards.fig: 图版Ⅰ　橡树树干横切面年轮照片。
cards.qe: When do trees grow fastest?
cards.shorte: Most growth in a few weeks
cards.fige: Plate I. Photograph of an oak trunk cross-section showing growth rings.
bodye: Annual growth in temperate trees is far from steady: most shoot elongation happens within about six weeks in late spring and early summer, then slows sharply and nearly stops by autumn.

Rising spring temperatures and lengthening daylight trigger a surge of auxin and gibberellin in the buds, driving rapid cell division and elongation; once levels fall back in midsummer, growth slows accordingly.
Trees are often imagined to thicken steadily all season, but trunk diameter growth is similarly crowded into early summer — and stops almost entirely once winter dormancy sets in.
cards.query: Quercus trunk cross section growth rings photograph

cards.q: 琥珀里的昆虫DNA能保存吗？
cards.short: DNA远撑不到琥珀年龄
body: 对已灭绝物种骨骼DNA的测年研究显示，其半衰期约521年，即每隔521年DNA键就断裂一半，该数据来自恐鸟骨骼样本。
DNA双螺旋骨架会持续水解断裂，环境温度越高降解越快；即使在接近理想的低温环境，键断裂仍按指数速率累积，数千年后遗传信息已破碎成读不出的短片段。
科幻作品常设定琥珀能锁住恐龙时代昆虫的完整DNA，但按此衰变速率，别说上亿年，百万年后DNA也已降解殆尽，早年号称提取出的琥珀古DNA后来均未获重复验证。
cards.fig: 图版Ⅰ　古DNA降解速率曲线，半衰期约521年。
cards.srcMeta: Allentoft等，英国皇家学会学报B辑，2012年
cards.qe: Can insect DNA survive inside amber?
cards.shorte: DNA can't outlast amber's age
cards.fige: Plate I. Decay curve of ancient DNA, with a half-life of roughly 521 years.
bodye: Dating studies on extinct-species bone DNA put its half-life at about 521 years — every 521 years, roughly half of the remaining DNA bonds break. The estimate comes from radiocarbon-dated moa bone samples.

DNA's double-helix backbone keeps hydrolyzing, and higher temperatures speed the breakdown. Even in near-ideal cold storage, bond breakage still accumulates exponentially, leaving only unreadable fragments after a few thousand years.

Fiction imagines amber sealing intact dinosaur-era insect DNA, but at this decay rate even a few million years would erase it, let alone a hundred million — and the 1990s claims of extracted amber DNA were never independently confirmed.
cards.srce: The Half-Life of DNA in Bone
cards.srcMetae: Allentoft et al., Proc. R. Soc. B, 2012

plate.imgTitle: Baltic Amber necklace with insects inclusions.jpg

cards.q: 黑洞会把周围所有东西都吸进去吗？
cards.short: 黑洞引力与同质量天体相同
body: 黑洞的引力范围完全由质量决定,与同等质量的普通天体一样;只要停留在事件视界之外,物体感受到的只是正常引力,并不会被额外吸入。
事件视界是逃逸速度等于光速的临界面,只有越过它的物质才无法逃脱;视界之外的引力规律与同质量恒星或行星完全相同,只是空间更集中。
若太阳此刻被替换成同质量的黑洞,地球的公转轨道不会发生任何改变,仍按原周期运行;黑洞并不会像吸尘器一样把周围星体统统卷走。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　太阳质量黑洞的史瓦西半径换算示意
cards.qe: Do black holes suck in everything around them?
cards.shorte: Black hole gravity matches an equal-mass body
cards.fige: Plate I. The Schwarzschild radius of a Sun-mass black hole.
bodye: A black hole's gravitational reach is set entirely by its mass, just like any ordinary object of the same mass; stay outside the event horizon and you feel only normal gravity, not extra pull.

The event horizon is the boundary where escape velocity equals light speed — only matter that crosses it can never escape. Outside it, gravity works exactly as it would around an equal-mass star or planet, just packed into less space.

If the Sun were replaced by an equal-mass black hole this instant, Earth's orbit would not change at all and would keep its same period; black holes do not vacuum up surrounding stars like some cosmic vacuum cleaner.
cards.query: M87 black hole Event Horizon Telescope image

cards.q: 哪种树的根系可以长出新树干？
cards.short: 颤杨根系可萌发新树干
body: 美国犹他州的'潘多'颤杨林由单一根系连接,地上约有四万根遗传完全相同的树干,覆盖约43公顷,是已知最大的单一生物体之一。
颤杨主要依靠根蘖繁殖:根部横向延伸并在地表萌发新芽,长成看似独立的树干,实际上都是同一株植物经由地下根系相连供养的分身。
地面看是一整片森林,地下其实是同一株植物;单根树干寿命通常只有一百多年,老死后会被新萌发的树干替换,而整个根系与基因体存活时间远超单株。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　潘多颤杨林地下根系与地上树干分布示意
cards.src: 潘多颤杨无性系遗传研究
cards.srcMeta: DeWoody et al., Western North American Naturalist
cards.qe: Which tree's root system can sprout brand-new trunks?
cards.shorte: Aspen roots sprout new trunks
cards.fige: Plate I. Root system and surface stems of the Pando aspen clone.
bodye: Utah's 'Pando' aspen grove is connected by a single root system, sending up roughly 40,000 genetically identical trunks across about 43 hectares — one of the largest known single organisms.

Quaking aspen spreads mainly by root suckers: roots extend sideways and sprout new shoots at the surface, which grow into seemingly separate trunks that are actually all clones of one plant, fed through a shared underground root system.

Above ground it looks like a forest; below ground it's a single plant. Individual trunks typically live only around a century and are replaced by fresh sprouts when they die, while the root system and genome persist far longer.
cards.srcMetae: DeWoody et al., Western North American Naturalist
cards.query: Pando quaking aspen Populus tremuloides forest photograph

cards.q: 铜雕为何常呈绿色而非铜色？
cards.short: 铜表面氧化生成铜绿
body: 青铜或纯铜雕塑长期暴露在空气中后,表面会生成一层薄薄的铜绿,主要成分是碱式碳酸铜等化合物,厚度通常只有几十微米,却完全遮盖原本的金属光泽。
铜先与氧、水汽反应生成暗红棕色的氧化亚铜,再进一步转化为绿色的碱式碳酸铜等矿物;这层锈致密而稳定,能阻隔氧气,反而保护内部金属不再继续腐蚀。
铜绿并非损坏而是保护层,许多博物馆和修复师会刻意保留甚至人工做旧;自由女神像的铜皮正是靠这层绿锈,一百多年来几乎不再被继续腐蚀。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　自由女神像铜皮氧化前后色泽对照
cards.src: 美国国家公园管理局自由女神像资料
cards.qe: Why do bronze or copper statues turn green instead of staying copper-colored?
cards.shorte: Oxidized copper forms green patina
cards.fige: Plate I. The Statue of Liberty's copper skin before and after oxidation.
bodye: Bronze or pure-copper statues left exposed to air develop a thin patina, mainly basic copper carbonate compounds, often just tens of micrometers thick — yet it completely hides the metal's original shine.

Copper first reacts with oxygen and moisture into reddish-brown cuprous oxide, then further converts into green minerals like basic copper carbonate; this dense, stable layer blocks oxygen and actually protects the metal beneath from further corrosion.

Patina isn't damage but a protective coat; many museums and conservators deliberately preserve or even artificially age it. The Statue of Liberty's copper skin has barely corroded further in over a century, thanks to exactly this green layer.
cards.srce: National Park Service — Statue of Liberty facts
cards.query: Statue of Liberty copper patina close-up photograph

b.query: Statue of Liberty copper patina green photograph

cards.q: 版画为何需反向刻制图像？
cards.short: 刻板图案与成品左右相反
body: 雕版印刷时,刻好的版面须与纸张贴合按压,图案在转印过程中会整体左右翻转;因此版画家在雕刻阶段就要把图像预先镜像反转。
以木刻或铜版为例,油墨附着在版面凸起或凹陷处,纸张覆上按压后揭开,如同盖印章:版面是反的,印出来才是正的,文字方向的错误最容易被看穿。
这也是老版画上偶尔出现镜像文字或反向落款的原因;经验丰富的匠人会在起稿阶段就用镜像草图核对,而不是刻完才发现方向错了。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　木刻版画刻板(镜像)与印刷成品对照
cards.src: 大英博物馆托马斯·比维克木刻藏品
cards.qe: Why must printmakers carve images in mirror image?
cards.shorte: The block is a mirror of the print
cards.fige: Plate I. A carved woodblock (mirrored) beside its printed impression.
bodye: In relief or intaglio printing, the carved block presses directly onto paper; the design flips left-to-right in transfer, so it must be carved in reverse from the start.

Take woodcut or engraving: ink sits on the raised or incised surface, and pressing the paper on and lifting it off works like a stamp — a backward block prints correctly, which makes reversed lettering the easiest mistake to spot.
This is why some old prints show mirrored text or reversed signatures; experienced printmakers check against a mirror at the drawing stage rather than discovering the error only after carving.
cards.srce: British Museum — Thomas Bewick wood engravings
cards.query: Thomas Bewick wood engraving block photograph

cards.q: 为何面团揉搓后更有弹性？
cards.short: 揉面激活麸质蛋白网络
body: 小麦面粉中的麦谷蛋白与醇溶蛋白遇水后彼此连接,形成有弹性的面筋网络;揉搓通过反复拉伸折叠的机械力,让这层网络排列得更紧密均匀。
麦谷蛋白提供弹性和强度,醇溶蛋白提供延展性,两者靠氢键、二硫键等相互交联;揉面时间越长,面筋链排列越整齐,面团抗拉伸能力也越强。
并非揉得越久越好,过度揉搓会拉断已经形成的面筋链,让面团重新变软发黏;面粉蛋白含量不同,高筋粉适合长时间揉制,低筋粉则相反。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　揉面时间与面团弹性变化曲线
cards.src: 美国谷物化学家协会面团流变学方法
cards.qe: Why does dough get more elastic after kneading?
cards.shorte: Kneading builds a gluten network
cards.fige: Plate I. Dough elasticity across kneading time.
bodye: Wheat flour's glutenin and gliadin proteins link up once hydrated, forming a stretchy gluten network; kneading's repeated stretching and folding packs that network tighter and more evenly.

Glutenin supplies elasticity and strength, gliadin supplies stretchiness, and the two cross-link through bonds like hydrogen and disulfide bonds; the longer you knead, the more aligned the gluten strands become and the more the dough resists stretching.

More kneading isn't always better: overworking tears the gluten strands back apart, leaving dough soft and sticky again. Flours differ in protein content, so high-protein flour tolerates longer kneading than low-protein flour.

cards.q: 树木如何将水输送到百米高处?
cards.short: 蒸腾产生负压拉水上升
body: 红杉等高树可达100余米，树顶到根部水柱几乎连续不断。叶片蒸腾在导管顶端形成负压，最高可达约-2兆帕，把水向上拉升。
水分子间氢键使其相互牵拉如同细线（内聚力），又借毛细管壁的附着力不致中断，蒸腾-内聚力-张力机制共同支撑起百米水柱。
单靠毛细作用远不足以升水百米；树越高，导管内负压越大，越容易产生气穴断裂水柱，这也是红杉高度普遍止步于约115至130米的原因之一。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　红杉（Sequoia sempervirens）树冠，展示支撑百米水柱的树体结构。
cards.qe: How do trees move water up to a hundred meters?
cards.shorte: Transpiration pulls water up
cards.fige: Plate I. Crown of Sequoia sempervirens, the structure that sustains a hundred-meter water column.
bodye: Redwoods can exceed 100 meters, with a nearly continuous water column from crown to root. Transpiration from leaves creates negative pressure at the top of the xylem, reaching roughly -2 megapascals, pulling water upward.

Hydrogen bonds let water molecules cling together like a thread (cohesion), while adhesion to vessel walls keeps the column from breaking — transpiration, cohesion, and tension jointly sustain a hundred-meter water column.

Capillary action alone cannot lift water anywhere near that high. The taller the tree, the more negative the xylem pressure, raising the risk of cavitation — one reason redwood height tends to cap out around 115 to 130 meters.

plate.imgTitle: Sequoia sempervirens and Sequoiadendron giganteum OB Wrocław 2025 6.jpg

cards.q: 斐波那契数列与黄金比例有何关系？
cards.short: 比值收敛于黄金比例
body: 斐波那契数列每一项都是前两项之和（1，1，2，3，5，8，13……）。相邻两项之比会不断逼近黄金比例φ≈1.6180339887。
根据比奈公式，数列通项由φ的幂主导，次要项随n增大迅速衰减，因此比值F(n+1)/F(n)以指数速度收敛到φ，大约第10项后相对误差已小于万分之一。
黄金比例并非斐波那契数列独有——任意以两个正数起始、按「前两项之和」规则递推的数列，比值最终都会收敛到同一个φ，这是递推规则本身决定的，与初始值无关。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　斐波那契螺旋，由连续正方形按数列比例拼接而成。
cards.qe: How does the Fibonacci sequence relate to the golden ratio?
cards.shorte: Ratio converges to the golden ratio
cards.fige: Plate I. The Fibonacci spiral, built from squares scaled by the sequence's ratios.
bodye: Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two before it (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13...). The ratio of consecutive terms keeps approaching the golden ratio φ ≈ 1.6180339887.

By Binet's formula, the sequence is dominated by a power of φ while the secondary term decays quickly, so F(n+1)/F(n) converges to φ exponentially fast — the relative error is below 0.01% by around the tenth term.

The golden ratio isn't unique to the Fibonacci sequence — any sequence built by 'sum of the previous two,' starting from any two positive numbers, converges to the same φ. The limit comes from the recurrence rule itself, not the starting values.

plate.imgTitle: PSM V79 D459 Logarithmic spiral in flower growth configuration.png

cards.q: 罗马军团为何在敌前连夜修筑营地？
cards.short: 每夜筑营防敌突袭
body: 罗马军团即使只停留一夜，也会挖壕筑垒、扎设尖桩栅栏，建成一座标准化营寨（castra）。据波利比乌斯记载，这套流程在数千人协作下几小时内即可完成。
每座营寨内部布局几乎一致——统一的主干道、指挥帐位置，士兵不必侦查地形就能在黑暗或混乱中迅速找到岗位，栅栏和壕沟则用来阻滞夜间突袭。
修营并非因为士兵怯战，而是罗马军纪律体系的一部分：标准化的营地让部队无论行军到何处，都能保持同等的防御强度与指挥效率，这被视为其常胜的关键因素之一。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　罗马军团标准化营寨（castra）复原场景，展示壕沟与栅栏防御结构。
cards.srcMeta: 波利比乌斯，约公元前2世纪
cards.qe: Why did Roman legions build a fortified camp before facing the enemy each night?
cards.shorte: Camp built nightly against raids
cards.fige: Plate I. Reconstruction of a standardized Roman marching camp (castra), showing its ditch-and-palisade defenses.
bodye: Even for a single night's halt, Roman legions dug a ditch and rampart and set sharpened stakes, building a standardized marching camp (castra). Polybius records that thousands of soldiers working together could finish it within hours.

Every camp followed almost the same layout — the same main roads, the same position for the command tent — so soldiers could find their post in the dark or in chaos without scouting the terrain; the rampart and ditch slowed night attacks.

Building a camp wasn't a sign of timidity — it was part of Roman military discipline. A standardized camp let the army keep the same defensive strength and command efficiency wherever it marched, considered one key to its lasting success.

cards.q: 古罗马公共厕所为何无隔间？
cards.short: 如厕不设私密隔断
body: 古罗马公共厕所（forica）常设连续石凳，凿出一排排锁孔状坐孔，彼此相邻甚至相对而坐，中间不设隔板。
坐孔下方是持续流动的渠水冲走排泄物，凳前另有一条浅水槽，供公用的海绵棒（tersorium）蘸水清洁，连续无间断的结构更便于渠水通畅流动。
缺少隔断常被现代人解读为「罗马人不讲隐私」，但更可能是水利结构决定的布局——连续渠道优先于个人遮蔽，如厕交谈在当时也确实是一种社交场景。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　奥斯蒂亚安提卡（Ostia Antica）遗址的古罗马公共厕所，连排坐孔无隔断。
cards.qe: Why did ancient Roman public restrooms have no partitions?
cards.shorte: Latrines had no privacy screens
cards.fige: Plate I. The public latrine at Ostia Antica, its row of seats built without partitions.
bodye: Roman public latrines (forica) typically had a continuous stone bench with a row of keyhole-shaped holes, seated side by side or even facing each other, with no partitions between them.

Beneath the seats ran continuously flowing water that carried waste away, and a shallow channel in front held water for the shared sponge-on-a-stick (tersorium) — an unbroken layout suited the flow of water.

The lack of partitions is often read as 'Romans didn't care about privacy,' but it more likely followed from the plumbing — a continuous channel took priority over individual screening — and chatting while seated was indeed a genuine social occasion.
cards.srce: The Archaeology of Sanitation in Roman Italy

plate.imgTitle: Ancient Roman Public Latrine, Ostia Antica (6075060094).jpg

cards.q: 威尼斯为何将玻璃工匠迁至孤岛？
cards.short: 玻璃炉迁岛防火非防泄密
body: 1291年，威尼斯共和国下令将城内玻璃熔炉全部迁往外海的穆拉诺岛（Murano），此后数百年间，威尼斯玻璃业几乎完全集中于此岛。
威尼斯当时房屋密集且多为木结构，玻璃熔炉需持续高温运作，一旦失控极易引发大火，把炉火集中隔离到一座独立小岛，是最直接的城市防灾手段。
常见说法是迁岛为了「锁住配方防泄密」，但迁移法令本身出于防火；对工匠流动与技术外泄的严格管制，是几十年后才逐渐加码形成的制度，并非最初动机。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　穆拉诺岛（Murano）玻璃熔炉，威尼斯共和国自1291年起将炉火集中于此。
cards.srcMeta: 威尼斯穆拉诺玻璃博物馆
cards.qe: Why did Venice move its glassmakers to an isolated island?
cards.shorte: Furnaces moved for fire safety, not secrecy
cards.fige: Plate I. A glass furnace on Murano, where the Venetian Republic concentrated its furnaces from 1291 onward.
bodye: In 1291, the Republic of Venice ordered all glass furnaces moved out to the island of Murano. For centuries afterward, Venetian glassmaking was concentrated almost entirely there.

Venice's buildings were densely packed and mostly wooden, and glass furnaces ran at sustained high heat — a single mishap could spark a major fire. Isolating the furnaces on a separate island was the most direct way to protect the city.

The move is often explained as 'locking away the formula,' but the original decree was about fire safety. The strict controls on glassmakers leaving and trade secrets only hardened into policy decades later — not the initial motive.

cards.q: 中世纪欧洲城墙为何建在城市外围？
cards.short: 城墙圈地为日后扩张
body: 中世纪欧洲城墙常修建在远超当时建成区的范围之外，如佛罗伦萨1284年动工的第三道城墙圈入大片农田，数百年后城区才填满这圈墙。
城墙建造耗资巨大且难以扩建，统治者一次性圈入预期的未来发展用地，同时纳入水源、菜园与牧场，以便长期围城时城内可自给。
城墙的实际防御作用常被高估，许多城市最终以谈判、贿赂或背叛破城，而非攻城战；城墙更多起到征税关卡与身份边界的作用。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　1471-1482年佛罗伦萨全景版画，可见环城城墙。
cards.srcMeta: A. E. J. Morris／Longman 1994年第三版
cards.qe: Why were medieval European walls built on a city's outskirts?
cards.shorte: Walls enclosed future growth
cards.fige: Plate I　A 1471-1482 panoramic engraving of Florence showing its encircling walls.
bodye: Medieval European walls were often built well beyond the area actually settled at the time; Florence's third wall circuit, begun in 1284, enclosed vast farmland that took centuries to fill in.
Walls were expensive and hard to extend, so rulers enclosed land for anticipated future growth in one pass, along with water sources, gardens, and pasture so the city could sustain a long siege.

Walls' defensive value is often overstated—most cities eventually fell to negotiation, bribery, or betrayal rather than direct assault; walls functioned as much as toll checkpoints and identity boundaries.
cards.srce: History of Urban Form: Before the Industrial Revolutions
cards.srcMetae: A. E. J. Morris / Longman, 3rd ed., 1994
