cards.q: 彗星尾巴指向哪里？
cards.short: 彗尾恒指背离太阳
body: 彗星尾巴并不指向彗星运动的反方向，而是始终背离太阳延伸，由太阳风与辐射压将彗核蒸发出的气体与尘埃向外推开而形成。
彗尾分为两种：离子尾受太阳风（带电粒子流）推动，笔直背向太阳；尘埃尾受光压影响较弱，沿彗星轨道略微弯曲拖曳，两者方向都由太阳决定而非运动方向。
当彗星远离太阳飞向深空时，尾巴反而拖在彗核前方而非后方，与人们直觉中彗尾如飞机尾迹般拖在身后的想象正好相反。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　海尔-波普彗星照片，可见蓝色离子尾与白色尘埃尾分离伸展。
cards.qe: Which way does a comet's tail point?
cards.shorte: Tail always faces from the Sun
cards.fige: Plate I　Comet Hale-Bopp with separate blue ion tail and white dust tail.
bodye: A comet's tail does not point opposite its direction of travel; it always extends away from the Sun, pushed outward by solar wind and radiation pressure acting on gas and dust released from the nucleus.

There are two tail types: the straight ion tail, driven directly away from the Sun by the solar wind's charged particles, and the curved dust tail, shaped more gently by radiation pressure along the comet's orbit—both governed by the Sun's position, not the comet's motion.

When a comet is heading away from the Sun into deep space, its tail actually leads in front of the nucleus rather than trailing behind—the reverse of how a tail, like a jet's contrail, is commonly imagined.

cards.q: 米开朗基罗在雕刻大卫像时用了多少块大理石？
cards.short: 整尊仅用一块大理石
body: 米开朗基罗的《大卫》像高5.17米，整尊雕像仅出自一块卡拉拉大理石，这块石料此前已被两位雕塑家先后放弃闲置了约25年。
这块被称为'巨人'的大理石因先前雕刻师在下部开凿过深、留下瑕疵而被弃用；米开朗基罗接手后巧妙地将大卫设计为扭转的站姿，以回避石料内部的裂纹与旧凿痕。
多数人以为如此巨大的雕像需拼接多块石料，但文艺复兴雕塑家以'整块石中已藏有形象，雕刻只是去除多余部分'为信条，大卫像正是这一理念的极致体现。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　佛罗伦萨学院美术馆藏米开朗基罗《大卫》像。
cards.qe: How many blocks of marble did Michelangelo use for David?
cards.shorte: Carved from one marble block
cards.fige: Plate I　Michelangelo's David at the Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence.
bodye: Michelangelo's David stands 5.17 meters tall, carved entirely from a single block of Carrara marble that two earlier sculptors had abandoned and left untouched for about 25 years.

Known as 'the Giant,' the block had been rough-cut too deep and left flawed by earlier attempts; Michelangelo designed David's twisting contrapposto stance partly to work around the block's internal cracks and old chisel marks.

Many assume a statue this large required multiple blocks pieced together, but Renaissance sculptors held that the figure already existed within the stone, with carving simply removing the excess—David is that idea's fullest expression.

cards.q: 英文招牌上的 Ye 为什么读作 The？
cards.short: 铅字缺字母，Y代古拼写
body: 古英语和中古英语曾用字母þ（thorn）表示th的发音，这个字母沿用超过千年，直到印刷术普及后才逐渐消失。
活字印刷从欧洲大陆传入英国时没有þ的字模，排字工便用形状相近的y临时替代，the因此常被印成ye。
很多人把招牌上的Ye读成yee，以为它代表旧时尊称you，它的发音与含义从始至终都只是the。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　中古英语手稿残页，可见字母þ与后来将其取代的y字形相近。
cards.qe: Why was the 'Ye' on old shop signs read as 'The'?
cards.shorte: Printers swapped þ for a plain y
cards.fige: Plate I　A Middle English manuscript leaf, showing the letter þ and the similarly shaped y that replaced it.
bodye: Old and Middle English used the letter þ (thorn) for the 'th' sound, and it stayed in use for over a thousand years — until movable-type printing spread.
Type imported to England from continental Europe had no þ, so printers substituted the similarly shaped y, and 'the' was often set as 'ye'.
Many people read the 'Ye' on old signs as 'yee', thinking it meant an old form of 'you' — but its sound and meaning were always simply 'the'.
cards.srce: The Cambridge Encyclopedia of the English Language

plate.imgTitle: The missing letter is N - geograph.org.uk - 5384294.jpg

cards.q: 复活节岛的朗格朗格文字为何至今无法破译？
cards.short: 存世不足30件文本
body: 朗格朗格文字刻在复活节岛的木板上，现存不到30件真品，分散收藏在多国博物馆，年代约在18至19世纪。
破译文字通常需要双语对照或大量重复语料，朗格朗格文字样本太少，也没有类似罗塞塔石碑那样的对照版本。
曾有学者宣称解读出部分符号，但都缺乏同行认可的完整方案，多数语言学家仍认为它没有被真正破译。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　朗格朗格木板拓片局部，可见密集刻划的鸟形与几何符号。
cards.qe: Why has Rongorongo, the script of Easter Island, never been deciphered?
cards.shorte: Fewer than 30 texts survive
cards.fige: Plate I　A detail of a Rongorongo tablet rubbing, showing densely carved bird-like and geometric glyphs.
bodye: Rongorongo glyphs are carved into wooden boards from Easter Island. Fewer than 30 authentic pieces survive today, scattered across museums, dating to roughly the 18th–19th century.
Decipherment usually needs a bilingual key or a large body of repeating text. Rongorongo has too little of either, and nothing like a Rosetta Stone to check readings against.
Some scholars have claimed to read individual glyphs, but no complete reading has won peer consensus — most linguists still consider the script undeciphered.

plate.imgTitle: A Rongorongo board in black and white glyphs. Oc,G.T.1733, Mana Expedition to Easter Islan

cards.q: 一战导火索刺杀案，凶手为何巧合出现在现场？
cards.short: 车队开错路遇刺客
body: 1914年6月28日，刺客第一次行刺失败后，斐迪南大公的车队本该改道前往医院，司机却仍按原计划驶入街道。
发现走错路后，司机试图停车倒车，车正好停在普林西普面前，他原本已放弃行动，却因此获得近距离开枪的机会。
这场看似周密的刺杀，关键转折是一次导航失误，而非缜密的埋伏计划，多部权威史著都记录了这一细节。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　萨拉热窝拉丁桥旧照，大公车队当年在附近停车调头。
cards.src: 《梦游者：1914年欧洲如何走向一战》
cards.qe: The assassination that sparked WWI — how did the gunman happen to be right there?
cards.shorte: A wrong turn put him in range
cards.fige: Plate I　A period photograph of the Latin Bridge in Sarajevo, near where the Archduke's car stopped to reverse.
bodye: On 28 June 1914, after an earlier assassination attempt failed, Archduke Franz Ferdinand's motorcade was meant to detour to the hospital — but the driver kept to the original route.
Told he'd gone the wrong way, the driver stopped to reverse, halting right in front of Gavrilo Princip, who had already given up and just happened to be standing there.
The plot's decisive turn was a navigation mistake, not a careful ambush — a detail recorded in multiple authoritative histories of the war's outbreak.
cards.srce: The Sleepwalkers: How Europe Went to War in 1914

cards.q: 哪个国家的国旗曾长期无人知晓？
cards.short: 锁国百年，国旗鲜为人知
body: 不丹国旗上的雷龙图案约在1949年确定，但不丹长期奉行锁国政策，直到1971年加入联合国才首次正式对外展示。
不丹几乎不与外国建交，也限制外国游客入境，电视和互联网直到1999年才解禁，国旗因此很少出现在国际场合。
多数国家一旦制定国旗便很快为世人所知，不丹说明：缺乏对外交流，再正式的国家象征也可能多年不为人知。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　不丹国旗实物照，黄橙对角分割，白色雷龙居中。
cards.qe: Which country's flag went largely unrecognized by the world for decades?
cards.shorte: Isolation kept its flag unseen
cards.fige: Plate I　A photograph of Bhutan's national flag, split diagonally in yellow and orange with a white dragon at its center.
bodye: The dragon on Bhutan's flag was fixed around 1949, but the country's long isolation meant it wasn't formally shown to the world until Bhutan joined the UN in 1971.
Bhutan kept almost no foreign relations and restricted tourist entry; television and the internet weren't allowed until 1999, so the flag rarely appeared internationally.
Most flags become known as soon as they're adopted. Bhutan shows that without outside contact, even an official national symbol can stay unrecognized for decades.

cards.q: 肥皂泡破裂前为什么会先变黑？
cards.short: 薄膜过薄，光发生干涉
body: 肥皂泡快要破裂时，水分因重力和蒸发不断流失，泡壁最薄处能降到只有几十纳米，远小于可见光的波长。
当薄膜厚度远小于光的波长，膜内外表面反射的光波会相互抵消，可见光各波段几乎都被抵消，那片区域看起来就是黑色。
这层「黑膜」不是因为脏污或变色，恰恰相反，它比周围五彩斑斓的部分更薄更纯净，是破裂前的最后阶段。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　肥皂泡表面局部特写，可见薄膜将破前呈现的暗黑斑块。
cards.qe: Why do soap bubbles turn black right before they pop?
cards.shorte: A too-thin film cancels all light
cards.fige: Plate I　A close-up of a soap bubble's surface, showing the dark patch that appears just before it bursts.
bodye: As a soap bubble nears bursting, gravity and evaporation drain its water away. The thinnest spots can drop to just a few tens of nanometers — far below the wavelength of visible light.
Once the film is far thinner than the light's wavelength, light reflecting off its inner and outer surfaces cancels itself out across nearly the whole visible spectrum, so that patch looks black.
This 'black film' isn't dirt or discoloration — quite the opposite. It's thinner and purer than the colorful patches around it, marking the last stage before the bubble bursts.
cards.srce: Soap Bubbles and the Forces Which Mould Them
cards.query: Soap bubble thin film macro photograph

cards.q: 世界上使用人数最多的语言是？
cards.short: 计入第二语言，英语第一
body: 计入第二语言使用者，英语约15亿人为世界第一，汉语普通话约11亿人次之，西班牙语、印地语随后。
英语反超源于其作为国际通用语的地位——科研、航空、互联网长期以英语为默认交流语言，第二语言学习者远超母语者。
若只算母语使用者，汉语普通话反而以约9.4亿人稳居第一，英语母语者不到4亿，两种统计口径结论正相反。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　新英格兰识字课本内页，反映英语的教育传播史。
cards.qe: Which language has the most speakers in the world?
cards.shorte: Including L2 users, English leads
cards.fige: Plate Ⅰ　An interior page of the New England Primer, tracing the spread of English through education.
bodye: Counting second-language users, English has about 1.5 billion speakers worldwide, more than Mandarin Chinese's roughly 1.1 billion.
English overtakes Mandarin mainly through its role as the default language of science, aviation, and the internet, where L2 learners vastly outnumber native speakers.
Counted by native speakers alone, Mandarin Chinese leads with about 940 million, while native English speakers number under 400 million — the two rankings invert.
cards.query: New England Primer title page engraving

cards.q: 汉语拼音声调符号为何标在元音上？
cards.short: 元音是声调的物理载体
body: 汉语声调靠元音的音高升降体现，辅音无法承载音高变化，拼音规则规定声调符号必须标在音节主要元音上。
多元音相连时，标调遵循固定优先级：a和e/o优先，其余按开口度排序，iu/ui并列时标在后一个元音上。
许多人以为标调位置随意或按书写习惯，实际上它是1958年公布的《汉语拼音方案》明文规定的固定规则，并非约定俗成。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　汉语拼音方案主要设计者周有光像。
cards.qe: Why are Mandarin Pinyin tone marks placed on vowels?
cards.shorte: Vowels are tone's physical carrier
cards.fige: Plate Ⅰ　Portrait of Zhou Youguang, principal designer of the Pinyin scheme.
bodye: Mandarin tone is expressed through pitch changes carried by vowels, not consonants, so Pinyin rules require tone marks to sit on a syllable's main vowel.
When multiple vowels appear together, placement follows a fixed priority: a or e/o take precedence; for the iu/ui pair, the mark falls on the second vowel.
Many assume the placement is just convention, but it was explicitly codified in the 1958 Scheme for the Chinese Phonetic Alphabet — a fixed rule, not folk habit.
cards.srce: Scheme for the Chinese Phonetic Alphabet

cards.q: 庞贝遇难者的样子是怎么留下的？
cards.short: 灰烬空腔浇入石膏成像
body: 公元79年维苏威火山喷发，庞贝居民被火山灰掩埋后遗体腐烂消失，只在硬化火山灰层中留下人形空腔。
1863年考古学家菲奥雷利将石膏浆灌入空腔，凝固后取出，还原出遇难者倒下瞬间的体态与衣纹细节。
许多人以为这些石膏像是遗体本身，实际骨骼仍嵌在石膏内部，石膏只是空腔的翻模，人体早已分解无存。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　庞贝火山灰石膏铸像，重现遇难者倒下瞬间的姿态。
cards.qe: How were the shapes of Pompeii's victims preserved?
cards.shorte: Ash cavities cast in plaster
cards.fige: Plate Ⅰ　Plaster cast of a Pompeii victim, capturing the final posture at the moment of death.
bodye: When Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE, Pompeii's residents were buried in ash; their bodies decayed away, leaving human-shaped voids in the hardened ash layer.
In 1863, archaeologist Giuseppe Fiorelli poured plaster into these voids; once hardened, the casts revealed the victims' final postures and even clothing folds.
Many assume these 'plaster figures' are the bodies themselves, but the actual skeletons remain embedded inside — the plaster is only a cast of the void the body left behind.

cards.q: 因纽特语真有几十个表示雪的词吗？
cards.short: 因纽特语雪相关词汇被夸大
body: 一九一一年人类学家博厄斯提到因纽特语有四个雪相关词根，后来传播中被夸大为几十甚至上百个。实际统计显示现代因纽特语各方言中独立的雪相关词根约为十至十五个。
因纽特语属于多式综合语，通过在词根上添加后缀构成复杂词汇。一个词根可派生出数十种形式，但这是语法机制而非独立词汇。英语同样可以用snowfall、snowflake、snowdrift等派生词描述不同雪态。
这一误传源于对词与词根的混淆，以及对黏着语特性的误解。语言学家普尔姆在一九八九年撰文批判这种文化刻板印象，指出类似夸张在描述其他语言时同样存在。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　因纽特语词汇结构示意
cards.qe: Does Inuit language really have dozens of words for snow?
cards.shorte: Inuit snow vocabulary has been exaggerated
bodye: In 1911, anthropologist Boas mentioned four snow-related word roots in Inuit, later exaggerated through retelling to dozens or even hundreds. Actual counts show modern Inuit dialects have about ten to fifteen independent snow-related roots.

Inuit is a polysynthetic language that builds complex words by adding suffixes to roots. One root can generate dozens of forms, but this reflects grammatical mechanism rather than separate vocabulary. English similarly uses derivations like snowfall, snowflake, and snowdrift to describe different snow states.

This misconception stems from confusing words with roots and misunderstanding agglutinative language features. Linguist Pullum's 1989 critique challenged this cultural stereotype, noting similar exaggerations occur when describing other languages.
cards.query: Inuit language morphology diagram linguistic structure

cards.q: 丙烯颜料比油画颜料快干多少？
cards.short: 丙烯颜料干燥速度快数百倍
body: 丙烯颜料通常在十至三十分钟内表干，厚涂也不超过数小时。而传统油画颜料表干需要数天，完全固化往往要数月甚至数年，两者干燥速度相差数百倍。
丙烯颜料以水为介质，通过水分蒸发和聚合物交联快速成膜。油画颜料则依赖亚麻籽油等干性油氧化聚合，这一化学过程极为缓慢，深层颜料可能数十年仍未彻底硬化。
快干特性使丙烯适合分层罩染和户外写生，但无法像油画那样长时间混色和修改。许多当代艺术家混用两种材料，在速写阶段用丙烯打底，精修时转用油彩。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　丙烯颜料管与调色刀
cards.qe: How much faster does acrylic paint dry than oil paint?
cards.shorte: Acrylic paint dries hundreds of times faster
bodye: Acrylic paint typically becomes touch-dry within ten to thirty minutes, with thick applications drying in a few hours. Traditional oil paint takes days to surface-dry and months or even years to cure fully, making acrylics hundreds of times faster.

Acrylic uses water as a medium, forming a film through water evaporation and polymer crosslinking. Oil paint relies on oxidative polymerization of drying oils like linseed oil, a slow chemical process that may leave deep paint layers uncured for decades.

Fast drying makes acrylic ideal for layered glazing and plein air painting, but eliminates the extended blending and reworking time oil allows. Many contemporary artists combine both media, using acrylic for underpainting and oil for refinement.

cards.q: 蛋彩画为何要在石膏底上作画？
cards.short: 石膏底吸收蛋彩中多余水分
body: 蛋彩画使用蛋黄或蛋清作为颜料粘合剂，含水量较高。传统工艺要求在木板上涂抹多层石膏底料，厚度可达数毫米，形成吸水性强且光滑的白色表面。
石膏底料由动物胶与石膏粉混合制成，其多孔结构能迅速吸收蛋彩中的水分，使颜料快速附着而不流淌。同时白色底料可增强颜色的亮度和透明感，这是蛋彩画特有的发光效果来源。
文艺复兴大师常在石膏底上先绘制精细的素描稿，再层层罩染透明色。这种技法在油画普及后逐渐式微，但二十世纪部分画家重新采用以获得独特的哑光质感。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　蛋彩画石膏底制作过程
cards.qe: Why must tempera paint be applied on gesso ground?
cards.shorte: Gesso ground absorbs excess water from tempera
bodye: Tempera paint uses egg yolk or egg white as a binder, resulting in high water content. Traditional practice requires applying multiple layers of gesso to wooden panels, building up millimeters of absorbent, smooth white surface.

Gesso consists of animal glue mixed with chalk or gypsum powder. Its porous structure rapidly absorbs water from tempera, allowing pigments to adhere quickly without running. The white ground also enhances color luminosity and transparency, creating tempera's characteristic luminous quality.

Renaissance masters often drew detailed underdrawings on gesso before applying transparent color glazes. Though this technique declined after oil painting became dominant, twentieth-century artists revived it to achieve distinctive matte finishes.
cards.query: gesso preparation wooden panel tempera painting process

cards.q: 铜雕为何要先做泥塑原型？
cards.short: 泥塑用于翻制浇铸模具
body: 传统失蜡法铸铜需先用黏土塑造与成品等大的原型，表面细节须完全完成。这一泥塑将用于制作外模，黏土干燥收缩率约百分之八，雕塑家需提前计算补偿。
泥塑表面涂石膏浆形成外模，待凝固后拆除内部黏土，换填蜡层和耐火芯料。加热时蜡熔化流出形成空腔，熔融青铜注入后冷却成型。一次浇铸后石膏模即损毁，无法重复使用。
现代雕塑家常用硅橡胶制作可重复使用的软模，但大型纪念碑雕塑仍采用传统泥塑翻制法。米开朗基罗的部分未完成泥塑原型至今保存在佛罗伦萨。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　雕塑工作室中的泥塑原型与工具
cards.qe: Why do bronze sculptures require clay prototypes first?
cards.shorte: Clay models are needed for casting molds
bodye: Traditional lost-wax bronze casting requires a full-size clay prototype with all surface details completed. This clay model forms the basis for the outer mold, and sculptors must compensate for clay's eight percent drying shrinkage.

Plaster slurry coats the clay surface to create the outer mold. After hardening, the clay interior is removed and replaced with wax layers and refractory core material. Heating melts the wax, leaving a cavity for molten bronze. The plaster mold breaks during casting and cannot be reused.

Modern sculptors often use silicone rubber for reusable flexible molds, but large monumental works still employ traditional clay prototype methods. Some of Michelangelo's unfinished clay models survive in Florence today.
cards.query: sculptor clay model studio tools photograph

cards.q: 水彩画为何不用白色颜料提亮？
cards.short: 传统水彩靠纸面留白提亮
body: 传统水彩技法依赖纸张本身的白色作为最亮部，画家通过控制颜料透明度和留白区域来表现高光。白色颜料会破坏水彩的透明感，使画面变得浑浊不清。
水彩颜料由极细颜料粉末与阿拉伯树胶混合，加水稀释后形成透明色层。光线穿过色层在白纸表面反射，产生独特的明亮感。添加白色颜料会引入不透明粒子，阻断这一光学效应。
现代部分画家使用不透明水彩或混入白色广告颜料以便修改，但这种做法在十九世纪前被视为违背水彩本质。英国皇家水彩画协会至今保留不使用白颜料的传统规则。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　水彩画中的留白技法示例
cards.srcMeta: 泰晤士与哈德逊出版社/2019
cards.qe: Why don't watercolor painters use white paint for highlights?
cards.shorte: Traditional watercolor preserves paper whites for highlights
bodye: Traditional watercolor relies on the paper's inherent whiteness for the brightest values, with artists controlling pigment transparency and reserved areas to depict highlights. White paint destroys watercolor's transparency, making the image muddy.

Watercolor pigments combine finely ground powder with gum arabic. When diluted with water, they form transparent color layers. Light passes through these layers and reflects off the white paper surface, creating characteristic luminosity. White pigment introduces opaque particles that block this optical effect.

Some modern painters use opaque watercolor or mix in white gouache for corrections, but this practice was considered contrary to watercolor's essence before the nineteenth century. Britain's Royal Watercolour Society maintains traditional rules against white pigment use.
cards.query: watercolor painting technique reserved whites demonstration

cards.q: 我们为什么永远只能看到月球的同一面？
cards.short: 月球自转公转同步，永远以同一面朝向地球
body: 月球绕地球公转一圈约27.3天，自转一圈也恰好是27.3天。两个周期精确相等，导致月球始终以同一半球面向地球——这一现象称为潮汐锁定，是引力长期作用的结果。
月球早期自转远快于今天。地球引力在月球上掀起固体潮汐隆起，隆起与转动之间的错位不断消耗自转能量，像一只无形的手按住转盘，经过数亿年将月球自转逐渐刹停在与公转同步的状态。
"月球背面"并非"月球暗面"——背面同样有昼夜交替，只是从地球上永远看不见。人类直到1959年苏联月球三号探测器传回照片，才第一次看到那半边布满环形山的陌生月面。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　月球潮汐锁定三维标本 · 可拖动环绕
cards.qe: Why do we always see the same face of the Moon?
cards.shorte: The Moon rotates in step with its orbit, always facing Earth
bodye: The Moon orbits Earth once every 27.3 days and rotates on its axis in exactly the same period. Because the two cycles match, one hemisphere permanently faces Earth - a state called tidal locking, the end result of long gravitational braking.

The young Moon spun much faster. Earth's gravity raised solid tidal bulges on it, and the constant misalignment between bulge and spin drained rotational energy like a hand pressed on a turntable, slowing the Moon over hundreds of millions of years until its day matched its orbit.

The far side is not a dark side - it gets days and nights like the near side; we simply never see it. Humanity first glimpsed that crater-packed hemisphere only in 1959, when the Soviet probe Luna 3 radioed back its photographs.

cards.q: 埃菲尔铁塔冬天和夏天一样高吗？
cards.short: 热胀冷缩让铁塔夏季比冬季高出约十五厘米
body: 埃菲尔铁塔由约7300吨熟铁构成。金属受热膨胀、遇冷收缩，巴黎冬夏温差可达三四十度，塔身高度随之变化——盛夏比寒冬高出最多约十五厘米。
这一伸缩完全在设计预料之中。铁塔的铆接结构允许构件之间微量位移，膨胀既不损伤结构，也无需任何人工干预，每年循环往复。
不止长高：阳光只晒得到塔的一侧时，受热面膨胀更多，塔顶会朝背阴方向微微偏斜。一天之中，三百米高的塔尖会随太阳的移动在空中缓缓画出一个十几厘米的小圈。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　埃菲尔铁塔三维标本 · 可拖动环绕
cards.src: 埃菲尔铁塔官方技术档案
cards.qe: Is the Eiffel Tower the same height in winter and summer?
cards.shorte: Thermal expansion makes the tower about fifteen centimetres taller in summer
bodye: The Eiffel Tower is built from roughly 7,300 tonnes of wrought iron. Metal expands when heated and contracts when cooled, and with Paris temperatures swinging by dozens of degrees across the year, the tower stands up to about fifteen centimetres taller at the height of summer than in deep winter.
The breathing was fully anticipated in the design. The riveted structure lets members shift minutely against each other, so the seasonal cycle neither damages the tower nor requires any intervention.

It does more than grow: when sunlight strikes only one side, that face expands more and the summit leans gently away from the sun. Over a single day the 300-metre tip slowly traces a small circle in the sky, following the sun's path.

cards.q: 一张纸可以只有一个面吗？
cards.short: 莫比乌斯环只有一个面和一条边
body: 取一根纸条，把一端扭转半圈后与另一端粘合，得到的环带就只有一个面、一条边。用笔沿表面一直画下去，不必翻越边缘，笔迹会走遍"正反两面"回到起点——这就是莫比乌斯环。
它由德国数学家莫比乌斯与利斯廷在1858年各自独立发现，是拓扑学最著名的入门标本：一个用一次扭转就打破"面必有正反"直觉的曲面。
沿中线把它剪开，得到的不是两个环，而是一个扭了两整圈的更大单环。这一性质曾被用于实际工程：单面传送带让磨损均匀分布在"两面"，环形录音带则凭一次扭转获得双倍播放时长。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　莫比乌斯环三维标本 · 可拖动环绕
cards.qe: Can a sheet of paper have only one side?
cards.shorte: A Möbius strip has just one side and one edge
bodye: Take a strip of paper, give one end a half twist, and glue it to the other. The resulting band has exactly one side and one edge: run a pen along the surface without ever crossing an edge and the line covers what looks like "both sides" before returning to its start. This is the Möbius strip.

Discovered independently by German mathematicians Möbius and Listing in 1858, it is topology's most famous specimen - a surface that overturns the intuition that every sheet must have a front and a back with a single twist.

Cut it along the centre line and you get not two rings but one larger loop with two full twists. The property has served real engineering: single-sided conveyor belts spread wear across "both faces", and loop recording tapes doubled their playing time with one twist.

cards.q: 核电站的大"烟囱"在冒烟吗？
cards.short: 双曲线冷却塔喷出的白雾是纯净水汽，不是烟
body: 电影里核电站的标志性巨塔常被当作烟囱，但那是冷却塔，顶上翻涌的白色不是烟，而是纯净的水蒸气——温热的水滴遇冷空气凝成的雾，与家中烧水壶口的白汽同源。
冷却塔的职责是给完成做功的蒸汽降温：热水在塔内被打散成水帘，与上升气流换热后循环使用。这套冷却水路与反应堆回路相互隔离，喷出的水汽并不接触放射性物质。
塔身的双曲线轮廓也不是为了造型：这种曲面用最少的混凝土提供最高的结构强度，还能像天然烟道一样加速空气自下而上流动，无需风机就完成大部分通风。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　双曲线冷却塔三维标本 · 可拖动环绕
cards.src: 世界核协会技术资料库
cards.qe: Is that giant nuclear plant "chimney" smoking?
cards.shorte: The white plume from a cooling tower is clean water vapour, not smoke
bodye: The giant towers that stand for nuclear power in films are routinely mistaken for chimneys, but they are cooling towers - and the white billows above them are not smoke but clean water vapour, warm droplets condensing in cool air, the same mist that rises from a kettle.

A cooling tower's job is to chill steam that has finished its work: hot water is shattered into a falling curtain inside the tower, gives up its heat to the rising air, and is recirculated. This cooling loop is isolated from the reactor circuit, so the plume never touches radioactive material.

Nor is the hyperbolic silhouette a stylistic whim: the curved shell delivers maximum structural strength from minimum concrete, and it accelerates airflow upward like a natural flue, doing most of the ventilation without a single fan.

cards.q: 把土星放进水里，它会浮起来吗？
cards.short: 土星平均密度小于水，是唯一能"浮起来"的行星
body: 土星的平均密度约为每立方厘米0.687克，比水还轻三成——它是太阳系唯一密度低于水的行星。若真有一个足够大的浴缸，土星理论上会浮在水面上。
这份轻盈来自成分：土星主体是氢和氦，最轻的两种元素包裹着相对小的岩石内核。庞大的体积摊薄了质量，造就了低于水的平均密度。
当然，这只是一个思想实验：需要直径超过十二万公里的水体，而作为气态巨行星，土星没有可以"放进去"的固体表面——真被放进水里，它会先散成一场无边的氢氦风暴。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　土星与光环三维标本 · 可拖动环绕
cards.qe: Would Saturn float if you dropped it in water?
cards.shorte: Saturn's average density is lower than water - the only planet that would float
bodye: Saturn's average density is about 0.687 grams per cubic centimetre - a third lighter than water, and the only planet in the solar system below water's density. Given a large enough bathtub, Saturn would, in theory, float.

The lightness comes from its recipe: Saturn is mostly hydrogen and helium, the two lightest elements, wrapped around a comparatively small rocky core. Its enormous volume spreads the mass thin, dragging the average density below water's.

It remains a thought experiment: the tub would need to span more than 120,000 kilometres, and as a gas giant Saturn has no solid surface to lower into the bath - dropped in, it would first come apart into a boundless storm of hydrogen and helium.

cards.q: 比萨斜塔为什么斜了八百多年还不倒？
cards.short: 只要重心垂线不出塔基，斜塔就倒不了
body: 比萨斜塔1173年动工，建到第三层时就因软黏土地基不均匀沉降而开始倾斜。此后八百多年它始终斜而不倒，物理学上的底线只有一条：塔身重心的铅垂线仍落在基座范围之内。
讽刺的是，拯救它的正是灾难本身——建造因战争两度中断近一个世纪，停工让地基有时间固结硬化。若当年一鼓作气盖完，塔大概率早已倾覆。后来的建造者还刻意把上层砌得偏向反方向，塔身因此微微弯成一根香蕉。
1990年斜塔一度逼近失稳临界，工程队封塔十一年，从高侧地基下缓缓抽走七十吨土，让塔体自然回正约四十四厘米——相当于回到十九世纪初的倾角。监测显示它此后仍在极缓慢地自行回正，未来数百年内无恙。

cards.qe: Why has the Leaning Tower of Pisa leaned for 800 years without falling?
cards.ae: Its centre of gravity stays over the base
cards.shorte: As long as the plumb line of its weight lands inside the foundation, the tower stands
bodye: Construction began in 1173, and by the third storey the tower was already tilting on its unevenly settling bed of soft clay. Through more than eight centuries the physics has come down to one line: the vertical through the tower's centre of gravity still lands inside the footprint of its base.

Ironically, disaster saved it - wars halted construction twice for nearly a century, and the pauses gave the clay time to consolidate. Built in one go, the tower would likely have toppled. Later builders also leaned the upper storeys against the tilt, bending the tower into a faint banana.

By 1990 it had crept toward instability. Engineers closed it for eleven years and slowly extracted seventy tonnes of soil from beneath the high side, letting the tower settle back about forty-four centimetres - roughly its early-1800s tilt. Monitoring shows it is still straightening imperceptibly, safe for centuries to come.
cards.srce: International Committee for the Safeguard of the Tower of Pisa

cards.q: 地球的一天从来都是24小时吗？
cards.short: 恐龙时代一天约23小时，地球自转正被月球缓缓刹车
body: 地球的一天并非从来都是24小时。恐龙称霸的白垩纪晚期，一天约23个半小时；再往前到四亿年前的泥盆纪，一天只有约22小时，一年因此塞下了四百多天。
证据封存在化石里：珊瑚的骨骼像树木年轮一样逐日生长，泥盆纪珊瑚化石上的日纹显示每年约四百层——天文学家由此反推出当时更快的自转。
刹车来自月球：潮汐摩擦持续消耗地球自转能量，平均每个世纪让一天变长约1.8毫秒。为了让原子钟与变慢的地球对齐，人类自1972年以来已28次在深夜悄悄拨入一秒——闰秒正是地球减速的收据。

cards.qe: Has a day on Earth always been 24 hours?
cards.shorte: Days were about 23 hours in the dinosaur era - the Moon is slowly braking Earth
bodye: An Earth day has not always been 24 hours. In the late Cretaceous, under the dinosaurs, a day ran about 23 and a half hours; back in the Devonian, four hundred million years ago, it lasted roughly 22 hours - packing more than 400 days into a year.

The evidence is sealed in fossils: coral skeletons grow daily layers the way trees grow rings, and Devonian corals show about four hundred growth lines per year - from which astronomers read off the faster spin of the ancient Earth.

The brake is the Moon: tidal friction steadily drains Earth's rotational energy, lengthening the day by about 1.8 milliseconds per century. To keep atomic clocks aligned with the slowing planet, humanity has quietly slipped in a leap second 28 times since 1972 - each one a receipt for Earth's deceleration.
cards.srce: International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service Bulletin

cards.q: 大金字塔原本是什么颜色？
cards.short: 吉萨金字塔曾包着打磨光亮的白色石灰岩外壳
body: 今天看到的金字塔是内部阶梯状的黄褐色砌块，但落成时的吉萨大金字塔包裹着一层打磨到近乎镜面的白色图拉石灰岩外壳，在沙漠烈日下亮得刺眼，数十公里外可见。
古埃及人称大金字塔为"Ikhet"，意为"辉光"。有学者推测其压顶石可能镀有金或金银合金，让塔尖在日出日落时率先亮起。
外壳的消失主要归咎于中世纪：1303年大地震震松了包面石，此后数百年开罗的建设者把它们成批剥走，化作清真寺与城墙的石料。如今只有卡夫拉金字塔的塔尖，还留着一小片原装外壳供人想象当年的白色。

cards.qe: What colour was the Great Pyramid originally?
cards.shorte: Giza's pyramids were cased in polished white limestone
bodye: The pyramids we see today are the tan, stepped core blocks - but the Great Pyramid of Giza was finished in a casing of white Tura limestone polished nearly to mirror, blindingly bright under the desert sun and visible from dozens of kilometres away.

The ancient Egyptians called the Great Pyramid "Ikhet" - "the shining one". Some scholars suggest its capstone was sheathed in gold or electrum, lighting the summit first at sunrise and last at sunset.

The casing was lost mainly to the Middle Ages: the great earthquake of 1303 loosened the facing stones, and over the following centuries Cairo's builders stripped them wholesale into mosques and city walls. Today only the tip of Khafre's pyramid keeps a patch of original casing, a swatch of the vanished white.
cards.srce: The British Museum, Ancient Egypt Collection Archive
